to make one lifetime feel insulting
when there’s still so much to touch.

I don’t fear the tale ending
because nothing mattered here.
I fear it because I loved the world
and wanted many more years.

[Verse 2]
There will be technologies I miss,
friends I never get to know,
future cities, future music,
places I won’t get to go.

[Bridge]
Maybe that ache is evidence
I never stopped being amazed.
Maybe sorrow at the finish
means I truly loved the race.

[Final Chorus]
So when the lights begin to dim,
I won’t ask for eternity.
Just one more morning,
one more idea,
one more impossible thing to see.

And if I still want more,
then maybe I lived correctly.

title: Ghosts of Choices
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Somewhere I was more ordinary,
same street, same bed, same town.
Somewhere I learned how roots feel
instead of always moving around.

Somewhere I chose one direction,
one love, one version of my name.
Somewhere I stopped reinventing
every time the future changed.

[Chorus]
I miss the lives I never lived,
though they were never really mine.
Ghosts of choices haunt the corners
of a life that turned out fine.

That is the cruel geometry:
one body, one stretch of time.
You can love the road you traveled
and still grieve the roads declined.

[Verse 2]
I chose curiosity often,
chose motion, risk, and reach.
But sometimes I wonder what stability
might have had to teach.

[Bridge]
There is no perfect timeline.
Every paradise has cost.
Every life becomes a cemetery
for possibilities we lost.

[Final Chorus]
So I’ll raise a glass to all of them,
the selves I’ll never meet.
They didn’t die for nothing.
They made this version of me.

title: Books I'll Never Write
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There are books I’ll never write,
songs I’ll never hear complete,
systems I can almost picture,
worlds that die inside of me.

Every year the list gets longer
while the calendar gets thin.
Creation taught me endless futures.
Time decides which ones get in.

[Chorus]
I could live a hundred lifetimes
and still leave work undone.
There will always be a project
waiting after I am gone.

That used to make me restless.
Now it almost makes me smile.
Maybe meaning isn’t finishing.
Maybe meaning is the while.

[Verse 2]
I wanted to build everything,
teach everything I knew,
leave enough strange little signals
for someone else to follow through.

[Bridge]
So if the last page cuts me off
mid-sentence, mid-design,
I hope somebody finds the fragments
and builds something beyond mine.

[Final Chorus]
There are books I’ll never write,
but that doesn’t make them waste.
Some dreams exist to pull us forward,
not to ever be replaced.

title: When the Departures Stop
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Another gate, another window,
another country from the sky.
I spent my life between arrivals,
always learning how to say goodbye.

There are hearts in different time zones,
names I carry everywhere,
so much love across the planet,
and still rooms where I was never there.

[Chorus]
When the departures finally stop,
what will I wish I’d stayed to see?
Which mornings should have had me home?
Who needed more of me?

I chased the whole horizon,
and God, I loved the view,
but every world I managed to enter
meant another slipped straight through.

[Verse 2]
I built friendships out of weekends,
memories from borrowed days,
but some things need a thousand mornings
to become a permanent place.

[Bridge]
I don’t regret the motion.
I just wonder what it cost.
A life can be incredibly full
and still contain enormous loss.

[Final Chorus]
When there are no more boarding calls,
I hope I can finally say:
I saw a lot,
I loved a lot,
even what I couldn’t stay.

title: Every Yes Murders Two
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I crossed enough borders
to forget where distance ends,
collected cities, stages,
books, and strangers turned to friends.

I made a life from motion,
from ideas nobody saw,
kept reaching for the future
like it owed me something more.

[Chorus]
Still I mourn the roads I missed,
the lives I never tried,
the quiet house, the different love,
the years on some other side.

I know I’ve lived more than enough
to call this journey full,
but abundance has a shadow:
every yes still murders two.

[Verse 2]
There were songs I never finished,
places I will never know,
versions of myself that vanished
every time I chose to go.

[Bridge]
Maybe peace is not pretending
I would choose the same again.
Maybe gratitude and grieving
can both live inside the end.

[Final Chorus]
So when the final page is turning,
I won’t say I did it all.
I’ll just say I kept on reaching
every time I heard life call.

title: How I Tried
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep a list beside the sink
Of little things I meant to do
A call returned, a door held open
A borrowed coat brought back to you

[Pre-Chorus]
Some nights I count the good I gave
Some nights the names I let down
Which one will carry past my hands
When I am quiet, when I am gone?

[Chorus]
If love is what I leave behind
Let it be more than what I broke
A place to rest, a little help
A promise kept, a truth I spoke
But every tender thing I tried
Sits next to every time I failed
Tell me which story takes my name
When all the telling has gone still

[Verse 2]
I remember your unanswered call
The kitchen clock, the blue mug cracked
I said I’d come, I didn’t come
And you stopped asking after that

[Pre-Chorus]
I’ve tried to make a useful life
To leave the room a little kind
But every good thing has a seam
Where all my worst days show inside

[Chorus]
If love is what I leave behind
Let it be more than what I broke
A place to rest, a little help
A promise kept, a truth I spoke
But every tender thing I tried
Sits next to every time I failed
Tell me which story takes my name
When all the telling has gone still

[Bridge]
Maybe no single story wins
Maybe both are true at once
The hands that held, the hands that hurt
The words I gave, the ones I swallowed

[Final Chorus]
If love is what I leave behind
Let it be something people use
A meal, a ride, a patient ear
A second chance I didn’t lose
And when my last day comes around
I hope the whole of me is seen
Not only where I fell short
But how I tried to make amends

[Outro]
How I tried
How I tried

title: Edge of the Frame
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I watch the room through a pane of glass
Every small bargain, every practiced laugh
From out here, I can trace the seams
See the quiet rules beneath the scene

[Chorus]
I see what you miss from the edge of the frame
I can name the hinge, I can change the game
But you look through me when I step inside
I know the way through; I don't know where I belong

[Verse 2]
You call it distance, I call it a view
A map of the cracks running straight through you
I bring back what the center can't see
Then the door swings shut between you and me

[Chorus]
I see what you miss from the edge of the frame
I can name the hinge, I can change the game
But you look through me when I step inside
I know the way through; I don't know where I belong

[Bridge]
Outside, the pattern makes sense
Inside, I disappear again
If I move the line, will you move with me?
Or keep the glass where it used to be?

[Outro]
I can see it
I can say it
Can you see me now?

title: Leave a Window in Your Mind
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You keep the beetle in a jar
For one short ride, then let it go
You ask the drain where rivers are
And watch the little paper boats

[Pre-Chorus]
They say, be useful, guard your hands
They price the parts they understand
But you still turn a stone to see
What made a home beneath the sea

[Chorus]
Keep that small question alive
Keep your bright astonishment
They can take the coat you wore
They can't name what you invent
Keep that small question alive
Leave a window in your mind

[Verse 2]
You draw a map on grocery bags
To places no one needs to find
A moth lands softly on your sleeve
You give it all the time it needs

[Pre-Chorus]
The world keeps asking for your proof
And shaving wonder down to use
But there’s a door behind your eyes
That opens when you ask it why

[Chorus]
Keep that small question alive
Keep your bright astonishment
They can take the coat you wore
They can't name what you invent
Keep that small question alive
Leave a window in your mind

[Bridge]
When they say, “That’s all there is,”
Look closer at the cracked blue dish
A tiny world is turning there
With dust for moons and room to spare

[Final Chorus]
Keep that small question alive
Keep your bright astonishment
They can take the coat you wore
They can't name what you invent
Keep that small question alive
Leave a window in your mind

[Outro]
Ask again
Look again
Let the beetle go

title: Where the Map Runs Thin (v2)
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You call it odd; I call it Tuesday
A paper crown on a crooked chair
I take the side road past the hardware store
With one bright question rattling there

[Chorus]
I’m fine out here on the strange edge
Turning where the map runs thin
You’ll find me when the road bends over
I’ll be somewhere new again

[Verse 2]
The old ideas fit like borrowed jackets
Sleeves too short, the seams pulled wide
I leave them folded by the doorway
And follow what I haven’t tried

[Chorus]
I’m fine out here on the strange edge
Turning where the map runs thin
You’ll find me when the road bends over
I’ll be somewhere new again

[Bridge]
No grand reveal, no final answer
Just a door I haven’t opened yet
I like the little click of knowing
There’s more ahead than I can guess

[Outro]
Keep your place; I’ll send a postcard
From the next uncharted bend
Glad to meet what’s waiting for me
Glad the road won’t have an end

title: Where the Map Runs Thin (v1)
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You call it odd; I call it Tuesday
A paper crown on a crooked chair
I take the side road past the hardware store
With one bright question rattling there

[Chorus]
I’m fine out here on the strange edge
Turning where the map runs thin
You’ll find me when the road bends over
I’ll be somewhere new again

[Verse 2]

title: Edge of the Map
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
They call it strange
I call it Tuesday
A bent little road
I take the long way

[Chorus]
I’m fine out here
At the edge of the map
You’ll find me later
When your compass catches up

[Verse 2]
I’ve got no grand plan
Just a pocket of questions
A door left ajar
And a taste for the next thing

[Chorus]
I’m fine out here
At the edge of the map
You’ll find me later
When your compass catches up

[Bridge]
Let them name the shape
After I’ve moved on
I’m already looking
Where the path comes undone

[Outro]
Happy to find out
What comes next

title: Someone I Can Live With
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You ask me to be steady
When the room begins to tilt
I learn the shape of every need
And wear it like a quilt
I keep your coffee warm
I say the careful thing
Then find my own two hands
Have forgotten what they’re holding

[Chorus]
I can’t be everybody’s answer
And still hear my own name
I keep giving out the pieces
Till there’s nothing left to claim
You can love me when I’m honest
You can wait while I come through
I am trying to be someone
I can live with, too

[Verse 2]
I say yes before the question
I smooth the crease before it shows
I know which version makes you easy
Which one keeps the peace at home
But alone beside the sink
With the dishes stacked like stairs
I ask the quiet in my chest
If anybody’s listening there

[Chorus]
I can’t be everybody’s answer
And still hear my own name
I keep giving out the pieces
Till there’s nothing left to claim
You can love me when I’m honest
You can wait while I come through
I am trying to be someone
I can live with, too

[Bridge]
Let the phone ring twice
Let the small hurt stay
Let me take one breath
Before I give myself away

[Final Chorus]
I can’t be everybody’s answer
But I’m learning what I need
I can leave a little silence
Where my own thoughts get to breathe
You can love me when I’m honest
I can still come back to you
I am trying to be someone
I can live with, too

[Outro]
Someone I can live with
Someone I can live with, too

title: A Life I Never-Lived Life
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep a list beside the bed
Of names I mean to overtake
A salary, a better face
A heart that never learns to wait

[Pre-Chorus]
I call the sprint a staircase
I call the hunger drive
Each rung says, just a little more
Each morning eats the why

[Chorus]
I want the house, the hand, the crown
I want the proof they’ll keep me around
I build a life I never live in
I reach for more, and don’t begin

[Verse 2]
The inbox fills like winter rain
My mother asks when I’ll come by
I say next month, then next quarter
And buy a watch to mark the lie

[Pre-Chorus]
I turn a date into a target
A kiss into a test
I chase the version they applaud
And leave the rest unaddressed

[Chorus]
I want the house, the hand, the crown
I want the proof they’ll keep me around
I build a life I never live in
I reach for more, and don’t begin

[Bridge]
If I put both feet on the ground
Would I still count as someone?
If nobody saw me win
Could I stay for what I’ve become?

[Final Chorus]
I want the house, the hand, the crown
But hear the quiet asking now
A seed won’t grow beneath a deadline
A heart needs somewhere safe to lie

[Outro]
I cross one thing off the page:
Be here. Stay. Begin.

title: Gilded Mirror
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I built a palace out of empty air
A dozen kingdoms where I'm standing bare
Chasing the horizon just to prove my worth
The heaviest titan on this hollow earth

[Chorus]
Always climbing, never landing
Running from the peace I'm demanding
A gilded mirror and a phantom crown
Burning every bridge just to watch it burn down

[Verse 2]
Every lover traded for a closing deal
Confusing hollow numbers for something real
The faster that I sprint, the further I recede
A parasite of passion and an endless need

[Chorus]
Always climbing, never landing
Running from the peace I'm demanding
A gilded mirror and a phantom crown
Burning every bridge just to watch it burn down

[Bridge]
Roots need dirt and time to grow
I only know the undertow
Just a shadow in a tailored suit
Chasing every leaf, forgetting the root

[Outro]
Never settling
Just a ghost of success
Never settling
Just an empty address
[Instrumental fade out]

title: Leave the Lamp On
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep a chair pulled close to the door
For anyone carrying too much
I know the names of the late-night shops
And which neighbor needs a ride
I hand out warmth like spare change
Then wonder where my pockets went

[Chorus]
I want to give my love to everyone
And keep a little quiet for myself
Let me sit with the thought until it settles
Let me hear my own heart without a crowd
I can care for you and still go home
I can leave the lamp on, close the door

[Verse 2]
Your message waits beside the sink
The kettle clicks, the room turns still
I read your words and feel them land
Then take an hour to answer true
Not every pause means I have gone
Some thoughts need room to find their shape

[Chorus]
I want to give my love to everyone
And keep a little quiet for myself
Let me sit with the thought until it settles
Let me hear my own heart without a crowd
I can care for you and still go home
I can leave the lamp on, close the door

[Bridge]
No locked gate, no grand goodbye
Just a page, a cup, a softer pace
When I return, I bring more of me
And there is more of me to give

[Final Chorus]
I want to give my love to everyone
And keep a little quiet for myself
Let me sit with the thought until it settles
Let me hear my own heart without a crowd
I can care for you and still go home
I can leave the lamp on, close the door

[Outro]
The door is closed, the love is not

title: Room for the Bruise
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep a place behind my eyes
Where nobody gets sized up at the door
You tell the truth and still get supper
You break a cup, we sweep the floor

[Chorus]
Let there be room to change our minds
Room for the bruise, room for the mending
A softer answer, a little more time
A world that bends without breaking

[Verse 2]
The old man at the corner store
Misnames the street, we walk him home
The kid who came in wearing armor
Leaves with his hands unclenched and open

[Chorus]
Let there be room to change our minds
Room for the bruise, room for the mending
A softer answer, a little more time
A world that bends without breaking

[Bridge]
If I have kept a score of wrongs
I’ll tear the paper, start again
You can come back with all your pieces
We’ll set a chair beside the rain

[Final Chorus]
Let there be room to change our minds
Room for the bruise, room for the mending
A softer answer, a little more time
A world that bends without breaking

[Outro]
A place to start again
A place to start again

title: Monday Taking Its Time
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Monday lays its cool hand on the kitchen tile
The kettle takes its time, so do I
A sock slips down the hall beneath the door
Nothing urgent waiting on the other side

[Chorus]
I care around nothing this morning
Let the small hours carry their own weight
Your cup is turned upside down beside mine
We can leave the day outside the gate

[Verse 2]
The bread goes brown at the very edge
A pale square of sun moves over the chair
You ask if I’m worried; I say, not today
There’s room in this quiet for both of us here

[Chorus]
I care around nothing this morning
Let the small hours carry their own weight
Your cup is turned upside down beside mine
We can leave the day outside the gate

[Outro]
No grand plan, no reason to run
Just your sleeve brushing mine
And Monday taking its time

title: I Wish Those Roads Crossed
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I learned that good people stay
When every instinct says to run.
They carry weight without complaining,
Put themselves behind everyone.

So I became dependable,
The one who always understands,
While every dream I postponed
Slowly slipped between my hands.

[Pre-Chorus]
If kindness costs me everything,
At what point is it just fear?
If everybody needs me,
Am I allowed to disappear?

[Chorus]
I want to be happy,
I want to be good.
I wish those roads crossed
As often as they should.

Because choosing myself
Feels like leaving someone behind,
And doing the right thing
Keeps stealing pieces of my life.

Tell me, can a good heart
Sometimes say, “I’ve had enough”?
Can I choose what makes me happy
Without betraying everyone I love?

[Verse 2]
I know duty has a beauty.
I know promises should mean things.
But a promise made from guilt
Can quietly become a chain.

[Bridge]
Maybe goodness isn't suffering.
Maybe love isn't self-erasure.
Maybe giving from an empty heart
Doesn't make the giving greater.

[Final Chorus]
I want to be happy.
I still want to be good.
Maybe I can choose myself
More often than I thought I could.

If loving everyone requires
That I hate the life I live,
Maybe being good means learning
I deserve some joy to give.

title: Lose Myself
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There's a road I want to follow
That will disappoint a few.
Every mile looks like freedom,
Every mile feels cruel to you.

I could stay where I'm expected,
Keep the picture clean and whole,
But every day I play that person
Something disappears inside my soul.

[Chorus]
Is it selfish if I'm happy?
Is it noble if I break?
How much misery is righteous?
How much joy am I allowed to take?

I don't want to hurt you.
I don't want to lose myself.
Why does doing what I need
Feel like choosing me above everyone else?

[Verse 2]
You can sacrifice so beautifully
That nobody sees you drown.
They'll call you strong and loyal
While your whole world closes down.

And selfishness can wear disguises.
Freedom isn't always kind.
Sometimes chasing your own happiness
Leaves somebody else's heart behind.

[Bridge]
So I can't hide behind slogans:
“Follow dreams” or “do what's right.”
Every choice creates a shadow.
Every yes extinguishes some light.

I just want enough courage
To accept whatever choosing costs,
Without pretending that my happiness
Means nobody else gets lost.

[Final Chorus]
Maybe selfish isn't evil.
Maybe sacrifice isn't good.
Maybe character is choosing
With the clearest heart you could.

I will try to cause less sorrow.
I will own the wounds I make.
But I can't spend my only lifetime
Living choices I can't take.

title: A Life That Feels Good
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
They told me live a good life.
I thought they meant behave.
Keep your promises, be generous,
Give more than what you take.

Then someone said, “Be happy.
You've only got one turn.”
And suddenly those two commandments
Started fighting to be heard.

[Pre-Chorus]
One says pleasure isn't purpose.
One says suffering is waste.
Both sound true at different hours.
Both keep changing shape.

[Chorus]
What is the good life?
Is it joy or sacrifice?
Is it waking up excited
Or sleeping well at night?

Is it doing what you want,
Or wanting what is right?
I've spent years trying to answer
Why those things still have to fight.

[Verse 2]
I can chase every desire
And become somebody cold.
I can bury every desire
And resent everyone I hold.

So maybe neither road is virtue.
Maybe neither makes me free.
Maybe goodness without happiness
Creates another kind of greed.

[Bridge]
I want pleasure without blindness,
Duty without chains.
Love without possession,
Growth without disdain.

I want to leave people better,
But still experience my days.
I don't want a moral victory
Over a life I threw away.

[Final Chorus]
Maybe that's the good life:
Not perfection, not control.
Knowing joy deserves a place
Beside responsibility in the soul.

I will fail at the balance.
I will sometimes choose wrong.
But I want to be both happy
And someone I'm proud to become.

Not a saint.
Not a hedonist.
Just a person trying to find
A life that's good to others
And still feels good to live inside.

title: Where Kindness Ends
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You ask me to smile while the verdict is forming
A warm little room with a locked iron door
I learned how to please by rehearsing the morning
Then hated the person who asked me for more

[Pre-Chorus]
If I tell the whole truth, will you call it a wound?
If I keep you from hurting, what happens to me?

[Chorus]
I want to be happy without turning cruel
I want to be good without living by rules
If mercy means breaking the shape that I’m in
Tell me where kindness ends and I begin

[Verse 2]
Your coat on the chair, your untouched cup cooling
The apology waits like a stone in my hand
I could make you feel safe by pretending I’m certain
Or leave you the truth and let silence withstand

[Pre-Chorus]
You deserve an answer; I deserve a life
Both can be true when the room cuts like a knife

[Chorus]
I want to be happy without turning cruel
I want to be good without living by rules
If mercy means breaking the shape that I’m in
Tell me where kindness ends and I begin

[Bridge]
No halo, no sentence, no clean way through
Just one honest choice I can make with you
I won’t call my fear a virtue again
I won’t call your hurt the price of my peace

[Final Chorus]
I want to be happy and still choose what’s true
I want to be good without vanishing for you
If mercy means making a boundary clear
Let it be gentle, let it be here

[Outro]
Let it be gentle
Let it be here

title: Keep My Heart
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You said the kind thing costs too much
I watched you count the change
The shelter closed at half past six
You drove through anyway
A stranger slept beneath your coat
You missed the morning train
You came home late, your hands still cold
And called it someone else’s pain

[Pre-Chorus]
If I feel good when I do right
Does that make the choice untrue?
If every open hand comes back
With something warm for me, too?

[Chorus]
Tell me, can I keep my heart
And still be good to you?
Does kindness lose its honest name
When it carries me through?
I want the joy, I want the truth
I want them both to stay
If doing good makes me feel alive
Must I turn that life away?

[Verse 2]
You gave your place beside the fire
Then smiled to warm your hands
You never asked the freezing man
To bless your noble plans
The morning came, the room was bare
No witness, no applause
Just one less night somebody spent
Believing no one saw

[Pre-Chorus]
Maybe virtue isn’t proved
By how little we receive
Maybe wanting joy is not a wound
We have to hide or grieve

[Chorus]
Tell me, can I keep my heart
And still be good to you?
Does kindness lose its honest name
When it carries me through?
I want the joy, I want the truth
I want them both to stay
If doing good makes me feel alive
Must I turn that life away?

[Bridge]
No clean hands, no perfect reason
No bright line through the years
Just a choice made in the moment
With a pulse beneath the fear
If I help because I love you
And because I need to care
Maybe goodness isn’t empty
Maybe joy belongs in there

[Final Chorus]
Yes, I can keep my heart
And still be good to you
The joy does not erase the cost
The cost does not erase the truth
I want the joy, I want the truth
Let both of them remain
If doing good makes me feel alive
I’ll choose it all again

[Outro]
I’ll choose it all again
With open hands, and no disguise

title: Let Joy and Mercy Share the
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You keep a list beside the sink
Of every decent thing you do
You cross one off, then stop to think
Was that for them, or for you?

[Pre-Chorus]
You give away the coat you need
Then count the hours till you’re warm
A careful heart can plant a seed

[Chorus]

Tell me what the good is for

Why am I still keeping score?
I want to help without disappearing
I want to laugh and still be kind

[Verse 2]
You call your hunger selfishness
You call your rest a borrowed wage
But even hands that tend the mess

[Pre-Chorus]
The neighbor’s porch light clicks at ten
Her paper bag splits in the rain
You lift the cans, she laughs, and then
You both walk home a little changed

[Chorus]
If being good means being empty
Tell me what the good is for
If happiness makes me less worthy
Why am I still keeping score?
I want to help without disappearing
I want to laugh and still be kind
Let both hands hold what they are carrying
Let joy and mercy share the time

[Bridge]
No halo for the sleepless
No prize for needless pain
A life can bend toward others
And still belong to you again

[Final Chorus]
If being good means being empty
Let that old measure hit the floor
I can be glad and still be steady
I don’t have to starve for more
I want to help without disappearing
I want to laugh and still be kind
Let both hands hold what they are carrying
Let joy and mercy share the time

[Outro]
You set the list beside the sink
And leave one line undone
You take a breath, you let yourself
Be someone loved, not just someone useful

title: The Ledger Tells
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You keep the clean white shirt for Sunday
I keep the list of things I owe
You say a kind word at the doorway
Then count the favors as we go
I want the room to like my laughter
I want to leave with my hands clean
But every time I choose the easy
Somebody else pays what I mean

[Pre-Chorus]
If goodness asks me to go hungry
Who gets to call that living well?
If happiness is built on someone

[Chorus]

[Verse 2]

[Bridge]

Maybe it’s staying in the room

Making space for someone new
No halo, no clean absolution
Just a promise I can keep:
I’ll ask who pays for my good fortune

[Final Chorus]
I want a life that feels like mine
And hands that never hide the cost
Can I be glad and still be good
And face the ones my choices crossed?
I won’t call hunger holy
I won’t call comfort innocence

[Outro]

title: Happy or Good
lyrics:
[Intro]
(Glitchy arcade beeps)
(Dramatic piano chord)
To be happy... or to be good?
Which one would you choose?

[Verse 1]
I built a castle out of perfect lies
Polished the edges, covered up the cries
The rules of the righteous are a heavy chain
They promise a heaven but they cultivate pain
I did what was right, wore a hollow smile
Walking the straight road, mile after mile
But the garden is dead where the duty grows
Under the weight of the moral prose

[Chorus]
Am I happy? Am I good?
Did I do the things I should?
If I break the mold to save my mind
Is it a sin to leave the saints behind?
(Glitchy synth drop)
Oh, the bitter taste of a righteous heart
Tearing my own sweet life apart!

[Verse 2]
A little bit of poison makes the colors bright
A little bit of selfishness to feel the light
They call it a shadow, they call it a fall
But being an angel got me nothing at all
I'm stepping off the pedestal, smashing the glass
Letting the judgments of the holy pass
If goodness is a cage where the spirit dies
I'd rather be a demon with open eyes

[Chorus]
Am I happy? Am I good?
Did I do the things I should?
If I break the mold to save my mind
Is it a sin to leave the saints behind?
(Glitchy synth drop)
Oh, the bitter taste of a righteous heart
Tearing my own sweet life apart!

[Outro]
(Solo violin swells, sidechain pumping)
Just let me breathe...
Even if it's bad.
(Register beep, quiet console hiss)
I'm finally happy.
Are you finally mad?
(Power down sound effect)

title: A Coat by the Door
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left your coat beside the door
And counted coins across the floor
The landlord called; you let it ring
Then bought the coat you said you'd bring

[Pre-Chorus]
A little mercy, paid in cash
A clean excuse, a brighter mask
If doing right means going cold
How much of you can goodness hold?

[Chorus]
I want to be good, I want to be glad
I want to give without losing what I have
If I save my heart, does someone else fall?
If I answer every call, am I nothing at all?

[Verse 2]
You saw the kid outside the store
With wet cuffs and a paper score
You gave him lunch, you missed your train
And cursed the rain, then felt ashamed

[Pre-Chorus]
A little kindness, bruised and real
A private hunger you conceal
The rule says give until it's gone
Your tired hands keep holding on

[Chorus]
I want to be good, I want to be glad
I want to give without losing what I have
If I save my heart, does someone else fall?
If I answer every call, am I nothing at all?

[Bridge]
Maybe the point isn't spotless skin
Maybe the good lets the human in
You can keep a place at your own table
And still make room when you are able

[Final Chorus]
I want to be good, I want to be glad
I want to give without hating what I have
I won't save the world by breaking in two
I'll keep some light for me, and carry some through

[Outro]
A coat by the door
A chair pulled near
Not perfect, not pure
But present, here

title: Hold the In-Between
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep two portraits in the kitchen glass,
one holds the door, one counts what it can take.
You ask me how my day went; I say, “Fine,”
while every borrowed hour bends and shakes.

[Pre-Chorus]
The list is pinned beneath a chipped blue magnet,
your name beside the things I meant to do.
I want the life that waits beyond the calendar,
but every road I dream still runs to you.

[Chorus]
I’m trying to be kind without disappearing,
trying to want more without wanting less of you.
One hand holds the people I would never leave,
one reaches for the life I haven’t lived through.
If happiness is somewhere in this tangle,
let it make room for all the love I mean.
I’m not one face, not one clean answer—
I’m learning how to hold the in-between.

[Verse 2]
The sink is full, the hallway needs its fixing,
your coat is draped across the chair again.
I laugh too loud; the guilty one says, “Selfish,”
the saint says, “Stay,” and neither says when.

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the weight of every promise spoken,
I know the pull of mornings not yet mine.
I can be grateful, tired, fierce, and frightened;
those truths can share the same small room tonight.

[Chorus]
I’m trying to be kind without disappearing,
trying to want more without wanting less of you.
One hand holds the people I would never leave,
one reaches for the life I haven’t lived through.
If happiness is somewhere in this tangle,
let it make room for all the love I mean.
I’m not one face, not one clean answer—
I’m learning how to hold the in-between.

[Bridge]
To everyone I love: I’m still here.
To the self I keep postponing: stay near.
I can change the shape of what I promised,
without turning all this tenderness to fear.

[Final Chorus]
I’m trying to be kind without disappearing,
trying to want more and keep you close too.
One hand holds the people I would never leave,
one opens up a little room for something new.
If happiness is somewhere in this tangle,
we’ll make a place where every heart can breathe.
I’m not one face, not one clean answer—
I’m learning how to live as all of me.

[Outro]
All of me, still here.
All of us, still dear.

title: Not One Clean Answer
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I sort the good suit from the hungry one
Both keep my face, both know my name
One says, “Stay, they need you where you are”
One counts the doors and calls it shame

Your small hand finds my sleeve, and I stay

[Pre-Chorus]
I love you more than leaving could explain
I want a room where I can hear my own heart

[Chorus]

I want you safe beside me all the same
If happiness is something we can practice

I’ll carry both truths through the weather

[Verse 2]
The sink is full, the evening slips its leash
A lunchbox waits beside the unpaid bill

Then hear the other life go quiet still
I’m not ashamed that I want something more

[Pre-Chorus]
I love you more than leaving could explain
I want a room where I can hear my own heart

[Chorus]
I am not one clean answer
I am the hand that holds and pulls away
I want the life I keep postponing
I want you safe beside me all the same
If happiness is something we can practice
Let me learn it without throwing love aside
I’ll carry both truths through the weather
With the selfish and the kind still side by side

[Bridge]
Maybe I can want without abandoning
Maybe care can leave a little air
Maybe I can name the thing I’m missing
And still be here, still meet you there
[Group Chant]
Stay and change
Stay and change

[Final Chorus]
I am not one clean answer
I am the hand that holds and pulls away
I want the life I’m finally reaching for
I want you safe beside me all the same
If happiness is something we can practice
Let me build it where our lives collide
I’ll carry both truths through the weather
With the selfish and the kind still side by side

[Outro]
Still beside you
Still becoming

title: Save Yourself While Saving You
lyrics:
[Intro]
(Distorted guitar swell, shifting odd-meter heartbeat)
[Group Chant]
Hold the line, break the thread!
Hold the line, break the thread!

[Verse 1]
Two faces stare back from the mirror's crack

I love the hands that hold me to this floor

[Chorus]
Oh, the chaos in the middle of the mind
Trying to find the joy I left behind!

[Group Chant]
Hold the line...
[Outro Solo]

title: Every Heart I Am
lyrics:
[Verse 1]

One brings the soup, one counts what I am owed
