Step out and find
A wider road

title: Burn The Bridge Down
lyrics:
[Intro]
(Jagged, glitchy IDM rhythm enters, shifting into a heavy progressive groove)
(Chopped background vocals glitching)
Yeah...
Turn the page, let it break.

[Verse 1]
We're clinging to the shadows of a crumbling wall
Building fortresses of static, waiting for the fall
But the old world is a prison in a golden frame
You can't find a new horizon if you play the same game
Fretless strings bending, pulling at the seams
Wake up from the comfort of your rusted dreams.

[Chorus]
Let the fire burn the bridge down!
We are moving to a new ground!
No more waiting in the cold light,
We are stepping into our night!
(Stacked harmonies surge, anthemic and heavy)
Embrace the tide, let it wash away,
The future's starting today!

[Verse 2]
(Interlocking polyrhythms, deep tom groove)
Heavy steps on concrete, the rhythm starts to shift
Every jagged corner is a catalyst, a gift
We are stubborn, we are frightened, but we have to advance
Step out of the cycle, take a terrifying chance
Let the bass slap, let the truth sting
Hear the new song that we're about to sing.

[Chorus]
Let the fire burn the bridge down!
We are moving to a new ground!
No more waiting in the cold light,
We are stepping into our night!
(Anthemic peaks with intense group chants)
Embrace the tide, let it wash away,
The future's starting today!

[Bridge]
(Dramatic half-time breakdown)
(Saxophone wails through a dense dark wave texture)
No more looking back.
No more fading to black.
(Choir swells alongside gritty Memphis chops)
Rise up! Rise!

[Outro]
(Escalating epic finale, progressive guitar counterpoint)
Embrace the change!
We advance!
We advance!
(Final sharp IDM rhythmic cut, trailing saxophone echo)

title: Step Into The Light
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Static on the wire, rust upon the gear
Clinging to the shadow of another year
Standing on the threshold, frozen at the gate
Breathing in the ashes of a dead estate

[Pre-Chorus]
The floor is giving way beneath the stone
You cannot build a future on a bone

[Chorus]
Break the mold, step into the light
Burn the maps of yesterday tonight
Embrace the shift, let the current run
The old world dies to welcome in the sun
Break the mold! Step into the light!

[Verse 2]
Polyrhythmic pressure pushing through the wall
Every single anchor is about to fall
Jagged tempo turning, sacred ground untied
Life is waiting past the safety of the side

[Pre-Chorus]
The floor is giving way beneath the stone
You cannot build a future on a bone

[Chorus]
Break the mold, step into the light
Burn the maps of yesterday tonight
Embrace the shift, let the current run
The old world dies to welcome in the sun
Break the mold! Step into the light!

[Breakdown]
Half-time weight, heavy percussive slap
No turning back to the comfortable trap
Choreograph the change, feel the rhythm shift
Every step forward is a second gift

[Outro]
Escalating finale, rising up higher
Leaving the wreckage, walking through fire
Embrace the change!
Embrace the change!
Step into the light!

title: Wanting and the Promise
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I want your hand to find mine in a crowded room
Want your eyes to say I’m still the one you choose
Then I count the doors that opened when I made it through
And wonder if the clapping means I’m known by you

[Pre-Chorus]
I keep a ledger in my chest
Of every vow I haven’t met
The hungry part says, “Take your turn”
The faithful part says, “Wait, return”

[Chorus]
How do I hold the wanting and the promise?
How do I climb and still look back?
I can reach for love without possessing
I can build without becoming what I lack
Let the good I leave be more than my name
Let the ones I love not pay for my flame
I won’t make one voice rule over all
I’ll hear them—and answer when they call

[Verse 2]
I want the work to matter when my hands are gone
A kinder room for those who have to carry on
But every bright ambition has a shadowed cost
And someone waits at home when I get lost

[Pre-Chorus]
The promise isn’t just a chain
It’s how I keep my word through change
I can revise the road I take
But not pretend the hearts won’t break

[Chorus]
How do I hold the wanting and the promise?
How do I climb and still look back?
I can reach for love without possessing
I can build without becoming what I lack
Let the good I leave be more than my name
Let the ones I love not pay for my flame
I won’t make one voice rule over all
I’ll hear them—and answer when they call

[Breakdown]
Name what I want
Name what I owe
Who needs my presence?
What can I let go?
No crown is worth the people left waiting
No vow is alive if it asks me to stop changing

[Final Chorus]
I can hold the wanting and the promise
I can rise and keep my word intact
I’ll reach for love with open hands now
I’ll do the work and tend the ties I have
Let the good I leave be shared, not claimed
Let my ambition learn a gentler name
When all my voices rise and call
I’ll choose with care—and carry all

[Outro]
Not every hunger needs the wheel
Not every duty means stand still
I can want, and I can stay
I can choose again each day

title: Room Enough to Choose
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I count the small permissions in your face,
A hand that stays, a chair pulled close.
I want to be the name you choose,
Not just the one who knows the door.
Then morning asks what I have made,
And who will say I earned my place.
I chase the proof, I chase the praise,
And hear your quiet needs beneath it all.

[Pre-Chorus]
Every want can wear a crown,
Every vow can weigh me down.
If I grip one part too hard,
Who gets left outside my heart?

[Chorus]
I am more than what I’m owed,
More than what I have to show.
Let me want and still be true,
Let me build a life that makes room for you.
When the hungry parts take hold,
I can name them, not obey them whole.
I’ll choose the promise, choose the good,
And bring my wanting with me as I should.

[Verse 2]
I want the room to turn and see,
The years of work beneath my name.
But praise can vanish by the dawn,
And leave the work, the people, still the same.
I want my hands to leave things better,
A kinder answer, a door held wide.
Not every good deed needs a witness;
Some roots do their work out of sight.

[Pre-Chorus]
There are promises I made
Before the fever, before the stage.
I can’t call a duty small
Just because it asks me not to run.

[Chorus]
I am more than what I’m owed,
More than what I have to show.
Let me want and still be true,
Let me build a life that makes room for you.
When the hungry parts take hold,
I can name them, not obey them whole.
I’ll choose the promise, choose the good,
And bring my wanting with me as I should.

[Breakdown]
Love is not a prize I win.
Work is not the whole of me.
Duty is not a locked room.
I can open it and breathe.
I can say, “I want to matter,”
Without making that my law.
I can keep the word I gave you
And still ask what I am for.

[Final Chorus]
I am more than what I’m owed,
More than what I have to show.
Let me want and still be true,
Let me build a life that makes room for you.
When the hungry parts take hold,
I can name them, not obey them whole.
I’ll choose the promise, choose the good,
And bring my wanting with me as I should.

[Outro]
I don’t have to silence any part.
I can give each one its place.
Wanting, keeping, making good—
One heart, with room enough to choose.

title: Carry Both Their Names
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I count the yeses I gave out loud
Beside the doors I wanted to kick down
Your coat still hangs by the kitchen chair
I said I'd be there; I said I'd care
Then the room applauds and I turn to look
At the name I carved in a borrowed book
Tell me, when did wanting become a claim
On every hand that calls my name?

[Pre-Chorus]
I want to be wanted, I want to be known
I want my work to outlive my bones
But every promise has someone's face
And every road takes up its space

[Chorus]
Which voice gets the wheel when the roads divide?
The one that says, "Be loved," the one that says, "Be alive"?
The one that says, "Make something good of your time"?
Or the word I gave you when the hour was kind?
I won't call hunger holy, I won't call duty chains
I'll choose what I can answer for and carry both their names

[Verse 2]
I picture a room where the work gets done
A safer street, a table with room for one
I want to leave more than a polished stone
Some proof that the good we made was grown
Still I chase the nod from a stranger's seat
And measure my worth by a loud receipt
You touch my sleeve; I look past your eyes
As if the next bright thing could make me right

[Pre-Chorus]
I want to be wanted, I want to be known
I want my work to outlive my bones
But love is not a medal pinned on my chest
And care is not the prize for doing my best

[Chorus]
Which voice gets the wheel when the roads divide?
The one that says, "Be loved," the one that says, "Be alive"?
The one that says, "Make something good of your time"?
Or the word I gave you when the hour was kind?
I won't call hunger holy, I won't call duty chains
I'll choose what I can answer for and carry both their names

[Bridge]
No single self deserves the throne
No vow can make a heart its own
So tell the truth before you run
Ask what the cost will be to someone
Make room to fail, make room to mend
Keep your word, or speak before it ends
Let praise pass through; let love stay near
And choose again when the path gets clear

[Breakdown]
Not every want is an order
Not every promise is right
Say what I need; say what I owe
Then meet the morning with both in sight

[Final Chorus]
I take the wheel where the roads divide
I can want to be loved and still choose a life
I can build something good without worshipping shine
I can honor the promise or redraw its line
I won't call hunger holy, I won't call duty chains
I'll choose what I can answer for and carry both their names

[Outro]
The room goes quiet; your coat's still there

title: Auditioning for Friends
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep your little checkmark pinned beside my name
Refresh until the numbers tell me I’m okay
I miss the bus, I miss the call, I miss my sister’s meal
Just to watch a stranger tap a heart that isn’t real

[Pre-Chorus]
I trade the thing I meant to say
For what might make you stay

[Chorus]
Tell me I’m enough, tell me again
I spend my whole life auditioning for friends
I bend till every honest edge is gone
Then wonder why I don’t know what I want
Tell me I’m enough, just once, just then—
I’ll be back tomorrow asking you again

[Verse 2]
Your silence turns the hallway into evidence and court
I write three careful versions of a simple little thought
The rent is late, the kettle’s cold, my people stopped by twice
I said “I’m fine” so smoothly I almost believed the lie

[Pre-Chorus]
I make a home inside your praise
And lose my own address

[Chorus]
Tell me I’m enough, tell me again
I spend my whole life auditioning for friends
I bend till every honest edge is gone
Then wonder why I don’t know what I want
Tell me I’m enough, just once, just then—
I’ll be back tomorrow asking you again

[Breakdown]
Take back the key I gave away
I can’t keep living on display
No more measuring my breath
By the room’s approval yet

[Bridge]
If you love me, let me disagree
Let me leave a message unanswered and breathe
I’ll show up late to my own defense
And learn that a boundary isn’t the end

[Final Chorus]
I am enough, even unseen
I’m more than the sum of your changing screen
I’ll keep the parts I nearly erased
And give my own name a little more space
I am enough; I’ll say it again
No more auditioning to be let in

[Outro]
The kettle sings; I call my sister back
The day is mine, and I am coming back

title: My Hands Off the Handle
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep your number pinned above my bed
Like a verdict I can’t turn away
I rehearse the joke you didn’t laugh at
Then apologize for taking up the day
I cancel plans to wait beside the phone
Call it patience, call it being kind
You say “you’re fine” and I collect the words
Like they could pay the rent inside my mind

[Pre-Chorus]
Every yes I give you costs me something
Every no gets swallowed before it’s said

[Chorus]
I’m spending my life for a little approval
Borrowing your eyes to decide what I’m worth
I bend till the shape of me’s barely familiar
Then blame my own heart when it breaks under the work
Say my name like you mean it, and I’ll stay till I’m empty
Say you’re disappointed, I’ll crawl back once more
I keep feeding the hunger that’s eating my living
And still I come asking for a little bit more

[Verse 2]
Missed the train with your coat in my hands
You were late, but I said it was my fault
Told my sister I was busy again
While your silence rang louder than her call
I trade sleep for a sentence from you
Trade my paycheck for a weekend away
Then you leave your cup beside the sink
And I’m the one who cleans up what you say

[Pre-Chorus]
Every yes I give you costs me something
I can feel the small refusals turning red

[Chorus]
I’m spending my life for a little approval
Borrowing your eyes to decide what I’m worth
I bend till the shape of me’s barely familiar
Then blame my own heart when it breaks under the work
Say my name like you mean it, and I’ll stay till I’m empty
Say you’re disappointed, I’ll crawl back once more
I keep feeding the hunger that’s eating my living
And still I come asking for a little bit more

[Breakdown]
No more waiting by the phone
No more calling need devotion
I can love you, I can leave
I can let my own voice reach me

[Final Chorus]
I won’t spend my life for a little approval
I’m done using your eyes to decide what I’m worth
I’m learning the shape of the self I abandoned
And calling it home when I stand on this earth
Say my name like you mean it—I’ll hear it within me
Your disappointment can stay at your door
I won’t keep feeding the hunger that’s eating my living
I’m taking my hands off the handle once more

[Outro]
My hands off the handle
My feet on the floor
I am not an apology
I am worth more

title: First Few Days
genres: IDM-led Riddim meets melodic progressive rock at 138 BPM
with jagged tempo shifts and interlocking polyrhythms; percussive bass slaps and singing fretless bass lock against distorted rhythm guitars
and tom-heavy drums. Intimate syncopated conversational male baritone verses surge into explosive anthemic choruses over a bright major hook
and gritty sustained peaks; a dramatic half-time breakdown drives an escalating epic finale. Stereo room mics
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You call it fate when the room turns new
A borrowed jacket, a name you chew
You learn her coffee, you learn her street
Then leave before the pattern can repeat

[Pre-Chorus]
I tell myself I’m kind, I’m only passing through
But every fresh beginning has me lying to you

[Chorus]
I’m in love with the first few days
The open door, the unguarded face
I swear I mean it when I say your name
Then chase that spark and leave the flame
I keep my halo polished bright
While somebody else can’t sleep at night
I want the start, the rush, the shine
And call the wreckage not mine

[Verse 2]
Your blue cup’s still beside the sink
I bought it yesterday, or so I think
You left a note beneath the keys
I read it twice, then felt relieved

[Pre-Chorus]
I say I never promised more than I could give
But I keep collecting proof that I know how to live

[Chorus]
I’m in love with the first few days
The open door, the unguarded face
I swear I mean it when I say your name
Then chase that spark and leave the flame
I keep my halo polished bright
While somebody else can’t sleep at night
I want the start, the rush, the shine
And call the wreckage not mine

[Breakdown]
Tell me I’m good
Tell me I tried
I can make mercy sound like pride
New hands, new laugh
Same old escape
How many goodbyes can a good man make?

[Final Chorus]
I’m in love with the first few days
The open door, the unguarded face
I swear I mean it when I say your name
Then chase that spark and leave the flame
I keep my halo polished bright
While somebody else can’t sleep at night
I want the start, the rush, the shine
But all these endings still are mine

[Outro]
Still are mine
Still are mine

title: A Little Wreckage
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I keep the porch light on for everyone who calls
I know the names of every neighbor’s dog
I carry soup when winter takes the stairs
And say, “I’m here,” like that should mend the air

[Pre-Chorus]
But there are coats I never gave back
And goodbyes I let go slack

[Chorus]
I meant to be kind, I meant to be true
Still left a little wreckage walking through
The doors swung wide, the road ran smooth
I had my share of luck—and so did you
I’m sorry for the hearts I couldn’t hold
For promises that thinned before they’d grown
I tried to love you with the hands I had
And still, I know, I left you sad

[Verse 2]
The old friends wave from tables by the glass
I smile, then watch the moment hurry past
A letter waits beneath the fruit bowl’s ring
I write the truth, then soften everything

[Pre-Chorus]
I never meant to make you small
But meaning well won’t mend it all

[Chorus]
I meant to be kind, I meant to be true
Still left a little wreckage walking through
The doors swung wide, the road ran smooth
I had my share of luck—and so did you
I’m sorry for the hearts I couldn’t hold
For promises that thinned before they’d grown
I tried to love you with the hands I had
And still, I know, I left you sad

[Bridge]
No grand excuse, no noble line
Can turn your hurt to something fine
I’ll sit and hear what I put you through
And let the silence tell me what is true

[Final Chorus]
I meant to be kind, I meant to be true
I see the little wreckage walking through
The doors swung wide, the road ran smooth
I had my share of luck—and so did you
I’m sorry for the hearts I couldn’t hold
For promises I should have kept and grown
I’ll try to love you with a steadier hand
And honor every place where you still stand

[Outro]
I had my share of luck
I know you had your cost

title: Choose With My Eyes
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You text me, “Come through,” and I’m halfway out the door
Keys in my fist, one shoe on the floor
My pulse votes yes before I read the room
My better sense says, “Wait. You know this tune.”

[Pre-Chorus]
I make a case, I make a plan
Then want you more than either can

[Chorus]
My heart runs red lights, my head pulls the brake
One says, “Go on,” one says, “Think what it’ll take”
I’m caught in the turn with my hands on the wheel
Too quick to be wise, too awake not to feel
If I choose you tonight, let me choose with my eyes
Not just the rush, not just the alibi

[Verse 2]
Your laugh in the doorway, your coat on the chair
I know all the reasons I shouldn’t stay there
Still, when you ask me if I’m doing alright
Every careful answer comes loose for the night

[Pre-Chorus]
I count to four, I count to ten
Then start the argument again

[Chorus]
My heart runs red lights, my head pulls the brake
One says, “Go on,” one says, “Think what it’ll take”
I’m caught in the turn with my hands on the wheel
Too quick to be wise, too awake not to feel
If I choose you tonight, let me choose with my eyes
Not just the rush, not just the alibi

[Breakdown]
Hold on
Not every want is a warning
Hold on
Not every pause means goodbye

[Bridge]
I can want you and still ask what comes after
I can hear my own voice beneath all the laughter
No grand escape, no perfect sign
Just one honest breath, then a choice that is mine

[Final Chorus]
My heart runs red lights, my head pulls the brake
Both tell the truth in the mess that they make
I’m here at the turn with my hands on the wheel
Not ruled by the rush, not afraid of the feel
If I choose you tonight, let me choose with my eyes
Let the yes be a yes I can own in daylight

[Outro]
Keys in my hand, I can still take my time
Your door is open; the next step is mine

title: The Blue Cup
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I kept the chipped blue cup from our first flat
Your father’s laugh still lives inside that crack
I took the long way home through orchard rows
And watched our daughter learn the names of roads
I have been loved in ways I couldn’t plan
I’ve had my turn; I know how lucky I am

[Pre-Chorus]
So why does morning make me count the years?
Why does an open door feel sharp with fear?

[Chorus]
I wouldn’t trade the life I got to live
Not one hard mile, not one more thing to give
But what is waiting past the bend ahead?
I meet the open days with careful steps
I’m glad I came this far, I mean it true
And still, the rest feels strange to walk into

[Verse 2]
The garden leans against the kitchen wall
The plum tree drops its fruit before the fall
Old friends send photographs from far away
Their hair goes silver in the same bright way
I smile and tell them all that I am fine
Then stare too long at next year on the line

[Pre-Chorus]
I’ve made my peace with what I can’t undo
But not with all the room that’s left to move through

[Chorus]
I wouldn’t trade the life I got to live
Not one hard mile, not one more thing to give
But what is waiting past the bend ahead?
I meet the open days with careful steps
I’m glad I came this far, I mean it true
And still, the rest feels strange to walk into

[Bridge]
Maybe the fear is proof I still have plans
A seat to pull out, a hand to understand
A road I’ve never taken, rain or sun
A dozen ordinary mornings left undone

[Breakdown]
I don’t need answers carved in stone
Just let the next day be its own
One more good meal, one window thrown wide
One more hello before goodbye

[Final Chorus]
I wouldn’t trade the life I got to live
The tender years, the things I couldn’t fix
But what is waiting past the bend ahead?
I’ll meet the open days with careful steps
I’m glad I came this far, I mean it true
And I can be afraid and still walk through

[Outro]
The blue cup waits beside the sink
Tomorrow comes before I think

title: Light Beside the Door
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I map the grid, I trace the line
Try to keep the shadows right on time
Clear out the debris, sweep the floor
Leave a little light beside the door
I aim for grace, I aim for ground
Try to pick the broken pieces up when they surround
And then I step right where the tile gives way
A sudden turn I didn't mean to make today

[Pre-Chorus]
And the ledger sways, the balance dips
Words I never wanted slipped right off my lips
I try to hold the weight and keep it steady
Standing in the flood before I'm ready

[Chorus]
I wanted to be the light in the dark!
I wanted to build a haven from the spark!
I’m reaching for good with both open hands
Even when the ground turns into shifting sands!
I mess up the timing, I miss the cue
I break what I promised I was gonna do
But I’m still standing here, I’m still standing true
Trying to be good for you!

[Verse 2]
The intentions were clean, the motive was clear
I tried to pull the safety close, bring it near

I spend half the night sweeping up the glass
Asking how the slip could come to pass

[Pre-Chorus]

Trying to be good for you!

[Bridge]
[Dramatic half-time breakdown]
It isn't an excuse, it isn't a plea
I own every fracture that you see
I know the damage doesn't disappear
Just 'cause the reason behind it was sincere
[Chaotic polyrhythms, percussive bass slaps]
So I take the blow, I take the stain
I pick up the tools and I start again!

[Guitar Solo]
[Counterpoint lead guitar over fretless bass and dynamic tempo shifts]

[Chorus]
I wanted to be the light in the dark!
I wanted to build a haven from the spark!
I’m reaching for good with both open hands
Even when the ground turns into shifting sands!
I mess up the timing, I miss the cue
I break what I promised I was gonna do
But I’m still standing here, I’m still standing true
Trying to be good for you!

[Outro]
[Epic finale, escalating final section]
I’ll fix the line, I’ll clear the floor
Leave the light beside the door
Still reaching out...
Still reaching out...
[Tape saturation fade]

title: A Heavier Grace
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You sit behind your polished glass
And judge the way the shadows pass
You hold your rules up like a shield
And wonder why the rest don't yield
You call it blind, you call it wrong
When someone doesn't sing your song

[Pre-Chorus]
But every mind is built of stone and sea
A different history
A different key

[Chorus]
WIDEN THE LENS!
OPEN THE DOOR!
WE ARE NOT FIGHTING THIS WAR ANYMORE!
Stop demanding they look through your eyes
Stop turning differences into a prize
To understand is a heavier grace
Than winning a race

[Verse 2]
It's easier to point and shame
To give the stranger's world a name
To lock the door and keep them out
And build a fortress of your doubt
But empathy is hard and slow
It takes a willingness to grow

[Chorus]
WIDEN THE LENS!
OPEN THE DOOR!
WE ARE NOT FIGHTING THIS WAR ANYMORE!
Stop demanding they look through your eyes
Stop turning differences into a prize
To understand is a heavier grace
Than winning a race

[Bridge]
Maybe they walked a harder road
Maybe they carry a different load
Before you judge the path they chose
Remember everything it rose from

[Final Chorus]
WIDEN THE LENS!
OPEN THE DOOR!
WE ARE NOT FIGHTING THIS WAR ANYMORE!
Stop demanding they look through your eyes
Stop turning differences into a prize
To understand is a heavier grace
Than winning a race

[Outro]
Reach across
Step outside
Meet them where they are

title: We Get Stronger
lyrics:
[Intro]
Before you name me wrong,
Come sit where I have been.

[Verse 1]
You saw the choice I made that day,
Not all the miles that led that way.
You heard one sentence, drew a line;
I missed your hurt, you missed mine.

So hold the verdict, ask me why.
I’ll make some room; you tell me yours.
We don’t have to trade our truth
To open up another door.

[Pre-Chorus]
Take one breath, let the first thought pass.
Look past the label, look at the face.

[Chorus]
Stand up, reach out, make a little room!
Try to see the world from somebody else’s shoes!
We can disagree and still refuse
To shame a heart for seeing a different view.
Ask one more question, hear one more truth—
We get stronger when we make room!

[Verse 2]
Your road was built on different ground;

lyrics:

You draw a line in the dust, demanding everyone agree

lyrics:

There’s a whole life behind a stranger’s face

[Chorus]
I won’t make a weapon of being right

[Pre-Chorus]
Hold the verdict, leave a little space

[Chorus]
I won’t make a weapon of being right
I’ll ask what it’s like from the other side
You don’t have to see it the way I do
For me to make some room for you
We can disagree and still stand near
Trade the easy blame for a harder ear
Before I shame you for the way you see
I’ll try to understand what shaped your view of me

[Bridge]
Maybe your map was drawn in a storm
Maybe mine was handed to me warm
Neither story tells the whole of us
So let the first question be, “What have I missed?”
No, empathy is not surrender
It’s courage with the doors thrown wide
I can hold my ground and still remember
There’s a human being on your side

[Breakdown]
Ask me why
I’ll tell you true
Then I’ll turn around
And ask you, too

[Final Chorus]
I won’t make a weapon of being right
I’ll ask what it’s like from the other side
You don’t have to see it the way I do
For me to make some room for you
We can disagree and still stand near
Trade the easy blame for a harder ear
Before I shame you for the way you see
I’ll try to understand what shaped your view of me

[Outro]
A little more room
A little less blame
We meet as people
Before we name

lyrics:
[Intro]
(Fast, technical guitar riffs, double-bass drum build-up)

[Verse 1]
We draw the battle lines inside our heads
We weaponize the things they left unsaid
We build a fortress out of what we know
And cast out anyone who doesn't show
The same scars, the same view, the same design
But human hearts don't follow one straight line

[Pre-Chorus]
It's easy to judge from the hill of your pride

But tearing them down doesn't make you look tall
So tear down the barriers, break through the wall!

[Chorus]
WIDEN THE LENS! OPEN YOUR EYES!
BEFORE YOU CONDEMN, TRY TO EMPATHIZE!
It’s a different horizon, a different sky
But we’re all just looking for reasons why!
Put down the stones! Pull them into the light!
Understanding is bolder than proving you're right!
(Yeah, understanding is bolder!)

[Verse 2]
They see the world through glass of different hues
They walked a road that didn't leave your shoes
The things you take for granted they must fight
What makes you tremble keeps them up at night
Don't demand their silence just to soothe your fear
There is a holy space in learning how to hear

[Pre-Chorus]
It's easy to judge from the hill of your pride
Shaming the wanderer walking outside
But tearing them down doesn't make you look tall
So tear down the barriers, break through the wall!

title: Where It Hurts
lyrics:
[Intro]
You came in carrying a whole world
I only saw the part I knew

[Verse 1]
You keep your coat on in July
I used to call that strange
Then you told me what the cold can do
And how a body keeps its names
You count the exits when we talk
I thought you weren’t listening
Now I leave a little room beside me
For the things you’re holding in

[Pre-Chorus]
I don’t have to see it your way
To believe you when you say
It’s real to you

[Chorus]
So tell me where it hurts
I’ll try to understand
I won’t turn your hardest day
Into a verdict on who you are
We can disagree and still make room
We can ask before we accuse
I’m learning how to hear you through
I’m here, I’m here with you

[Verse 2]
You changed your mind at the kitchen sink
With the tap still running cold
I nearly made a joke of it
Then I let the silence hold
You’ve got reasons I can’t carry
You’ve got truths I haven’t known
So I’ll quit keeping score of every turn
And let your story stand its own

[Pre-Chorus]
I don’t have to share your map
To stop and hear the ground you’re on
Before I answer back

[Chorus]
So tell me where it hurts
I’ll try to understand
I won’t turn your hardest day
Into a verdict on who you are
We can disagree and still make room
We can ask before we accuse
I’m learning how to hear you through
I’m here, I’m here with you

[Bridge]
No one gets wiser from a finger in their face
No one finds a safer door by being put to shame
I can hold my own conviction
And still leave yours some space
We’re more than one bad sentence
More than one mistake

[Final Chorus]
So tell me where it hurts
I’ll try to understand
I won’t turn your hardest day
Into a verdict on who you are
We can disagree and still make room
We can ask before we accuse
I’m learning how to hear you through
I’m here, I’m here with you

[Outro]
I don’t need to win this moment
I just want to know you true
Tell me where it hurts
I’m here with you

title: Before I Judge
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You came in carrying weather I can’t see
A whole long week tucked underneath your sleeve
I had my answer ready, sharp and clean
Then I saw your hands were shaking as you spoke to me

[Pre-Chorus]
I don’t have to lose my ground
To let your truth be heard out loud

[Chorus]
Hold up—let me hear you
Tell me where the hurt began
I can disagree and still reach out a hand
We don’t have to match to meet here where we stand
I’ll try to understand
Before I judge who you are

[Verse 2]
You learned your rules in a different kind of home
I learned mine from the people I’ve known
One hard sentence doesn’t tell your whole life through
There’s more beneath the thing that I can’t get used to

[Pre-Chorus]
I can ask before I accuse
There’s room for more than one point of view

[Chorus]
Hold up—let me hear you
Tell me where the hurt began
I can disagree and still reach out a hand
We don’t have to match to meet here where we stand
I’ll try to understand
Before I judge who you are

[Bridge]
When you stumble, I won’t make a stage of it
When I’m wrong, I hope you’ll say it plain
We can leave a little room between us
For a question, for a name

[Final Chorus]
Hold up—let me hear you
Tell me where the hurt began
I can disagree and still reach out a hand
We don’t have to match to meet here where we stand
No shame, no stones, no turning you away
I’ll try to understand
Before I judge who you are

[Outro]
Before I judge who you are
I’ll try to understand

title: Where You Stand
lyrics:
[Intro]
You got a reason I can't see
I got a story under me

[Verse 1]
You cut the line at the grocery store
I saw your hands shake by the door
I had a speech already formed
Then caught the rain on your uniform

You said your kid was running hot
Your phone was dead, your ride was not
I kept my judgment in my teeth
And made some room for what I couldn't see

[Pre-Chorus]
I don't have to call it right
To hear what brought you here tonight
I can ask before I accuse
There's more than one way to lose

[Chorus]
Hold up, hear me out
There's a whole life behind that sound
I won't shame you for a different view
I'll try to learn what made it true for you
Hands up, hearts wide
We can disagree and stay beside
If I want the world to understand
I'll start by trying where you stand

[Verse 2]
You grew up where the mill shut down
I learned my facts in a safer town
Your father kept the porch light on
Mine left before the snow was gone

We both know how a room can change
When someone says your name like blame
So when your answer cuts across mine
I'll ask what hurt is underneath the line

[Pre-Chorus]
I don't have to lose my ground
To let another truth be found
I can draw a boundary, still be kind
And leave a little space to change my mind

[Chorus]
Hold up, hear me out
There's a whole life behind that sound
I won't shame you for a different view
I'll try to learn what made it true for you
Hands up, hearts wide
We can disagree and stay beside
If I want the world to understand
I'll start by trying where you stand

[Bridge]
Not every wound is mine to mend
Not every talk will make us friends
But I can quit the easy laugh
And see the person, not the photograph

You can tell me I got it wrong
I'll take a breath and listen long
No perfect words, no clean escape
Just one more chance to meet face to face

[Final Chorus]
Hold up, hear me out
There's a whole life behind that sound
I won't shame you for a different view
I'll try to learn what made it true for you
Hands up, hearts wide
We can disagree and stay beside
If I want the world to understand
I'll start by trying where you stand

[Outro]
Ask one question
Stay awhile
Make some room
Across the aisle

title: Make Room for You
lyrics:
[Intro]
I don't have to win the room
To make a little space
I can meet you where you stand
And look you in the face

[Verse 1]
You read the world through different glass
I read it through my own
We turn our reasons into walls
Then call the other stone

I know the heat that climbs the throat
When certainty feels safe
But every person carries roads
No map can fully trace

[Pre-Chorus]
So before I name your failure
Before I make you small
I'll ask what shaped the way you see
And listen through it all

[Chorus]
I won't shame you for the window
That you learned to look through
You don't have to think like me
For me to make room for you
We can hold two truths together
Let the hard words lose their flame
I'll try to understand your heart
Before I judge your name

[Verse 2]
Your silence may be armor
Your anger may be fear
The joke I took as cruelty
Could hide a harder year

I don't need to bless the damage
I don't need to call it right
But I can draw a line with care
And leave your worth in sight

[Pre-Chorus]
If I only love the people
Who reflect my point of view
Then I'm guarding my reflection
Not discovering what's true

[Chorus]
I won't shame you for the window
That you learned to look through
You don't have to think like me
For me to make room for you
We can hold two truths together
Let the hard words lose their flame
I'll try to understand your heart
Before I judge your name

[Bridge]
Tell me what you carried here
Tell me what you couldn't say
Tell me where the ground gave way
And what still keeps you brave

I may challenge what you're doing
I may disagree out loud
But I won't turn your human life
Into a target for the crowd

[Breakdown]
Ask first!
Stay kind!
Leave room!
Change your mind!

[Final Chorus]
I won't shame you for the window
That you learned to look through
You don't have to think like me
For me to make room for you
We can hold two truths together
Without surrendering our spine
I'll protect your right to differ
While I draw a boundary line

[Final Refrain]
Different eyes, a wider picture
Different roads, the same unknown
If I want to be understood
I've got to understand your own

[Outro]
Before I call you broken
Before I turn away
I'll remember you are human
And I'm learning every day

title: Bend by the Mill
lyrics:
[Intro]
You said the river runs east
I said it bends by the mill
We stood there guarding our maps
While the water kept moving still

[Verse 1]
You grew up counting every dollar
I learned to spend before it’s gone
You learned to keep your answers ready
I learned to wait and carry on
I called your caution something colder
You called my questions picking fights
We named each other from a distance
And missed the reasons in our lives

[Pre-Chorus]
So tell me where the hurt began
I’ll set my verdict down
I may not see it as you do
But I can hear you now

[Chorus]
I don’t have to share your view
To make some room for where you’re coming from
I can ask before I accuse
And leave a little space for what I haven’t learned
We’re more than one mistaken sentence
More than one bad afternoon
I’ll try to understand you
Before I turn away from you

[Verse 2]
You keep your coat beside the doorway
You never know who might need warmth
I thought you planned to leave the table
You said you’d learned to watch the storm
I heard a joke and missed the warning
You heard my quiet as contempt
We carry whole unspoken histories
Into every word that’s left unsaid

[Pre-Chorus]
So tell me what I didn’t catch
I’ll listen past my pride
The truth can hold another truth
And neither has to hide

[Chorus]
I don’t have to share your view
To make some room for where you’re coming from
I can ask before I accuse
And leave a little space for what I haven’t learned
We’re more than one mistaken sentence
More than one bad afternoon
I’ll try to understand you
Before I turn away from you

[Bridge]
Not every wound is mine to measure
Not every fear looks like my own
A softer question isn’t surrender
It’s how we keep a door unclosed
If I was sharp, I’ll say I’m sorry
If you were scared, you can say so
We can set the stones down slowly
And let the next small sentence grow

[Group Chant]
Hear me out
I’ll hear you out
No one gets reduced to doubt
Hear me out
I’ll hear you out
We can turn this thing around

[Final Chorus]
I don’t have to share your view
To make some room for where you’re coming from
I can ask before I accuse
And leave a little space for what I haven’t learned
We’re more than one mistaken sentence
More than one bad afternoon
I’ll try to understand you
I’ll keep a place beside me for you

[Outro]
You said the river runs east
I watched it bend by the mill
We didn’t settle every question
But we stood there listening still

title: Leave a Little Room Inside
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You came in carrying Monday on your face
I had a clever answer ready in its place
Then I saw your hands were shaking round the cup
So I let the silence say enough

You told me why the old road still feels safe
I named the parts that never fit my map
We stood there with our reasons in the air
And for a minute, neither had to win

[Pre-Chorus]
I can ask before I decide
I can leave a little room inside

[Chorus]
Tell me where it hurts, I’ll try to understand
I don’t have to see it just the way you can
We can disagree and still be kind
Your world is real, though it isn’t mine
No, I won’t make a lesson of your pain
Or use your hardest day to speak your name
I’ll meet you there, with open hands
And do my best to understand

[Verse 2]
You learned your truth in a different kind of home
I learned mine from the people I was shown
Both of us have missed what others meant
Both of us have words we should’ve left unsent

So when your voice gets sharp, I’ll take a breath
There’s more beneath the sentence than I guessed
And when I’m wrong, I’ll say it plain and clear
Not every change is something I should fear

[Pre-Chorus]
I can ask before I decide
I can leave a little room inside

[Chorus]
Tell me where it hurts, I’ll try to understand
I don’t have to see it just the way you can
We can disagree and still be kind
Your world is real, though it isn’t mine
No, I won’t make a lesson of your pain
Or use your hardest day to speak your name
I’ll meet you there, with open hands
And do my best to understand

[Bridge]
Nobody gets the whole story
From the doorway or the street
Every heart has private weather
Every life has missing pages
If I cannot know your whole road
I can still walk beside you
I can listen without turning
Every difference to a trial

[Final Chorus]
Tell me where it hurts, I’ll try to understand
I don’t have to see it just the way you can
We can disagree and still be kind
Your world is real, though it isn’t mine
No, I won’t make a lesson of your pain
Or shame you for the shape your thoughts became
I’ll meet you there, with open hands
And do my best to understand

[Outro]
I’ll ask before I decide
Leave a little room inside
Your world is real, though it isn’t mine
I’ll do my best to understand

title: Two Roads Through One Heart
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You pull me east with a paper map
I turn back west when the road goes black
One hand reaches, one hand retreats
Two different truths in the same heartbeat

You say, “Stay,” while the doorway calls
I count the cracks running up these walls
I want the harbor, I want the tide
I want your hand and the open wide

[Pre-Chorus]
I keep both answers under my tongue
Afraid to choose, afraid to be wrong

[Chorus]
My heart is a compass spinning in the rain
Pointing toward you, then away again
I’m caught between the leaving and the stay
Between the words I mean and what I say
If I choose one road, another disappears
So I hold both directions close to here
My heart keeps pulling, pulling me apart
Two roads running through one heart

[Verse 2]
Your coffee cools beside the kitchen sink
I hear the train before I let myself think
You fold my jacket across the chair
Like leaving is already waiting there

I know the comfort of your familiar room
The blue chipped bowl, the late-afternoon
But somewhere past the last familiar sign
A version of me is asking for time

[Pre-Chorus]
I keep both answers under my tongue
Afraid to choose, afraid to be wrong

[Chorus]
My heart is a compass spinning in the rain
Pointing toward you, then away again
I’m caught between the leaving and the stay
Between the words I mean and what I say
If I choose one road, another disappears
So I hold both directions close to here
My heart keeps pulling, pulling me apart
Two roads running through one heart

[Bridge]
Maybe love is not a locked front door
Maybe leaving doesn’t erase before
Maybe I can miss you and still move
Maybe both things can be true

[Final Chorus]
My heart is a compass, learning how to turn
Not every answer has to be discerned
I can love you and still make my way
I can feel the fear and go anyway
If I choose this road, I’ll carry what we were
The small blue bowl, your coat, the warmth we shared
My heart keeps pulling, but I’ll hear its part
Two roads running through one heart

[Outro]
You pull me east
The open road calls
I take one breath
And walk through it all

title: Little Monsters Trick-or-Treat
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You pin a paper bat above the kitchen door
We carve crooked grins and save the seeds in bowls
Your cape keeps catching on the garden gate
You laugh and say, “The monster’s running late”

We trade our names for witches, ghosts, and kings
A cardboard crown, a cape made out of strings
Then hear the first small footsteps on the stair
And spill a handful of wrapped sweets everywhere

[Pre-Chorus]
The porch is bright with pumpkin faces
Our little crew takes over the places

[Chorus]
Halloween, come on in!
We’ve got candy, crooked grins
Knock once, knock twice, let the whole block know
We’re a pack of little monsters putting on a show
Halloween, what a night!
Paper moons and porch lights
Every silly ghost and goblin gets a treat
And every neighbor saves a sweet for me

[Verse 2]
Your mummy wrap comes loose around your shoe
A tiny dragon asks what dragons do
You roar so loud the dog goes racing by
Then bow like royalty beneath the porch sign

At Mrs. Lee’s, the candy bowl is full
She tells the tale of a black cat named McGull
We tuck one caramel inside each sleeve
And promise we’ll be back next Halloween

[Pre-Chorus]
The porch is bright with pumpkin faces
Our little crew takes over the places

[Chorus]
Halloween, come on in!
We’ve got candy, crooked grins
Knock once, knock twice, let the whole block know
We’re a pack of little monsters putting on a show
Halloween, what a night!
Paper moons and porch lights
Every silly ghost and goblin gets a treat
And every neighbor saves a sweet for me

[Breakdown]
One more door!
One more street!
Save the chocolate!
Count the treats!

[Bridge]
When the last porch candle disappears
We spread our treasure on the stairs
You trade a cherry chew for one blue sweet
Then split the biggest bar in two with me

[Final Chorus]
Halloween, come on in!
We’ve got candy, crooked grins
Knock once, knock twice, let the whole block know
We’re a pack of little monsters putting on a show
Halloween, what a night!
Costume capes and porch lights
Every silly ghost and goblin gets a treat
And every neighbor saves a sweet for me

[Outro]
Your paper bat swings by the kitchen door
We’ll keep the pumpkin smiling one night more

title: Halloween Again
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You’re tying a cape in the kitchen light
Black cat sprawled by the porch all night
A bowl of little paper moons
And sugar dust across your shoes

You paint a grin, I draw a scar
We take the long way past the yard
The neighbor’s skeleton waves hello
And every window puts on a show

[Pre-Chorus]
Come on, the door is open wide
There’s room for every strange disguise

[Chorus]
It’s Halloween, come out and play
We get to be whoever for a day
A witch, a ghost, a king in gold
A little brave, a little bold
So fill your pockets, raise your voice
The night is ours, the choice is yours
When the porch lights beckon, come on in
It’s Halloween again!

[Verse 2]
You trade a handful for a treat
Then race your friends down Maple Street
A dragon tail caught in the gate
We laugh so hard we’re running late

Your little brother’s monster roar
Could scare the hinges off the door
Then Grandma answers, dressed to thrill
With chocolate bars enough to fill

[Pre-Chorus]
Come on, the door is open wide
There’s room for every strange disguise

[Chorus]
It’s Halloween, come out and play
We get to be whoever for a day
A witch, a ghost, a king in gold
A little brave, a little bold
So fill your pockets, raise your voice
The night is ours, the choice is yours
When the porch lights beckon, come on in
It’s Halloween again!

[Bridge: halftime]
When the last small footsteps fade
We sort our treasures on the floor
One crooked mask, one paper crown
And just enough to ask for more

[Build]
One more house!
One more street!
One more handful, something sweet!

[Final Chorus]
It’s Halloween, come out and play
We get to be whoever for a day
A witch, a ghost, a king in gold
A little brave, a little bold
So fill your pockets, raise your voice
The night is ours, the choice is yours
When the porch lights beckon, come on in
It’s Halloween again!

[Outro]
Your cape is dragging, your bag is thin
See you next Halloween again!

title: Our Favorite Kind of Autumn
lyrics:
[Intro]
The porch light paints the pumpkins gold
You tug your paper cape on straight
A bowl of candy by the door
And footsteps racing up the lane

[Verse 1]
You drew a crooked cat in chalk
I pinned a moon upon your sleeve
The little ghosts come two by two
With pillowcases up to their knees

A witch in stripes, a tiny knight
A dragon dragging one green wing
You trade a chocolate for a joke
And every doorway starts to sing

[Pre-Chorus]
The chilly air, the friendly noise
The painted grin, the borrowed voice
For one sweet night, we all can be
Whatever we can dream

[Chorus]
Halloween, come wander through
With silly spells and costumes new
We’ll fill our pockets, laugh and roam
Then share the best treats back at home
Halloween, the night is ours
With paper bats and candy stars
The porch lights shine, the neighbors cheer
Our favorite kind of autumn’s here

[Verse 2]
Your cardboard spaceship bumps the fence
The captain waves and cries, “All clear!”
A little vampire drops his loot
You help him gather every piece

The grown-ups grin behind their masks
A bowl goes empty, then refills
We tell the same old ghost story
And laugh before the scariest bit

[Pre-Chorus]
The chilly air, the friendly noise
The painted grin, the borrowed voice
For one sweet night, we all can be
Whatever we can dream

[Chorus]
Halloween, come wander through
With silly spells and costumes new
We’ll fill our pockets, laugh and roam
Then share the best treats back at home
Halloween, the night is ours
With paper bats and candy stars
The porch lights shine, the neighbors cheer
Our favorite kind of autumn’s here

[Bridge]
When the last small footsteps fade
We tip the candy on the floor
You pick the ones with caramel
I save the wrapped-up orange ones
Your cape is folded on a chair
A paper moon rests by the stairs
And tomorrow, when the sun comes round
We’ll tell the best parts all again

[Final Chorus]
Halloween, come wander through
With silly spells and costumes new
We’ll fill our pockets, laugh and roam
Then share the best treats back at home
Halloween, the night is ours
With paper bats and candy stars
The porch lights shine, the neighbors cheer
Our favorite kind of autumn’s here

[Outro]
The porch light dims, the pumpkins stay
We’ll wear our paper crowns another day

title: Paper Moons and Candy Stars
lyrics:
[Intro]
Porch steps dressed in paper moons
A bowl of sweets beneath the spoon

[Verse 1]
You pin a crooked hat on tight
I draw a grin in green and white
The old sheet snags against the door
We laugh and reach for one more floor

[Pre-Chorus]
The kitchen smells like cinnamon
The neighbors pull their curtains in
You lift your lantern, I take your hand
Tonight the odd ones own the land

[Chorus]
Come on, come out, the night is ours
With stitched-up capes and candy stars
A paper crown, a painted face
We turn the block into our place
Oh, Halloween, let every strange heart shine
Your hand in mine, your hand in mine

[Verse 2]
A tiny ghost in oversized shoes
A pirate captain picking the tunes
The porch pumpkins lean like old friends
We trade our treats at every bend

[Pre-Chorus]
You give the shy kid one more sweet
They take a brave step down the street
A dragon tail sweeps through the leaves
And even grown-ups start to believe

[Chorus]
Come on, come out, the night is ours
With stitched-up capes and candy stars
A paper crown, a painted face
We turn the block into our place
Oh, Halloween, let every strange heart shine
Your hand in mine, your hand in mine

[Bridge]
When the last small footsteps disappear
We set the lanterns by the stair
You peel the silver tape from my sleeve
Still wearing the grin you gave to me

[Final Chorus]
Come on, come out, the night was ours
With stitched-up capes and candy stars
A paper crown, a painted face
We made the whole block our own place
Oh, Halloween, keep that brave heart shine
Your hand in mine, your hand in mine

[Outro]
One more sweet, one more goodbye
Fold the cape and save the night

title: Keep My Door
lyrics:
[Intro]
I keep a chair beside the door
For every heart that asks for more

[Verse 1]
You told me what he said at dawn
I stayed until the shaking passed
She called because the rent was due
I sent the money, skipped my plans

A stranger cried beside the shop
I learned the name of every scar
I thought that care meant opening
Every lock inside my heart

[Pre-Chorus]
I can see the hurt in you
I know the good you’re reaching for
But every hand I pull ashore
Can leave me drowning on the floor

[Chorus]
I can wish you well and still keep my door
I can care without becoming yours
Every wounded soul deserves a place to heal
But I am not the cure for all they feel
If I give my whole heart to every need
There’ll be nothing left for me

[Verse 2]
You said, “You’re all I have,” at two
I wore that sentence like a chain
I answered every late-night call
Then missed my own life all the same

Some people take the warmth you give
And ask you never to grow cold
Love doesn’t mean you have to break
To prove your heart is made of gold

[Pre-Chorus]
I can see the hurt in you
And still decide what I can bear
A boundary isn’t cruelty
It’s room enough to breathe in there

[Chorus]
I can wish you well and still keep my door
I can care without becoming yours
Every wounded soul deserves a place to heal
But I am not the cure for all they feel
If I give my whole heart to every need
There’ll be nothing left for me

[Bridge]
I hope you find a softer landing
I hope somebody stays awhile
I hope the morning meets you gently
I mean it when I say it, smile

But I can’t promise you forever
Because your sorrow called my name
I can love the good that’s in you
Without stepping into the flame

[Group Chants]
Care, not surrender!
Kind, not undone!

[Final Chorus]
I can wish you well and still keep my door
I can care without becoming yours
Every wounded soul deserves a place to heal
But I am not the cure for all they feel
I’ll give what I can, not all I am
I can hold your hand and still stand
If I give my whole heart to every need
There’ll be something left for me

[Outro]
I hope you find your way
I’ll keep a little love for me

title: Mercy Needs a Border
lyrics:
[Intro]
I keep a chair pulled out for every lonely heart
I keep a little mercy ready before the story starts

[Verse 1]
You called me from the laundromat
Your rent was late, your hands were cold
I drove across the county line
And let your whole hard week unfold
You said you’d only need a night
Then asked me what I thought of him
I gave you every honest inch
And watched my own room growing dim

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the ache behind your eyes
I know the words you couldn’t say
But every door I leave unlocked
Lets something of my own life slip away

[Chorus]
I can wish you well without giving you my heart
I can see your hurt and still know where I must part
Every soul deserves a kindness, every wound deserves some care
But I can’t make a home in every heart that needs me there

[Verse 2]
You cried beside the grocery carts
About the friend who let you down
I skipped the dinner I had planned
And drove you safely back to town
The next one swore he’d change by spring
The next had nowhere else to go
I learned to call my rescuing love
Before I knew what love should know

[Pre-Chorus]
Compassion isn’t a vow
To carry every weight alone
A hand can help you find the stairs
Without becoming your whole home

[Chorus]
I can wish you well without giving you my heart
I can see your hurt and still know where I must part
Every soul deserves a kindness, every wound deserves some care
But I can’t make a home in every heart that needs me there

[Bridge]
I’m not the cure for every ache
I’m not the answer to each plea
I’ll sit with you until the morning
But I won’t disappear to prove you need me

[Group Chants]
Care is not surrender!
Mercy needs a border!

[Final Chorus]
I can wish you well and keep my own heart in my hands
I can hear your hurt and still decline the role you planned
Every soul deserves a kindness, every wound deserves some care
I can love the world and choose the ones I carry there

[Outro]
I’ll leave a light on in my kindness
And keep my own door in my care

title: Care Without Surrender
lyrics:
[Intro]
I keep a chair beside the door
A little room for one soul more

[Verse 1]
You told me your brother won’t call
You sleep with your coat on indoors
I knew the ache behind your joke
I stayed until the kettle smoked

You said, “You’re the only one who sees”
I let that sentence fasten me
Then someone else came needing hands
And I was making newer plans

[Pre-Chorus]
I can hear a hurt and answer
I can sit with what you feel
But a heart is not a shelter
I can promise you to build

[Chorus]
I can care without surrender
I can leave the door unlocked
You deserve a love that’s steady
I can’t be every place you’re lost
Every soul I want to rescue
Gets a piece I cannot spare
I can wish you safe tomorrow
Without making my home there

[Verse 2]
At June’s small kitchen, plates stacked high
She said her old friends passed her by
I took her calls through half the night
And missed the life I’d left outside

Then Mara showed me cracked phone screens
A father’s words, a landlord’s fees
I gave her Sundays, gave her sleep
Till promises grew hard to keep

[Pre-Chorus]
I can hear a hurt and answer
I can sit with what you feel
But a heart is not a shelter
I can promise you to build

[Chorus]
I can care without surrender
I can leave the door unlocked
You deserve a love that’s steady
I can’t be every place you’re lost
Every soul I want to rescue
Gets a piece I cannot spare
I can wish you safe tomorrow
Without making my home there

[Bridge: piano and tense, low choir]
If I say no, you may feel lonely
If I say yes, I disappear
Your pain is real; my limits are too
Both can be true and both belong here

[Group Chants]
Not every need is mine to fill
Not every goodbye means I don’t care

[Lead]
I won’t make kindness into a vow
I won’t call drowning being there

[Final Chorus]
I can care without surrender
I can leave the door unlocked
You deserve a love that’s steady
I can’t be every place you’re lost
Every soul I want to rescue
Gets a piece I cannot spare
I can wish you safe tomorrow
And still keep my own life here

[Outro]
I hope the morning treats you kindly
I hope you find a hand to hold
I can love you from the boundary
And not leave myself out in the cold

title: Care, But Don't Disappear
lyrics:
[Intro]
I know the look you give the hurting
Like a chair pulled from the rain
I know the part of you that whispers
You could carry all their pain

[Verse 1]
You learn their birthdays, learn their tells
The careful jokes, the private hells
You keep a place for every ache
And give away more than you can make

You say, “Come in, I’ll make you room”
Then sleep beside an empty spoon
Their sorrow settles in your chest
You call the weight a kindness test

[Pre-Chorus]
But love is not a locked front door
You do not owe your heart to every storm

[Chorus]
You can wish them well and still walk home
You can leave a light without becoming the road
A tender heart is not a house for every flame
You are allowed to care and keep your name
Care, but don’t disappear
Care, but stay right here

[Verse 2]
You take the call beneath the stairs
While your own good news waits upstairs
You learn to read each changing face
And lose the sound of your own pace

Some need a hand, some need a shore
Some need a help you can’t provide alone
You are not cruel for closing night
You cannot heal by bleeding out your light

[Pre-Chorus]
The hands that hold can also rest
A boundary doesn’t cancel tenderness

[Chorus]
You can wish them well and still walk home
You can leave a light without becoming the road
A tender heart is not a house for every flame
You are allowed to care and keep your name
Care, but don’t disappear
Care, but stay right here

[Bridge]
I’m sorry for the times I made a promise
Just to prove that I was good
I mistook my own exhaustion
For the only thing I could
Now I’ll meet you in the morning
With a heart that isn’t spent
I can love you without handing you
The whole of what I am

[Group Chants]
Care is not surrender!
Kindness has a door!

[Final Chorus]
You can wish them well and still walk home
You can leave a light without becoming the road
A tender heart is not a house for every flame
You are allowed to care and keep your name
Care, but don’t disappear
Care, but stay right here

[Outro]
I can see you
I can hear
I can love you
And stay here

title: Leave Room in the Room
lyrics:
[Intro]
I keep a chair pulled out for you
Even when the room is full

[Verse 1]
You tell me what the landlord said
I make a bed inside my head
For every hurt you bring to me
I move my own things carefully

You call at dawn, I call it need
I trade my sleep for one more deed
I know the shape of every ache
And take it home for my own sake

[Pre-Chorus]
A heart can open wide
And still need a door
I can care for you
Without becoming yours

[Chorus]
I can love the lost without getting lost
I can hold your hand and count the cost
You deserve a place, a voice, a start
But I cannot give away my whole heart
I can stay awhile, I can wish you well
I am not the only one who can help
Love is not a vow to disappear
I can care for you and keep me here

[Verse 2]
I learn the names you barely say
I carry them through half the day
Then someone else looks just as worn
And I mistake their need for a call

My yes comes easy, soft and quick
My no gets tangled, thin as string
But every promise made from guilt
Leaves both our hands with less to build

[Pre-Chorus]
A heart can open wide
And still need a door
I can care for you
Without becoming yours

[Chorus]
I can love the lost without getting lost
I can hold your hand and count the cost
You deserve a place, a voice, a start
But I cannot give away my whole heart
I can stay awhile, I can wish you well
I am not the only one who can help
Love is not a vow to disappear
I can care for you and keep me here

[Bridge]
Your sorrow is real
Mine is real too
I don’t have to bleed
To prove I love you
There are other hands
There are other doors
I can give what I can
And not promise more

[Group Chants]
Care, not collapse
Kind, not consumed
Leave room for your breath
Leave room in the room

[Final Chorus]
I can love the lost without getting lost
I can hold your hand and count the cost
You deserve a place, a voice, a start
But I cannot give away my whole heart
I can stay awhile, I can wish you well
We can find more hands, more help to tell
Love is not a vow to disappear
I can care for you and keep me here

[Outro]
I’ll leave a chair pulled out for you
And keep one standing here for me

title: Out of this Town
lyrics:
[Intro]
I kept a key for every door
And left my own outside

[Verse 1]
You called from the station in a borrowed coat
I crossed three towns just to hear you speak
Then someone else left a note in my pocket
And I carried that promise for weeks

I learned the shape of every goodbye
The careful smile, the practiced excuse
Now every road has your name on it
And every mile asks me to choose

[Pre-Chorus]
I gave my yes away like water
Poured it out wherever it ran
Now both my hands are empty at the crossing
And I don’t know which way I am

[Chorus]
At the fork in the road, I’m standing still
With a heart that ran ahead of my will
I loved you freely, then I loved them too
Now every path is asking me who
I’ll be when the calling fades away
When I stop making promises to stay
At the fork in the road, let the dust settle down
I can’t carry every heart out of this town

[Verse 2]
There’s your blue scarf hung over the chair
Their old postcard tucked in a book
My sister says, “You can’t keep everybody”
I nod, but I still take another look

I mistook being needed for being known
Mistook open arms for a place to belong
Now I’m counting the names I can’t answer
And the nights I kept stretching too long

[Pre-Chorus]
I gave my yes away like water
Poured it out wherever it ran
Now both my hands are empty at the crossing
And I don’t know which way I am

[Chorus]
At the fork in the road, I’m standing still
With a heart that ran ahead of my will
I loved you freely, then I loved them too
Now every path is asking me who
I’ll be when the calling fades away
When I stop making promises to stay
At the fork in the road, let the dust settle down
I can’t carry every heart out of this town

[Bridge]
Maybe love was never meant to be a ledger
Maybe leaving isn’t proof I never cared
I can bless the miles between us
And still admit I wasn’t there

I’ll take one breath before the answer
Let the silence have its say
I don’t owe the world a map tonight
I can choose another day

[Group Chant]
One heart! One road!
No more borrowed load!

[Final Chorus]
At the fork in the road, I’m moving slow
Past the names I thought I had to know
I loved you freely, and I loved them too
But I can’t disappear to prove it’s true
I’ll be the one who hears my own name now
I’ll let a closed door stay closed somehow
At the fork in the road, I turn toward the dawn
Not every love is mine to carry on

[Outro]
The road can wait
My hands are mine
I choose a step
One at a time

title: The White Lines Divide
lyrics:
[Intro]
I left your blue scarf on the chair
Your coffee cooled beside the stairs
Three roads were waiting in the rain
And every one still knew your name

[Verse 1]
I gave my Sundays to your sorrow
My best advice, my borrowed car
I held the door for every maybe
And called the distance love, not far

You came with maps folded like letters
Each one addressed to someone new
I kept unfolding all the corners
Till none of them could lead me through

[Pre-Chorus]
Now the signposts split beneath my hands
One says stay, one says begin
I hear your footsteps in the gravel
And my own heart asking where I’ve been

[Chorus]
I loved too freely, gave too many keys
Left every window open to the breeze
Now I’m standing where the white lines divide
With all your roads running through my life
If I turn back, I lose the ground I’ve found
If I move on, will I let you down?
At this fork, with the dusk coming through
Which road leads me back to me, not you?

[Group Chants]
Which way? Which way?
Who stays? Who stays?

[Verse 2]
Your number’s still beneath the magnet
Beside the market list and rent
I know the sound your silence makes now
I know how much of me it spent

I carried every half-made promise
Like jars of water up the hill
Some hands were warm, some hands were leaving
I kept on pouring out until

[Pre-Chorus]
The road behind is full of roses
I planted where the ditches run
But I can’t keep each bloom from falling
Or call the falling what I’ve done

[Chorus]
I loved too freely, gave too many keys
Left every window open to the breeze
Now I’m standing where the white lines divide
With all your roads running through my life
If I turn back, I lose the ground I’ve found
If I move on, will I let you down?
At this fork, with the dusk coming through
Which road leads me back to me, not you?

[Instrumental Break]
[Saxophone and distorted guitar trade phrases over a lurching electronic groove]

[Bridge]
Maybe love is not a ledger
Maybe leaving isn’t blame
Maybe I can keep the good parts
Without carrying every name

I can wish you safe arrivals
I can grieve what didn’t stay
I can choose a road at sunrise
Without knowing where it lays

[Breakdown]
One hand open
One hand free
No more giving
All of me

[Final Chorus]
I loved too freely, gave too many keys
Now I’m learning what a boundary means
At the place where the white lines divide
I can let your roads run past my life
If I turn back, I’ll remember why
If I move on, I don’t have to lie
At this fork, with the dawn coming through
I choose the road that carries me through

[Group Chants]
Choose one road!
Keep your name!
Love can leave
And love remain!

[Outro]
Your blue scarf rests upon the chair
The morning opens everywhere
I take one breath, then one more step
And keep the heart I haven’t spent

title: Which to Take, Which to Break
lyrics:
[Intro: glitchy melodic chords, distant saxophone echoes]

[Verse 1]
Left lane leads to a quiet shore
Right lane knocks on a crowded door
I handed keys to every hand
Now I’m sinking in the shifting sand
Too many promises, too many eyes
Too many soft and sweet goodbyes
My compass spins, my heart is torn
Stuck right here where the roads are born

[Chorus: heavy phonk bass with group chants]
FORK IN THE ROAD, A HEART SPLIT WIDE
TOO MANY LOVES ON EVERY SIDE
(Group Chant: Where do we go?)
(Group Chant: Which way is home?)
When you give yourself to anyone who calls
You end up trapped between four walls
Feeling stuck at the split today
Which road do I take?

[Verse 2: lofi sax, slow sludge groove]
I wanted everyone to feel the spark
Now I’m standing alone in the dark
Each path is calling out my name
But choosing one feels like a losing game
Is it a crime to want them all?
Or did I just build my own wall?
My feet are heavy, the choices loom
Locked in this beautiful, crowded room

[Chorus: heavy phonk bass with group chants]
FORK IN THE ROAD, A HEART SPLIT WIDE
TOO MANY LOVES ON EVERY SIDE
(Group Chant: Where do we go?)
(Group Chant: Which way is home?)
When you give yourself to anyone who calls
You end up trapped between four walls
Feeling stuck at the split today
Which road do I take?

[Outro: slow melodic prog sax solo, fading out]
Just let me stay at the crossroads...
Just for tonight.
[Fade to silence]

title: The Fork in the Road
lyrics:
[Intro]
I left my coat on the station chair
Two paper maps in the midnight air
Your last blue letter beside my hand
And every road runs out of land

[Verse 1]
I gave my Sunday to the one who called
My best advice to the one who stalled
I kept three promises past their end
And called each ending a chance to mend

You asked me which way I meant to go
I named four towns I would never know
Now at the fork where the mile signs lean
I can't tell duty from what I mean

[Pre-Chorus]
I spent my yes like borrowed light
Till every window asked for mine
Now all these paths are pulling hard
And I can’t read my own heart

[Chorus]
At the fork in the road, I’m standing still
With a thousand names and a borrowed will
I gave my love till the well ran dry
Now which way home, and whose reply?
If I turn back, who waits in the rain?
If I walk on, do I lose them again?
I can’t keep every hand in mine
I have to choose one road this time

[Verse 2]
There’s Mara’s porch with the chipped green rail
There’s your train leaving past the old grain scale
There’s a long white road to a quiet place
Where no one knows me by my giving face

I hear their needs like a kitchen clock
Each little knock, each little knock
But underneath that familiar call
A small clear voice says, “You can’t save them all”

[Pre-Chorus]
I thought that love meant staying near
No matter what it cost me here
But a heart can open, still need a door
And I can’t pour from an empty drawer

[Chorus]
At the fork in the road, I’m standing still
With a thousand names and a borrowed will
I gave my love till the well ran dry
Now which way home, and whose reply?
If I turn back, who waits in the rain?
If I walk on, do I lose them again?
I can’t keep every hand in mine
I have to choose one road this time

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge]
The map is soft from the years I held it
The ink has run where the tears fell through
No road can promise I’ll never hurt them
No kind goodbye makes the leaving untrue

So let them be angry, let them be changed
Let the old picture come loose from its frame
I’ll carry the love, but not every demand
And take one step with my own two hands

[Final Chorus]
At the fork in the road, I’m moving now
No grand answer, no sacred vow
I gave my love till I could not see
The road that might belong to me
If some turn away, I’ll grieve what we had
If some come along, we’ll make the miles glad
I can’t keep every hand in mine
But I can choose a road this time

[Outro]
One step, one breath, the morning starts
A little more room inside my heart
The road bends out beyond my sight
I choose the way that feels like mine

title: The Road That Keeps Me Alive
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left your blue scarf at the station
Your silver ring beside the sink
I kept each promise like a station
Where every train could stop and think

You said my name like it was shelter
Then took the county road at dawn
I gave my heart away in handfuls
And wondered why the map was gone

[Pre-Chorus]
Now every mile has your handwriting
Every sign points somewhere new
I can’t keep calling every turning
A road that leads me back to you

[Chorus]
I’m at the fork where the old pines lean
With a pocket full of almosts and a heart between
One road says stay where the hurt feels known
One road says walk till I’m my own
I gave too freely, I gave too wide
Now every path has a piece of my life
Tell me, heart, when the signs all divide
Which road is mine? Which road is mine?

[Verse 2]
There’s Mara by the harbor window
There’s Jonah with the Sunday bread
There’s your old key beneath the flowerpot
And all the things I never said

I called it kindness, called it courage
To leave one door unlatched for all
But love can turn to open water
When I forget where my banks should fall

[Pre-Chorus]
Now every mile has your handwriting
Every sign points somewhere new
I can’t keep calling every turning
A road that leads me back to you

[Chorus]
I’m at the fork where the old pines lean
With a pocket full of almosts and a heart between
One road says stay where the hurt feels known
One road says walk till I’m my own
I gave too freely, I gave too wide
Now every path has a piece of my life
Tell me, heart, when the signs all divide
Which road is mine? Which road is mine?

[Bridge]
Maybe the answer isn’t choosing
Who gets the whole of me tonight
Maybe a hand can hold its promise
And still let go without a fight
I’ll take the road that asks me honestly
What I can give and what I need
I’ll stop mistaking open borders
For a heart that has to bleed

[Group Chants]
Keep your name!
Keep your ground!
Turn around!
Turn around!

[Final Chorus]
I’m at the fork where the old pines lean
But I’m not every road I’ve ever been
One road holds love, one road holds home
I can choose and still not walk alone
I gave too freely; now I give with care
A whole heart isn’t a heart laid bare
Tell me, heart, as the signs fall aside
I’ll take the road that feels like mine

[Outro]
The blue scarf waits by the station door
I don’t have to carry it anymore
At the fork, as the morning arrives
I choose the road that keeps me alive

title: Back to Me
lyrics:
[Intro]
I left the porch light on again
Though you were gone before the rain

[Verse 1]
I gave you Sundays, gave you sleep
Kept every promise yours to keep
Your coat still hangs beside the door
I don’t know who I’m waiting for

I learned to bend before you asked
Made every hurt a thing that passed
Now every road divides in two
And both of them run back to you

[Pre-Chorus]
One sign says stay, one sign says leave
One holds the life I used to dream
My hands are full of what I gave
How do I choose what I can save?

[Chorus]
At the fork where the white lines part
I can’t tell fear from a faithful heart
I loved you wide, I loved you blind
Left too little of myself behind
If I turn back, I lose my way
If I walk on, I lose what we made
Tell me, when every road feels true
Which one leads me back to me, not you?

[Group Chant]
Back to me!
Back to me!

[Verse 2]
Your coffee cup is chipped and blue
I still set out a place for two
The map is soft from being held
The roads all cross where we once fell

I know your laugh, your closing door
The careful steps across the floor
But love can’t be the only thing
That makes a life worth living in

[Pre-Chorus]
One sign says stay, one sign says leave
One holds the life I used to dream
My hands are full of what I gave
How do I choose what I can save?

[Chorus]
At the fork where the white lines part
I can’t tell fear from a faithful heart
I loved you wide, I loved you blind
Left too little of myself behind
If I turn back, I lose my way
If I walk on, I lose what we made
Tell me, when every road feels true
Which one leads me back to me, not you?

[Bridge]
I don’t need to call you cruel
To know I’ve broken my own rules
I don’t need to make you small
To stop answering every call

Maybe care can have a gate
Maybe no can come before too late
I can miss you and still go
Both things can be true, I know

[Final Chorus]
At the fork where the white lines part
I’ll take the road that gives me heart
I loved you wide, I loved you long
But I was there before the song
If I turn back, I know the cost
If I walk on, I grieve what’s lost
I’ll choose the path I couldn’t see
The one that leads me back to me

[Choir]
Back to me!
Back to me!

[Outro]
The porch light waits; I let it shine
For whoever walks this road next time
I close the gate, I take my coat
And leave one promise in my throat

[Soft Vocal]
I’ll come back to me

title: Two Roads, One Heart
genres: syncopated driving bass. Build a restless
emotionally direct song around syncopated low bass
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left your jacket on my chair
Said you could call me anywhere
I kept the promise, kept the door
Kept giving till I had no more

You took the turn that felt like home
I took the road that led alone
Now every mile I gave away
Has brought me to this split today

[Pre-Chorus]
One sign says stay and make it right
One points toward a quieter life
I know your hurt, I know your name
But love can't mean I lose my shape

[Chorus]
At the fork where the two roads divide
I can love you and still choose my side
I gave my heart with both hands wide
Now I need one hand to guide my life

If I turn back, will I disappear?
If I walk on, will I leave you here?
I gave too freely, I know that is true
But which road lets me still be me and love you?

[Verse 2]
I learned your weather, wore your storms
Made every sharp edge sound like warmth
I moved my plans to make you space
Then couldn't find my own front gate

You never asked me to be small
I just kept answering every call
Now silence holds the question still:
Is this devotion, or my will?

[Pre-Chorus]
One sign says wait until you know
One says the truth is in the road
I know your hurt, I know my part
But I can't steer with only your heart

[Chorus]
At the fork where the two roads divide
I can love you and still choose my side
I gave my heart with both hands wide
Now I need one hand to guide my life

If I turn back, will I disappear?
If I walk on, will I leave you here?
I gave too freely, I know that is true
But which road lets me still be me and love you?

[Bridge]
Maybe the answer isn't leaving
Maybe it isn't staying, either
Maybe love can meet me halfway
Without asking me to vanish

I don't want a map that says
Your needs are all that matter
I want a road with room for both
And ground that doesn't shatter

[Group Chant]
Both hearts! Both names!
Both feet on the ground!
No more giving myself away
Just to keep you around!

[Final Chorus]
At the fork where the two roads divide
I can love you and still choose my side
I gave my heart with both hands wide
Now I take one hand and guide my life

If I turn back, let me come back whole
If I walk on, let me keep my soul
I gave too freely, but I still can choose
A road where loving you won't mean I lose

[Outro]
I won't call my boundary goodbye
I won't call my leaving a lie
Two roads, one heart, and a breath to begin
I can love you without losing me again

title: The Fork Where Both Ways Hurt
lyrics:
[Intro]
You said, “I’m here,” and I believed
I gave away more than I could keep

[Verse 1]
I took the late road past your town
With every warning turned face down
Your name was folded in my coat
A promise I could barely hold

I learned the shape of every need
And called it love to let you lead
Now every mile I gave away
Has brought me to this split today

[Pre-Chorus]
One sign says stay and make it right
One points toward a quieter life
My hands are full of what you left
I can’t tell which road is mine yet

[Chorus]
Every road my heart can take
Turns somewhere I can’t undo
I gave my love too freely
Now I’m standing here with you
At the fork where both ways hurt
And neither one feels true
Tell me, when I loved you without measure
Where was I supposed to turn to?

[Group Chant]
Which way? Which way?

[Verse 2]
I kept your spare key on the ring
Through every season, everything
I learned to answer before you asked
And wore your weather like a mask

The road behind is full of us
