Small good days and broken trust
Ahead, the blank signs catch the rain
I want my name back all the same

[Pre-Chorus]
One sign says wait, the years will mend
One says don’t make this hurt again
I’m tired of choosing what you need
Before I hear my own heartbeat

[Chorus]
Every road my heart can take
Turns somewhere I can’t undo
I gave my love too freely
Now I’m standing here with you
At the fork where both ways hurt
And neither one feels true
Tell me, when I loved you without measure
Where was I supposed to turn to?

[Bridge]
Maybe love is not a debt
I have to pay with what is left
Maybe leaving isn’t proof
That every tender thing was false

I can miss you and still go
I can love you, say it slow
But if I keep on losing me
There’ll be no one left to choose

[Group Chant]
Choose yourself! Choose yourself!

[Final Chorus]
Every road my heart can take
May lead somewhere I can’t yet see
I gave my love too freely
Now I’m learning what is mine to keep
At the fork where both ways hurt
I will take the road that lets me breathe
I can wish you well and still remember
That my heart belongs to me

[Outro]
The signs are worn, the dawn is pale
I take one step beyond the trail
No map can tell me what comes through
But this next road belongs to me

title: Does the Love Story End
lyrics:
[Intro]
Some names are written in pencil
Some stay beneath the skin

[Verse 1]
You found me counting winter mornings
With your coat across my chair
You held the door through all my talking
Like there was time enough to spare
You taught my hands to unclench slowly
Left the kettle by the stove
I thought a heart could learn its measure
By the kindness that it knows

[Pre-Chorus]
Then another came like summer
With a key to every room
I mistook the rush for promise
And the promise for a truth

[Chorus]
Does the love story ever end?
Or does it change its face again?
One love mends, one love enthralls
One takes the pieces, one takes it all
I’ve been held, I’ve been undone
I’ve asked the dark what I’ve become
If every ending turns a page
Does love grow quiet, or just change?

[Verse 2]
You could make a crowded table
Feel like it was built for two
Then you learned which words would move me
And kept each one to use
I gave you every second chance
Till none were left to spend
Some goodbyes arrive as breathing
After begging has to end

[Pre-Chorus]
Now I check the locks more gently
Now I trust the pause I feel
Not every ache is asking for you
Not every wound is meant to heal

[Chorus]
Does the love story ever end?
Or does it change its face again?
One love mends, one love enthralls
One takes the pieces, one takes it all
I’ve been held, I’ve been undone
I’ve asked the dark what I’ve become
If every ending turns a page
Does love grow quiet, or just change?

[Bridge]
Maybe love is not one answer
Maybe it is many rooms
Some with sunlight on the table
Some we leave before they bloom
I can miss you without returning
I can grieve what wasn’t true
I can keep the parts that taught me
And still make a life that’s new

[Final Chorus]
Does the love story ever end?
Or do we learn to begin again?
One love mends, one love enthralls
One takes the pieces, one breaks the walls
I’ve been held, I’ve been undone
But I am more than what I’ve become
If every ending turns a page
I’ll write the next one at my pace

[Outro]
Does the story end?
I don’t know yet
But I am here
And I am not finished

title: Calling From Inside of Me
lyrics:
[Intro]
One cup split on the kitchen tile
I count the pieces, lose the count

[Verse 1]
You ask me where I’m going tonight
I say “home,” then turn toward the door
One part of me wants your hand
One part can’t take this pull anymore

I keep your note inside my coat
The fold has worn a paper seam
I read the same four crooked words
Then choose a different one to mean

[Pre-Chorus]
Every piece has got a compass
Every needle turns away
I can hear them arguing softly
Over what I should obey

[Chorus]
My heart broke into a hundred pieces
Each one pulling on a different thread
One says stay here, one says leave me
One keeps every tender word you said
I’m held in every direction
I can’t make the pieces agree
If you ask which one is really me
They’re all still calling from inside of me

[Verse 2]
Your blue scarf hangs behind the door
The sleeve still carries cedar soap
I almost call you by your name
Then swallow half the sound of hope

The bus rolls past the corner store
Where we split oranges in the cold
I want the life we almost had
And want the right to let it go

[Pre-Chorus]
Every piece keeps its own weather
Every shard remembers rain
I am tired of making one voice
Pretend it can explain the pain

[Chorus]
My heart broke into a hundred pieces
Each one pulling on a different thread
One says stay here, one says leave me
One keeps every tender word you said
I’m held in every direction
I can’t make the pieces agree
If you ask which one is really me
They’re all still calling from inside of me

[Bridge]
I won’t glue them into silence
I won’t tell them not to ache
Let the room hear all their answers
Let the old shape finally break

Some want morning at the window
Some want one more hour with you
Some want nothing but a quiet table
And a place to set the truth

[Choir]
All of me
All at once

[Final Chorus]
My heart broke into a hundred pieces
Each one pulling, none erased
One says stay here, one says leave me
One still reaches for your face
I am more than one direction
More than what I couldn’t keep
I can carry every answer
And still choose the road beneath my feet

[Outro]
The cup is gone; the floor is clean
I keep the note, but let it be
Every piece still turns within me
And none of them gets all of me

title: A Hundred Directions
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You pull me east, you call me home
A dozen hands around one bone
I try to stand where all roads meet
But every road drags at my feet

One piece says stay, one says run
One counts the damage, one says done
I hold the shards against my chest
And none of them can point me west

[Pre-Chorus]
You ask me which way I belong
I’m split between the right and wrong
Each little piece keeps calling out
A different name, a different doubt

[Chorus]
My heart broke into a hundred directions
Every fragment knows a different way
You pull me close, the pieces pull against you
I want to stay, I want to get away
If you can hold me without making me whole
I might find a place to lay them down
My heart broke into a hundred directions
And every road keeps turning me around

[Verse 2]
There’s one of me that keeps your key
One wants the door to set us free
One saves the note you never sent
One keeps the hours that we spent

I hear your voice in every room
A different answer, different tune
I gather what I can’t repair
Then lose another piece somewhere

[Pre-Chorus]
You ask me which way I belong
I’m split between the right and wrong
Each little piece keeps calling out
A different name, a different doubt

[Chorus]
My heart broke into a hundred directions
Every fragment knows a different way
You pull me close, the pieces pull against you
I want to stay, I want to get away
If you can hold me without making me whole
I might find a place to lay them down
My heart broke into a hundred directions
And every road keeps turning me around

[Bridge]
Don’t make a map from what is missing
Don’t call the fracture something clean
I’m not a puzzle for your keeping
I’m all the roads that run through me

[Breakdown]
One says go
One says wait
One says love
One says late

[Final Chorus]
My heart broke into a hundred directions
Every fragment knows a different way
You pull me close, the pieces pull against you
I want to stay, I want to get away
If you can hold me without making me whole
I might find a place to lay them down
My heart broke into a hundred directions
But I can choose where I turn now

[Outro]
I can choose where I turn now
Piece by piece, I turn somehow

title: Fractured by Love
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I learn the shape of every room
The names beside the coat hooks
You laugh about your cracked blue mug
I keep the way your whole face looks

At every stop, a different thread
A different kind of tender
I love the way you bite your lip
The way you make December warmer

[Pre-Chorus]
I never meant to make a promise
With every open hand
But every heart I hold is precious
And I don’t know where to stand

[Chorus]
I’m falling in love everywhere I go
In a hundred ways that only you could know
Each one a card, each one a home
Stacked so high on hands that shake below
If one slips, all the careful rooms come down
And every heart I love is in the house
I want to keep you safe, I want to let you go
I’m fractured by the love I can’t make one

[Verse 2]
You save the seat beside the window
She sends the songs at closing time
He tells me things he’s never said
And you bring peaches from the roadside stand

No love is lesser, none a copy
Each has its own small constellation
But I can’t swear the cards won’t scatter
When truth arrives without invitation

[Pre-Chorus]
I never meant to make a promise
With every open hand
But every heart I hold is precious
And I don’t know where to stand

[Chorus]
I’m falling in love everywhere I go
In a hundred ways that only you could know
Each one a card, each one a home
Stacked so high on hands that shake below
If one slips, all the careful rooms come down
And every heart I love is in the house
I want to keep you safe, I want to let you go
I’m fractured by the love I can’t make one

[Bridge]
I can hear the paper bending
At the quietest goodbye
I can see the whole room leaning
Though nobody asks me why

I don’t want to make you a secret
I don’t want to make you compete
I just wish my hands were steadier
When the cards begin to leave

[Breakdown]
One for your kindness
One for her fire
One for the truth
That I can’t retire

[Final Chorus]
I’m falling in love everywhere I go
In a hundred ways that only you could know
Each one a card, each one a home
Built from every promise I don’t know how to hold
If one slips, all the careful rooms come down
And every heart I love can feel the ground
I want to keep you safe, I want to tell the truth
I’m fractured, but my love for you is true

[Outro]
Not one of you was ever less
Not one of you was just a phase
I love you each in your own language
And I’m afraid of what that makes

title: We’re More
lyrics:
[Intro]
When the kettle starts to sing
Leave a place beside the sink

[Verse 1]
You came in late with rain on your sleeve
I moved the chair; you didn’t have to explain
The whole long day had sharpened your words
I let them pass; we started again

At the corner shop, the queue stood still
A tired cashier dropped the change
We waited while she counted twice
Small mercies make a little space

[Pre-Chorus]
We don’t know what a stranger carries
Or what it took to make them stay
So give a little room for breathing
And let a softer answer have its say

[Chorus]
Make room at the table
Make room in your heart
We’re more than the worst thing
We did in the dark
Hold out a hand when the hard words are done
A little more mercy can turn us toward one
Make room at the table
Let kindness begin

[Verse 2]
You kept my coat when I was sure
I’d never cross your door again
I brought your book back, spine repaired
We found the page and tried as friends

We won’t agree on every road
Or call each other right each time
But I can hear the fear beneath
And you can listen past my pride

[Pre-Chorus]
We don’t know what a stranger carries
Or what it took to make them stay
So give a little room for breathing
And let a softer answer have its say

[Chorus]
Make room at the table
Make room in your heart
We’re more than the worst thing
We did in the dark
Hold out a hand when the hard words are done
A little more mercy can turn us toward one
Make room at the table
Let kindness begin

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge]
Forgiving isn’t saying it was nothing
It’s setting down the stone you’ve held so long
It’s drawing clear lines, keeping your own name
And leaving open one small path beyond

You can be gentle and still say no
You can be brave and change your mind
There’s room for both of us to grow
There’s more than one way to be kind

[Final Chorus]
Make room at the table
Make room in your heart
We’re more than the worst thing
We did in the dark
Hold out a hand when the hard words are done
A little more mercy can turn us toward one
Make room at the table
Let kindness begin

[Outro]
If tomorrow finds us different
Leave the chair pulled out again
Make room at the table
Let kindness begin

title: You Make Room
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You held the elevator with your coffee going cold
Made room for the new kid carrying a box of files
You showed her where the spare keys hang beside the old coat
She learned the names, then found a way to make the whole place smile

[Pre-Chorus]
A little trust can travel farther than a favor asked
One open hand can turn a locked door into a path

[Chorus]
Give a little good, watch the good come round
One small yes can lift somebody off the ground
When you make a place for another to begin
They remember how it felt, and they invite you in
Pass the chance along, let the circle grow
Every door you hold becomes a door you know

[Verse 2]
You stayed to walk the intern through the numbers on the page
She caught the flaw that would've cost the team a month
At Friday's table, she saved you a seat beside the sage
By Monday, both your names were on the project up front

[Pre-Chorus]
No grand design, just showing up and doing what you can
A steady kind of generosity makes allies where it lands

[Chorus]
Give a little good, watch the good come round
One small yes can lift somebody off the ground
When you make a place for another to begin
They remember how it felt, and they invite you in
Pass the chance along, let the circle grow
Every door you hold becomes a door you know

[Bridge]
Not a bargain, not a tally on a page
Just the way we keep each other from getting turned away
You lend your name, you share the map, you say, “Come sit with us”
And later, when your hands are full, they make a little room

[Final Chorus]
Give a little good, watch the good come round
One small yes can lift a whole team off the ground
When you make a place for another to begin
They remember how it felt, and they invite you in
Pass the chance along, let the circle grow
Every door you hold becomes a door you know
Give a little good—let it travel, let it spread
A thousand new beginnings from the kind words that you said

[Outro]
You make room, they make room
That’s how a way gets made
You make room, they make room
And nobody walks alone

title: Pass It On
lyrics:
[Intro: lone piano and distant voices]
A paper cup rolls by the station stairs
You stop to catch it; someone sees you there
A small held door, a name remembered right
Can change the weather in a stranger's night

[Verse 1]
You saved a seat beside the window
For the nurse whose shift ran late
She came back with a warm introduction
To the shop that needed help that day
One open hand became a doorway
One kind word became a key
A chance passed on from you to someone
Came back wider than it used to be

[Pre-Chorus]
No grand design, no perfect plan
Just room made by a human hand
And every time you make room, another can

[Chorus]
Pass it on, pass it on
Let a little good keep moving
Give somebody ground to stand on
Watch a closed door start improving
One bright chance becomes two more
Kindness turns the key again
When you lift somebody forward
They can lift somebody then

[Verse 2: jagged riff, quick phrasing]
You tell the new kid, “Take your time here”
You show the trick they missed last week
They make a place for one more voice now
And ask the shy one what they think
A ride across town, a clear reference
A second look at someone’s work
These aren’t favors lost to distance
They’re seeds that travel through the dirt

[Pre-Chorus]
A little trust can change the scale
A chance to try, a softer fail
A hand that helps another hand set sail

[Chorus]
Pass it on, pass it on
Let a little good keep moving
Give somebody ground to stand on
Watch a closed door start improving
One bright chance becomes two more
Kindness turns the key again
When you lift somebody forward
They can lift somebody then

[Instrumental: intricate keyboard figure, angular guitars, half-time electronic drop]

[Bridge: piano and strings]
Maybe you never learn the ending
Of the help you gave away
Maybe years from now a stranger
Gets a chance because you stayed
No tally kept, no ribbon waiting
Just a life made less alone
And somewhere down the turning road
Your kindness finds its way back home

[Build]
A seat becomes a welcome
A welcome makes a team
A team gives someone footing
To attempt a larger dream

[Final Chorus: key change, choir and full-band drop]
Pass it on, pass it on
Let a little good keep moving
Give somebody ground to stand on
Watch a closed door start improving
One bright chance becomes two more
Every open hand can send
A better path through one small moment
Round the bend and round again

[Outro: piano, soft choir]
You made room
They made room
Now there’s room for someone new
Pass it on
Pass it on
Let the next good thing begin

title: Split Heart
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left your laugh in Lisbon rain
Your Sunday coat on a Tokyo train
A chipped blue cup in my kitchen sink
And half your letters I still can’t bring

I keep one hand on the map you drew
With coffee rings and a crooked Peru
Each little mark says where we’ve been
Each empty mile lets the pieces in

[Pre-Chorus]
I thought a heart was one locked room
One front door and one way through
Now every border pulls a thread
From all the places we called home instead

[Chorus]
My heart is split in pieces around the world
One part where the harbor ropes are curled
One part beneath that red Madrid sun
One part still asking where you’ve gone
And if I cross those miles, will I find
The little parts I left behind?
My heart is split in pieces around the world
Still beating wherever you are

[Verse 2]
There’s your green scarf in a Montreal drawer
A ticket stub by the kitchen door
A borrowed book with your note inside
That says, “Take the long way, enjoy the ride”

I pass the bakery near the old square
The woman there still thinks you’re somewhere
I nod like I know what she means by “soon”
Then ride home under a paper moon

[Pre-Chorus]
I thought goodbye could close a gate
And leave the rest to time and fate
But every town keeps one small thing
A key, a joke, the way you’d sing

[Chorus]
My heart is split in pieces around the world
One part where the harbor ropes are curled
One part beneath that red Madrid sun
One part still asking where you’ve gone
And if I cross those miles, will I find
The little parts I left behind?
My heart is split in pieces around the world
Still beating wherever you are

[Bridge]
Maybe the map was never meant
To show the way we’d come undone
Maybe each piece became a room
With its own weather, its own sun

I can’t collect the days we lost
Or fold the distance small
But when I hear your name in passing
I still feel every wall fall

[Final Chorus]
My heart is split in pieces around the world
One part where the harbor ropes are curled
One part beneath that red Madrid sun
One part still asking where you’ve gone
And even if I never find
The little parts I left behind
My heart is split in pieces around the world
Still beating wherever you are

[Outro]
Lisbon rain, Tokyo train
Your green scarf, your crooked name
A thousand miles, a thousand starts
You left your laugh in all my parts

title: Disagree and Sit Down
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You said the river starts up north
I thought it rose behind the mill
We stood there drawing different maps
And neither one was standing still

I almost brought my best argument
All polished up and wrapped in facts
Then asked you what you’d seen that day
And watched the whole conversation change

[Pre-Chorus]
I don’t have to win the room
To leave a little space to bloom

[Chorus]
We can disagree and still sit down
Let your reasons find their way around
I’ll ask what brought you to that view
And listen long enough to learn what’s true for you
No need to pull your thinking through my door
I’m curious; I don’t need to score
And when the air is easy, you might ask me too
What I see from where I’m standing, what I’ve come to

[Verse 2]
You said the old bridge should come down
I said it held our town together
You told me where the flood ran high
I told you how we fixed it after

A story has a second side
When someone lets the first one land
I found a reason in your words
I hadn’t seen from where I stand

[Pre-Chorus]
I don’t have to win the room
To leave a little space to bloom

[Chorus]
We can disagree and still sit down
Let your reasons find their way around
I’ll ask what brought you to that view
And listen long enough to learn what’s true for you
No need to pull your thinking through my door
I’m curious; I don’t need to score
And when the air is easy, you might ask me too
What I see from where I’m standing, what I’ve come to

[Bridge]
Maybe understanding isn’t surrender
Maybe questions aren’t a clever disguise
I can hold my own thought without a hammer
You can keep yours while I look through your eyes

[Final Chorus]
We can disagree and still sit down
Let your reasons find their way around
I’ll ask what brought you to that view
And listen long enough to learn what’s true for you
No need to pull your thinking through my door
I’m curious; I don’t need to score
And if you wonder what I’m thinking, I’ll tell you true
Not to change your mind, just to share my view

[Outro]
We can leave with our minds still our own
And a little more known than before

title: Let the Kind Part Rise
lyrics:
[Intro: sparse and tense]
There are two hands on the wheel inside me.
One grips hard.
One keeps reaching for the brake.

[Verse 1]
You keep a ledger by the bed,
You count the careless things I said.
You call a bruise a lesson learned,
You feed the match and watch it burn.

But there’s a voice beneath your jaw,
That still can stop before the fall.
It knows the name of every hurt,
And won’t make somebody else its dirt.

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the dark can sound like sense,
A clean excuse, a locked defense.
But I can choose what gets my breath—
The hand that mends, not one that wrecks.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
LET THE KIND PART RISE!
LET IT TAKE THE ROOM!
Not the fist, not the verdict,
Not the old familiar wound!
When the cruel voice calls me righteous,
When it begs me to divide—
LET THE KIND PART RISE!
I can choose which one survives!

[Verse 2]
You know the sentence that will sting,
The perfect little sharpened thing.
You set it ready on my tongue,
Then swear the damage can’t be undone.

I see your fear beneath the sneer,
The younger self you kept in here.
I won’t pretend you’re not in pain;
I just won’t pass it on again.

[Pre-Chorus]
I hear the dark rehearse its case,
A borrowed law, a hard-set face.
I can be honest, still be kind;
I don’t have to leave you behind.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
LET THE KIND PART RISE!
LET IT TAKE THE ROOM!
Not the fist, not the verdict,
Not the old familiar wound!
When the cruel voice calls me righteous,
When it begs me to divide—
LET THE KIND PART RISE!
I can choose which one survives!

[Bridge: exposed, accusatory spoken delivery]
You were trying to keep me safe.
I know.
You learned that softness got punished.
I know.
But protection that keeps hurting people
is just fear with a better name.
You don’t get to drive us there again.

[Build]
Take one breath.
Name the feeling.
Keep your hands open.
Make a different ending.

[Final Chorus: full-force gang vocals]
LET THE KIND PART RISE!
LET IT TAKE THE ROOM!
Not the fist, not the verdict,
Not the old familiar wound!
When the cruel voice calls me righteous,
I will hear it, not comply—
LET THE KIND PART RISE!
I can choose which one survives!

[Outro]
You’re still here.
I’m still here.
We can do this differently.

title: Kinder Soil
lyrics:
[Intro]
[jagged palm-muted guitar riffs over electronic glitch beats]
[Spoken: accusatory]
You guard the borders of your minds like a vault.
Thinking conformity buys stability.
How blind.

[Verse 1]
You want a ledger that’s clean and straight
So you lock the different outside the gate
You force the minds to match the mold
Then wonder why the market's cold
A monoculture in the soil
Yields nothing but exhausted toil
When everyone must think the same
You kill the spark, you stall the game

[Pre-Chorus]
[synth choir pads rise]
But talent doesn't check your tidy rules
It goes where it can find the tools
A closed door is a frozen hand
Prosperity needs a wider land

[Chorus: explosive drop, shouted gang vocals]
KINDER SOIL, STRONGER YIELD!
THE OPEN MIND IS THE ENGINE SHIELD!
When you crush the heart to save the dime
You build a tomb before your time!
TOLERANCE IS THE REAL CAPITAL!
BREAK THE WALLS AND WATCH IT GROW!

[Verse 2]
[halftime trap drums, detuned lead synth]
[Spoken: sharp, bitter]
Innovation isn't born on assembly lines.
It thrives in the friction of different lives.
The safest rooms are always the quietest.
And the quietest rooms produce nothing at all.

[Pre-Chorus]
[chiming delay guitar, fretless bass runs]
A fearful nation hoards its bread
But a trusting culture builds instead
You buy the chains, you pay the cost
Think of the brilliant minds you lost

[Chorus: explosive drop, shouted gang vocals]
KINDER SOIL, STRONGER YIELD!
THE OPEN MIND IS THE ENGINE SHIELD!
When you crush the heart to save the dime
You build a tomb before your time!
TOLERANCE IS THE REAL CAPITAL!
BREAK THE WALLS AND WATCH IT GROW!

[Outro]
[guitars feedback, drum glitching out to a halt]
[Spoken: dry, direct]
A stronger economy isn't built on fear.
It's built on room.
Room for everyone to exist.
Do the math.
[Final heavy crash]

title: Let The Talent In!
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken, close and pointed]
They call the welcome sign a cost.
Then count the shops that never opened.

[Verse 1: spoken rhythmic delivery]
A name crossed out before the interview
A locked front door with a polished view
A bright idea left outside the room
A town that calls that waste “the rules”

You keep the gate; you lose the hands
The cooks, the coders, the repair plans
The nurse who’d stay, the firm that’d grow
All sent away before they show

[Pre-Chorus]
You want a market built to last?
Make room for more than one forecast.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
OPEN THE DOOR—LET THE TALENT IN!
MORE PEOPLE WORK, MORE IDEAS BEGIN!
WHEN EVERYONE CAN BUILD AND BUY,
THE WHOLE TOWN’S NUMBERS CLIMB!

[Verse 2]
A safe first job, a fair wage earned
A corner store where cash returns
A family stays, the rent gets paid
New customers fill the lunch-hour trade

No wasted years behind a wall
No useful skill refused at all
A wider table, stronger hands
More makers shaping local plans

[Pre-Chorus]
You want a market built to last?
Make room for more than one forecast.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
OPEN THE DOOR—LET THE TALENT IN!
MORE PEOPLE WORK, MORE IDEAS BEGIN!
WHEN EVERYONE CAN BUILD AND BUY,
THE WHOLE TOWN’S NUMBERS CLIMB!

[Bridge: stripped, accusatory spoken vocals]
Kindness isn’t charity
when the work is there to do.
It’s a fair shot at the paycheck,
a fair shot at the breakthrough.

A worker with a steady shift
spends nearby, keeps neighbors paid.
A business built on open doors
has stronger ground beneath its trade.

[Build]
Count the customers!
Count the skills!
Count the firms that meet their bills!

[Final Chorus: explosive gang vocals]
OPEN THE DOOR—LET THE TALENT IN!
MORE PEOPLE WORK, MORE IDEAS BEGIN!
WHEN EVERYONE CAN BUILD AND BUY,
THE WHOLE TOWN’S NUMBERS CLIMB!

NO ONE’S FUTURE THROWN AWAY!
NO GOOD IDEAS KEPT AT BAY!
FAIRER GROUND, A STRONGER TOWN—
THAT’S HOW WE GROW, THAT’S HOW WE RISE!

[Outro: spoken]
A kinder country isn’t weaker.
It’s leaving less value on the table.

title: Be The Kindness You Believe
lyrics:
[Intro: single piano chord, distant room tone]
[Spoken]
They taught us how to win the room.
He showed us how to make one safe.

[Verse 1]
You learned the names the others missed,
The kid who ate alone at lunch,
The neighbor hauling groceries in,
The tired parent out of touch.
You sat down low, you met their eyes,
You gave a hurting heart its time.
No grand parade, no perfect speech—
Just kindness practiced within reach.

[Pre-Chorus]
So when the easy answer says,
“Walk on, you don’t owe them a thing,”
Remember how a gentle word
Can change the shape of everything.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
BE THE KINDNESS YOU BELIEVE!
Make a place where all can breathe!
Say their name, stay when it’s hard,
Let a little care go far!
No one small, no one unseen—
Make the world a little more kind!

[Verse 2]
You hold the door, you hear them out,
You ask what’s wrong and wait awhile.
You teach the room that strength can bend,
That brave can sound like “I’m your friend.”
You don’t need cameras, praise, or proof,
A steady hand can tell the truth.
The lesson lives in what you do
When no one’s keeping score of you.

[Pre-Chorus]
And when the noise gets sharp and fast,
When anger wants to take the lead,
Choose the patient, honest thing.
Be the person you would need.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
BE THE KINDNESS YOU BELIEVE!
Make a place where all can breathe!
Say their name, stay when it’s hard,
Let a little care go far!
No one small, no one unseen—
Make the world a little more kind!

[Bridge: piano and strings]
You can’t mend every hurt tonight,
You can’t make every promise true.
But you can sit beside one person
And let them know they’re not alone with you.
A child remembers who looked up.
A stranger remembers who stayed.
The smallest good you do with love
Can outlast the loudest thing you say.

[Final Chorus: full band, gang vocals]
BE THE KINDNESS YOU BELIEVE!
Make a place where all can breathe!
Say their name, stay when it’s hard,
Let a little care go far!
No one small, no one unseen—
Take that lesson into the street!
BE THE KINDNESS YOU BELIEVE!
Make the world a little more kind!

[Outro: piano and soft choir]
[Soft Vocal]
One small kindness, freely given.
[Choir]
Make a place where all can breathe.
[Lead]
Let them know they matter here.

title: The Neighbor Who Stays
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken]
A cardigan is not a costume.
It’s a promise you make with your hands.

[Verse 1]
You learned the names of every child
You kept your temper soft, your questions mild
A chair pulled close, a zipper zipped
A little patience in your fingertips
You didn’t preach from some high shelf
You showed us how to tend ourselves
One button, one apology
One small act of decency

[Pre-Chorus]
When the room says, “Hurry up and harden,”
You make a different choice
You meet the hurt without a weapon
You answer anger with your voice

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
BE THE NEIGHBOR WHO STAYS
WHEN THE EASY ONES LEAVE
MAKE A PLACE AT THE TABLE
MAKE IT SAFE TO BELIEVE
No grand speech, no borrowed crown
Just look a frightened person in the eye
And let them know they matter now

[Verse 2]
You show a child the stitches in a shoe
The patient work that makes a worn thing new
You let the silence have its honest size
You never told us not to cry
And when the world was sharp and loud
You didn’t need to beat the crowd
You held a steady, human line:
Your feelings matter. So do mine.

[Pre-Chorus]
No medal for the kindest gesture
No camera has to see
A gentle word can change the weather
Inside a family

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
BE THE NEIGHBOR WHO STAYS
WHEN THE EASY ONES LEAVE
MAKE A PLACE AT THE TABLE
MAKE IT SAFE TO BELIEVE
No grand speech, no borrowed crown
Just look a frightened person in the eye
And let them know they matter now

[Bridge: spoken, stripped back]
Not every child gets a quiet room.
Not every hurt can be mended by one sentence.
But you can stop, listen, learn their name.
You can refuse to pass the hurt along.

[Build]
One honest question!
One open door!
One more chair beside the poor!
One patient hand! One voice that says—
You don’t have to earn your place!

[Final Chorus: explosive gang vocals]
BE THE NEIGHBOR WHO STAYS
WHEN THE EASY ONES LEAVE
MAKE A PLACE AT THE TABLE
MAKE IT SAFE TO BELIEVE
No grand speech, no borrowed crown
A thousand little mercies, day by day
Can turn a whole wide world around

[Outro: spoken]
The neighborhood begins
where you decide to care.

title: Be The Kindness You Ask For
lyrics:
[Intro: single piano chord, distant room tone]

[Spoken]
A small thing counts.
A name remembered.
A chair pulled close.

[Verse 1]
You held the door when rain came down
You learned the new kid’s name in town
You let the angry sentence pass
And asked what hurt beneath the mask

No medal pinned, no cameras near
Just one more person met with care
A steady hand, a patient face
A little room for someone’s place

[Pre-Chorus]
They call it soft as if that means
It cannot stand against the mean
But every day, by what we do
We teach the world what people can do

[Chorus: explosive gang vocals]
BE THE KINDNESS YOU ASK FOR
MAKE A LITTLE SPACE
LOOK THE LONELY IN THE EYE
AND MEET THEM FACE TO FACE

You don’t need a grand parade
You don’t need to save the whole
Just choose the decent thing again
And make it part of who you are

[Gang Vocals]
One small act!
One more day!

[Verse 2]
You keep your promise when it’s hard
You own the bruise your words have caused
You tell the truth without a blade
You stand beside the one betrayed

You let a child ask one more why
You don’t make tenderness a lie
And when the room says, “Look away,”
You stay, and help, and choose to stay

[Pre-Chorus]
A gentle voice is not a crown
It’s how we lift each other up
A neighbor’s worth is not a test
The measure is the care we give

[Chorus]
BE THE KINDNESS YOU ASK FOR
MAKE A LITTLE SPACE
LOOK THE LONELY IN THE EYE
AND MEET THEM FACE TO FACE

You don’t need a grand parade
You don’t need to save the whole
Just choose the decent thing again
And make it part of who you are

[Instrumental Break: jagged guitar and detuned synth lead]

[Spoken, accusatory]
You say the world is cruel.
Then what will you do with the person in front of you?

[Bridge: piano and strings]
When you have less than you can spare
Can you still make a place to share?
When someone stumbles, tired and small
Will you make room, or watch them fall?

It won’t fix every broken street
Or put the missing back in reach
But care is not a thing we praise
Then leave unused on ordinary days

[Drums return]

[Final Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
BE THE KINDNESS YOU ASK FOR
LET IT SHAPE YOUR DAYS
SAY THE NAME THAT NO ONE SAYS
AND WALK WITH THEM A WAYS

No grand parade, no perfect plan
Just open hands, just where you stand
Choose the decent thing again
And make it part of who you are

[Gang Vocals]
You belong!
You are seen!

[Outro: piano and soft choir]
One small act.
One more day.
Make a little room.
Choose care.

title: Heart, Not an Open Safe
lyrics:
[Intro: clipped guitar pulse, spoken close and measured]
I brought a full bowl to the table.
Then I learned to watch the hands.

[Verse 1: spoken, tense]
I know the weight of an empty cupboard,
The last clean coat in winter rain.
So when you knock, I hear the old ache—
I reach before I know your name.

You say your phone died, your rent came due,
Your luck ran out, your ride fell through.
I split my bread, I lend my coat—
Then find my kindness in your throat.

[Pre-Chorus: gathering pressure]
I won’t turn stone; I won’t turn blind.
A tender heart still needs a mind.
Show me the work behind the plea.
Let time tell what your words can’t be.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
I’VE GOT A HEART, NOT AN OPEN SAFE!
I’LL GIVE WHAT’S TRUE—NOT WHAT YOU TAKE!
Bring honest hands, bring honest need!
I’ll know the difference by the deed!

[Post-Chorus]
Earn my trust—then share my table.
No more promises on borrowed labels.

[Verse 2: rhythmic spoken delivery]
You praised my patience, called it gold,
Then spent it like it couldn’t fold.
You knew just where my soft spots lay,
And called me cruel when I stepped away.

Now I ask who stays when there’s no favor,
Who keeps their word when the room gets quiet.
Who takes a little, leaves the rest,
Who sees my no and lets it rest.

[Pre-Chorus]
I won’t turn stone; I won’t turn blind.
A tender heart still needs a mind.
Show me the work behind the plea.
Let time tell what your words can’t be.

[Chorus: shouted gang vocals]
I’VE GOT A HEART, NOT AN OPEN SAFE!
I’LL GIVE WHAT’S TRUE—NOT WHAT YOU TAKE!
Bring honest hands, bring honest need!
I’ll know the difference by the deed!

[Bridge: stripped, spoken plainly]
To the one who carried water
And never counted every cup—
To the one who heard me say “not now”
And didn’t try to dress it up—
There’s room beside me.
There’s food to spare.
There’s time to give.
There’s care to share.

But love is not a door with no hinge.
And giving isn’t disappearing.

[Build]
I can keep my heart wide open
And still choose where the welcome goes.

[Final Chorus: explosive gang vocals]
I’VE GOT A HEART, NOT AN OPEN SAFE!
I’LL GIVE WHAT’S TRUE—NOT WHAT YOU TAKE!
Bring honest hands, bring honest need!
I’ll know the difference by the deed!

I’LL SHARE THE LOAD WITH THOSE WHO STAY!
I WON’T BE GUILTED INTO GIVING AWAY!
Bring honest hands, bring honest need!
My kindness has a gate—and I hold the key!

[Outro: spoken, resolved]
I’m still generous.
I’m just paying attention now.

title: The Gate Stays Locked
lyrics:
[Intro]
[Halftime trap drums enter, chiming delay guitar, fretless bass runs]

[Verse 1]
[Spoken]
My hands are open, but my eyes are sharp.
I used to hand out keys to every open door.
Now I measure the step before you cross the threshold.
You think generosity means blind surrender?
Think again.

[Pre-Chorus]
[Jagged palm-muted guitar riffs, syncopated crash accents]
Every hand outstretched carries a hidden ledger.
Every smiling mouth calculates the return.
I’m mapping out the grid, shifting in the shadows,
Sorting out the pretenders from the ones who earn.

[Chorus]
[Explosive chorus drop, shouted chorus gang vocals, detuned lead synth]
I HAVE A WELL THAT WILL NEVER RUN DRY!
BUT YOU DON'T GET A DROP JUST BY PASSING BY!
MANEUVER THE FIELD, FILTER THE GREED!
SAVING THE GOLD FOR THE ONES IN REAL NEED!
BITTER DEFIANCE, I DRAW THE BOUNDARY LINE!
WHAT IS TRULY EARNED IS ALL THAT I ASSIGN!

[Verse 2]
[Spoken]
You call it cold. I call it survival.
Too many parasites lining up at the gate.
I step to the left, I pivot to the right,
Letting the leech trip over their own expectations.
My heart stays warm, but my gate stays locked.

[Pre-Chorus]
[Tape saturation, tom-heavy fills]
Every hand outstretched carries a hidden ledger.
Every smiling mouth calculates the return.
I’m mapping out the grid, shifting in the shadows,
Sorting out the pretenders from the ones who earn.

[Chorus]
[Explosive chorus drop, shouted chorus gang vocals, detuned lead synth]
I HAVE A WELL THAT WILL NEVER RUN DRY!
BUT YOU DON'T GET A DROP JUST BY PASSING BY!
MANEUVER THE FIELD, FILTER THE GREED!
SAVING THE GOLD FOR THE ONES IN REAL NEED!
BITTER DEFIANCE, I DRAW THE BOUNDARY LINE!
WHAT IS TRULY EARNED IS ALL THAT I ASSIGN!

[Bridge]
[Synth choir pads, plate reverb, tempo slows]
[Spoken]
To the worthy... I will give everything.
To the takers... you get nothing at all.

[Outro]
[Jagged palm-muted guitar riffs fade, syncopated crash accents]
Watch your step.
Earn the grace.
The gate stays locked.

title: The Shape of You
lyrics:
[Intro]
I used to ask one question
Like it had one answer

[Verse 1]
You held my keys while I ran for the train
You kept them safe, then you lost them again
You show up early when somebody’s sick
But dates and directions don’t always quite stick

I used to sort people in yes or in no
A door locked tight or a wide-open road
Then I watched you try, watched you miss, watched you learn
And found there are corners we earn as we turn

[Pre-Chorus]
Not every hand can carry every weight
Not every promise means the same thing
We learn by asking, we learn by time
By saying what’s yours, what’s yours and what’s mine

[Chorus]
Trust isn’t all or nothing
It’s knowing where to place it
The ways you show up steady
The parts we need to name yet
I learn the shape of you
You learn the shape of me
And every honest boundary
Makes room for us to meet

[Verse 2]
You’re good with the truth when the room gets tense
But don’t lend you money without talking it through first
I keep a secret, but I’m slow to reply
You’ll make the hard call when I freeze up inside

No verdict, no stamp, no perfect design
Just two changing people drawing a line
Then moving it gently when something is new
The map gets more human the more that we do

[Pre-Chorus]
Not every hand can carry every weight
Not every promise means the same thing
We learn by asking, we learn by time
By saying what’s yours, what’s yours and what’s mine

[Chorus]
Trust isn’t all or nothing
It’s knowing where to place it
The ways you show up steady
The parts we need to name yet
I learn the shape of you
You learn the shape of me
And every honest boundary
Makes room for us to meet

[Bridge]
Maybe you can sit beside my grief
But not decide how long it stays
Maybe I can guard the plans we share
But need you to remind me of the dates

There’s joy in finding out the edges
There’s kindness in a limit understood
We don’t have to call each other flawless
To notice where we do each other good

[Final Chorus]
Trust isn’t all or nothing
It’s knowing where to place it
The ways you show up steady
The parts we need to name yet
I learn the shape of you
You learn the shape of me
Each person is a country
Worth the time to read

[Outro]
Not everything, not nothing
A little more known each day
And in the learning, there’s the joy
Of meeting you your way

title: Beneath the Paper Scars
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You keep a paper heart inside your coat
With little cuts from every word they wrote
But underneath the folds, still warm and whole
A good small garden waiting in your soul

[Pre-Chorus]
So when your hands are shaking, take mine
We can mend one edge at a time

[Chorus]
You are good beneath the paper scars
Still tender where the hard days are
A careful word, a hand held out
Can help the hurting breathe back out
We heal a little, me and you
With every kind thing that we do

[Verse 2]
You saved the seat, you let me speak
You saw the brave behind the weak
No grand repair, no perfect plan
Just room to be a person, hand in hand

[Pre-Chorus]
When someone’s edges catch and tear
Be gentle; there is goodness there

[Chorus]
You are good beneath the paper scars
Still tender where the hard days are
A careful word, a hand held out
Can help the hurting breathe back out
We heal a little, me and you
With every kind thing that we do

[Bridge]
Not every wound will close today
But kindness makes a softer way
We pass that softness, palm to palm
And find the good beneath the harm

[Final Chorus]
We are good beneath the paper scars
Still tender where the hard days are
A careful word, a hand held out
Can help the hurting breathe back out
We heal a little, me and you
With every kind thing that we do

[Outro]
One gentle word
One open hand
The good in us
Can grow again

title: Kindness Keeps on Traveling
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You held the door when my hands were full
You learned my name when the room was loud
A paper cup of water, a chair pulled near
Small things make a little more room here

[Pre-Chorus]
I carried that care past the corner store
And left it with someone who needed it more

[Chorus]
Kindness keeps on traveling
Hand to hand, heart to heart
What you give becomes a way through
What we share becomes a start
Every patient word can open
Every welcome make us whole
The world grows rich in what we give
And richer still in every soul

[Verse 2]
You stayed a while while I found my words
You let the silence take the time it takes
I brought that patience home with me
And gave it where a hard day breaks

[Pre-Chorus]
One gentle act can cross a town
A dozen hands can pass it round

[Chorus]
Kindness keeps on traveling
Hand to hand, heart to heart
What you give becomes a way through
What we share becomes a start
Every patient word can open
Every welcome make us whole
The world grows rich in what we give
And richer still in every soul

[Bridge]
Not coins in a jar, not a score to keep
But meals set out and a promise you keep
A place at the table, a second chance
A little more courage to take the next step

[Final Chorus]
Kindness keeps on traveling
Hand to hand, heart to heart
What you give becomes a way through
What we share becomes a start
Every patient word can open
Every welcome make us whole
The world grows rich in what we give
And richer still in every soul

[Outro]
You gave a little room to breathe
I’ll pass that room along
A world made richer, one kind act
One open door, one song

title: How We Care
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You held the door when my hands were full
Said my name when the room went dull
Left the last orange on the kitchen plate
Small things arrive before it’s too late

You asked how I was, then waited there
Long enough for the honest answer to appear
I took that patience out into the day
And gave it to somebody on the way

[Pre-Chorus]
One open hand can change the shape
Of what another hand will make

[Chorus]
Kindness travels farther than we know
Passed from heart to heart, it starts to grow
What you give comes back in what we share
A richer world is built by how we care

[Verse 2]
You brought warm bread to the upstairs room
Where Mrs. Alvarez nursed her winter bloom
She saved a slice for the courier downstairs
Who called his sister just to say he cares

A child saw that, and offered her seat
To a tired man with rain on his sleeves
He smiled at the child, she smiled at me
That’s how a town becomes what it can be

[Pre-Chorus]
No grand design, no golden key
Just you making room for me

[Chorus]
Kindness travels farther than we know
Passed from heart to heart, it starts to grow
What you give comes back in what we share
A richer world is built by how we care

[Bridge]
Not a bargain, not a debt
Not a kindness to forget
Just a little more room at the table
A chance to begin again, when able

[Final Chorus]
Kindness travels farther than we know
Passed from heart to heart, it starts to grow
Every welcome makes the circle wide
Every gentle act leaves more inside
What you give comes back in what we share
A richer world is built by how we care

[Outro]
You made room for me
I’ll make room for you

title: Kindness Takes Root
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left the last orange on the stair
For the neighbor hauling boxes there
She wrote your name on a paper sack
And left two pears when she came back

A door held open, a coat passed down
Small mercies travel through a town
They cross the counter, climb the stairs
And teach the hands that kindness is shared

[Pre-Chorus]
One careful word can turn a day
One open hand can make a way

[Chorus]
Be kind, and kindness takes root
In the ordinary things we do
It grows from one heart to another
Till strangers make room for each other
Give what you can, however small
The more we share, the rich we all become

[Verse 2]
You let the tired cashier take her time
She smiled, then called her sister in line
He heard that smile and softened his tone
That night he brought soup to a friend alone

No ledger keeps what passes through
A little grace comes back as something new
A safer block, a table wide
More room for everyone inside

[Pre-Chorus]
One careful word can turn a day
One open hand can make a way

[Chorus]
Be kind, and kindness takes root
In the ordinary things we do
It grows from one heart to another
Till strangers make room for each other
Give what you can, however small
The more we share, the rich we all become

[Bridge]
Not in gold locked out of sight
But in a neighbor checking in at night
In the seat you save, the truth you tell
In learning how to listen well
No one grows poorer giving care
The wealth is in the welcome there

[Final Chorus]
Be kind, and kindness takes root
In every ordinary thing we do
It grows from one heart to another
Till strangers stand beside each other
Give what you can, let mercy run
The more we share, the more the world has become
A place with open doors and room
A hundred hands to help things bloom

[Outro]
You held the door
I passed it on
And somewhere else
A light came on

title: Leave A Little Room
lyrics:
[Intro: single piano chord, distant room murmur]

[Spoken]
You don’t need a grand gesture.

You don’t need the perfect thing to say.

[Pause]
Start by making room.

[Drums enter]

[Verse 1]
You see the cashier count the change
The line is long, the day feels strange
You meet her eyes, you let her take her time
A little patience costs you nothing, still it matters every time

You hold the door when hands are full
You ask before you offer help
You hear the story all the way through
Without rehearsing what you’ll say next

[Backing Vocals]
Small things!
Soft words!
Right here!

[Lead]
That counts.

[Pre-Chorus]
No medal waiting, no applause
Just choosing care without a cause

A little grace can change the shape
Of someone’s hardest hour today

[Chorus: wide guitars and layered harmonies]
LEAVE A LITTLE ROOM
FOR THE HEART YOU HAVEN’T KNOWN
GIVE A LITTLE GRACE
MAKE THE COLD DAY LESS ALONE

You don’t know what they carried
When they walked into the room
So let kindness be your first reply
Leave a little room

[Choir]
MAKE ROOM!

[Lead]
For the bold
For the worn
For the late and the unsure

For the ones who need a minute
For the ones who need the door

You can’t mend every trouble
You can still be something kind
A steady hand, a gentler answer
A place to set a heavy mind

[Verse 2: bouncing bass, handclaps]
You bring a bowl next door when someone’s sick
You learn the name the new kid picked
You send the note you nearly never sent
And mean the words, not just the sentiment

You thank the nurse at closing time
You let a friend change their mind
You share the bench, you split the pear
You notice who is standing there

[Backing Vocals]
I see you!
I see you!

[Lead]
Funny how a simple kindness
Can make a stranger feel less strange

[Pre-Chorus]
A softer answer isn’t weak
A patient pause can let folks speak

No perfect person, no perfect day
Just one more chance to choose your way

[Chorus]
LEAVE A LITTLE ROOM
FOR THE HEART YOU HAVEN’T KNOWN
GIVE A LITTLE GRACE
MAKE THE COLD DAY LESS ALONE

You don’t know what they carried
When they walked into the room
So let kindness be your first reply
Leave a little room

[Choir]
MAKE ROOM!

[Instrumental Break: triumphant guitar solo]

[Handclaps]

[Choir]
For the tired!
For the new!
For the ones we never knew!

[Lead, smiling]
There’s enough care to go around.

[Bridge: music drops to piano and strings]
It isn’t easy staying gentle
When the day has worn you thin
When the same old sharp remark
Comes ready to your tongue again

When your own small grief is waiting
When you’re running out of room
You can name the hurt you’re carrying
And still leave a little room

[Pause]
For the neighbor at the doorway
For the friend who missed your call
For the stranger with the shaking hands
Who says they’re fine, that’s all

[Strings swell]
Kindness isn’t fixing
Every broken thing in sight
Sometimes it is sitting with someone
Till the morning feels less far

Sometimes it’s a boundary
Sometimes it’s a truthful no
Care can hold its shape and still say
I can’t come, but I hope you know

[Drums explode back in]

[Final Chorus: key change]
LEAVE A LITTLE ROOM
LET IT CARRY THROUGH THE HALL
YOU DON’T HAVE TO SAVE THE WORLD
TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE SMALL

Let them stumble
Let them speak
Let them have a day that’s hard

One unhurried moment of care
Can reach farther than you thought

[Choir]
KINDNESS COUNTS!

[Lead]
Here’s to the patient
Here’s to the brave

Here’s to the person who listens
When nothing can be changed

You don’t need to be a saint
You don’t need to get it right
Just meet the next soul in front of you
With a little more light

[Choir]
Stay kind!
Stay true!
Start anew!

[Lead]
The smallest decent choice
Can see somebody through

[Final Refrain]
Share the seat
Learn the name
Say you’re sorry
Take the blame

Give them time
Tell the truth
Keep your word
Make room

[Choir rising]
Not for credit
Not for show
Not because you’re owed

[Lead]
Let your care be something ordinary
That the people near you know

[Music drops]
And when the day is almost done…

[Pause]
Be gentle with yourself
The way you’d be with someone

[Outro: piano and soft choir]

[Soft Vocal]
Leave a little room

[Choir]
A little room

[Lead]
The kindness you give away
Can help a hard day move

[Final guitar chord]

title: Default to Grace
lyrics:
[Intro: atmospheric IDM synth pads, soft glitchy percussion]

[Verse 1]
The world is sharp, the world is loud
A million voices in the crowd
They build up armor, grow so cold
Trading their warmth for what is sold
But there's a quiet strength in choosing grace
A steady anchor in this crowded space

[Pre-Chorus]
Before you walk into the storm
Before you take another form
Decide the ground on which you stand
A gentle word, a steady hand

[Chorus]
MAKE KINDNESS YOUR DEFAULT
THE FIRST STEP IN THE DARK
A quiet revolution
A soft, electric spark
It's not a weakness, not a compromise
It's looking forward with open eyes
Let the world be cold and blue
Your first move is waiting, warm and true

[Verse 2]
An easy cynicism, cheap defense
To build a wall that makes no sense
But treating every stranger like a friend
Is where the broken patterns start to end
It takes a fierce and quiet kind of heart
To play the gentle, unexpected part

[Bridge: glitch phonk beats and soaring melodic rock guitars]
When they strike, you do not bend
You don't break, you don't pretend
Kindness is the shield you wear
A deeper power, a silent prayer

[Guitar Solo]

[Chorus]
MAKE KINDNESS YOUR DEFAULT
THE FIRST STEP IN THE DARK
A quiet revolution
A soft, electric spark
It's not a weakness, not a compromise
It's looking forward with open eyes
Let the world be cold and blue
Your first move is waiting, warm and true

[Outro: fading melodic synths, gentle ambient wash]
Default to grace.
Before the anger starts to rise.
Look at the world
With actual eyes.

title: Meet Them With Kindness
lyrics:
[Intro: single piano chord, distant crowd murmur]

[Spoken]
A small kindness can change a day.
A hand held out can make room.

[Pause]

[Drums enter]

[Verse 1]
You dropped your papers in the rain
I held my coat above the page
You laughed and said, “I’m fine, I’m fine”
I stayed until the bus arrived

You learned my name, I learned yours too
A little room made something new
No grand display, no perfect plan
Just seeing someone where they stand

[Backing Vocals]
Make room!
Reach out!
Stay kind!

[Lead]
Right here.

[Pre-Chorus]
A kinder world is built this way
With what we choose to do today
One open door, one honest ear
A little less to fear

[Chorus: huge guitars and choir]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET SOMEBODY IN
MEET THEM WITH A KINDNESS
WHERE A HARD DAY MIGHT BEGIN

If the road feels heavy
And the morning’s running late
Walk beside each other
We can lighten what we take

[Choir]
WE CAN LIGHTEN WHAT WE TAKE!

[Lead]
Here’s to the patient
Here’s to the brave
Here’s to the ones
Who stop and stay

A world gets better, step by step
With every care we choose to give

[Verse 2: bouncing bass, handclaps]
You saved me the seat by the window side
When my hands were full and the bus pulled wide
I brought soup when your fever came
You sent a note when I missed the train

The new kid eating lunch alone
The neighbor carrying boxes home
The friend who says, “I need a while”
We listen first; we don’t demand a smile

[Backing Vocals]
You belong!
You belong!

[Lead]
Sometimes the bravest thing we do
Is let another person tell the truth

[Pre-Chorus]
No one is only what they show
No one should have to hurt alone
A simple question, asked with care
Can say, “I’m glad you’re here”

[Chorus]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET SOMEBODY IN
MEET THEM WITH A KINDNESS
WHERE A HARD DAY MIGHT BEGIN

If the road feels heavy
And the morning’s running late
Walk beside each other
We can lighten what we take

[Choir]
WE CAN LIGHTEN WHAT WE TAKE!

[Instrumental Break: triumphant guitar solo]

[Handclaps]

[Choir]
Make room!
Reach out!
Stay kind!

[Lead, laughing]
That’s a good place to start.

[Bridge: music drops to piano and strings]

It isn’t always easy
To know the thing to say
Sometimes just a quiet chair
Can help someone stay

When anger fills the kitchen
When the words come out too fast
We can choose to take a breath
And not make hurtfulness last

[Pause]

So here’s to every mended trust
And every second try
To telling someone, “That was wrong,”
Then showing why we’ll try

[Strings swell]

Kindness isn’t weakness
It can ask us to be strong
To hold a boundary gently
And still help someone belong

[Drums explode back in]

[Final Chorus: key change]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET THE WHOLE WORLD IN
MEET EACH OTHER WITH A KINDNESS
LET THE HEALING WORK BEGIN

When the road feels heavy
When the night runs long and late
Walk beside each other
We can change the weight we take

[Choir]
WE CAN CHANGE THE WEIGHT WE TAKE!

[Lead]
Here’s to the hurting
Here’s to the healed
Here’s to the care
That helps us rebuild

A kinder world is not a distant place
It starts between us, face to face

[Choir]
Stand near!
Speak true!
Stay kind!

[Lead]
There is room enough for you and me

[Final Refrain]
Share the table
Learn the name
Give the time
Without a claim

Hear the story
Make amends
Hold the door
And make a friend

[Choir rising]
Not someday
Not somewhere
Not for someone else to do

[Lead]
Let the world feel gentler
Because it met you

[Music drops]

And when the day turns rough…

[Pause]

Be the person who stays

[Outro: piano and soft choir]

[Soft Vocal]
Make a little room

[Choir]
Make room

[Lead]
A kinder world begins with what we do

[Final guitar chord]

title: Let Somebody In
lyrics:
[Intro: single piano chord, distant room murmur]
[Spoken]
A door held open.
A name remembered.
A place made at the table.

[Verse 1]
You saved the seat beside the wall
And noticed I had missed the call
You asked me how the morning went
Then stayed to hear what I meant

No grand parade, no perfect plan
Just time you gave another hand
A little room to breathe and try
A little truth without a lie

[Pre-Chorus]
When the day has worn us thin
Let one kind word begin again
Pass it on from hand to hand
Make a little more room where we stand

[Chorus]
MAKE ROOM, MAKE ROOM
LET SOMEBODY IN
A patient ear, a place to begin
Small acts of care can travel far
From one open door to where we are
MAKE ROOM, MAKE ROOM
Let the good move through
The world gets kinder
When I make room for you

[Verse 2]
You learned the new kid’s lunchbox name
You took the blame when blame was aimed
You left the last warm roll for me
And let an old friend disagree

You called your neighbor just to ask
If carrying groceries felt like a task
You gave the tired cashier a smile
And let the rushed line breathe a while

[Pre-Chorus]
No one has to earn their worth
No one should stand alone on earth
A hand extended, steady, plain
Can help somebody start again

[Chorus]
MAKE ROOM, MAKE ROOM
LET SOMEBODY IN
A patient ear, a place to begin
Small acts of care can travel far
From one open door to where we are
MAKE ROOM, MAKE ROOM
Let the good move through
The world gets kinder
When I make room for you

[Instrumental Break: fretless bass and toms, rising guitars]

[Bridge: sparse piano and strings]
If you’re carrying more than you can say
You don’t have to explain it all today
I can sit here; we can take our time
No fixing, no hurry, no reason to hide

And when I’m the one who loses my way
I hope you’ll remember these words I say
A gentle answer, a shoulder nearby
Can keep one more hope from saying goodbye

[Build]
One cup of tea
One honest call
One extra chair
Can change it all

[Final Chorus: bright major lift]
MAKE ROOM, MAKE ROOM
LET EVERY HEART IN
A patient ear, a place to begin
Small acts of care can travel far
From one open door to where we are
MAKE ROOM, MAKE ROOM
Let the good move through
The world gets kinder
When I make room for you

[Choir]
Room for the weary
Room for the new
Room for a different point of view

[Lead]
No one is too small to start
Kindness grows from an ordinary heart

[Final Refrain]
Hold the door
Learn the name
Share the weight
Skip the blame
Hear them out
Stay awhile
Offer truth
Leave room to smile

[Outro: piano and soft choir]
Make room for you
Make room for me
A kinder world
Begins quietly

title: One Small Act
lyrics:
[Intro: single piano chord, distant crowd murmur]

[Spoken]
A small thing can change a day.
A hand held open.
A name remembered.

[Pause]
You can begin right here.

[Drums enter]

[Verse 1]
You saw her carrying two paper bags
One handle split, the oranges rolled
You caught them by the corner shop
And walked beside her half a block

You let the older man finish his thought
Though everyone else had turned away
You asked the kid what they liked to be called
Then used that name the very next day

No grand parade, no perfect plan
Just notice where another stands

[Backing Vocals]
Make room!
Stay near!
Be kind!

[Lead]
Right here.

[Pre-Chorus]
A softer answer can stop a spark
A little patience can reach the heart

A chair pulled close, a door held wide
A quiet “you can sit with us” tonight

[Chorus: huge guitars and choir]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET ANOTHER HEART COME THROUGH

SHARE THE LOAD
SAY THEIR NAME
LET THEM KNOW THEY’RE WELCOME TOO

When the day has been unkind
Be the pause, be the proof

One small act can travel far

[Choir]
PASS IT ON!

[Lead]
Here’s to the ones who notice first
Who bring the water, share the words

Here’s to the ones who stay awhile
And make a hard room easier to cross

No one has to earn a place
No one should have to ask for grace

Start with what you do

[Verse 2: bouncing bass, handclaps]
You split your lunch beneath the bus stop sign
For someone counting coins in the rain
You helped your neighbor carry a chair upstairs
Then stayed to hear about the pain

You gave the new kid space to speak
You didn’t turn their fear to a joke
You called your brother after all that time
And let the first hello be slow

The nurse remembered a worried face
The shop clerk gave the tired dad a minute
The stranger held the elevator door
And made the whole day feel less distant

[Backing Vocals]
I see you!
I’m here, too!

[Lead]
Kindness isn’t grand from far away
It’s what you choose in the ordinary

[Pre-Chorus]
A neighborhood is made by hands
By little promises we understand

A warm meal left beside the door
A second chance, a little more

[Chorus]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET ANOTHER HEART COME THROUGH

SHARE THE LOAD
SAY THEIR NAME
LET THEM KNOW THEY’RE WELCOME TOO

When the day has been unkind
Be the pause, be the proof

One small act can travel far

[Choir]
PASS IT ON!

[Instrumental Break: triumphant guitar solo]

[Handclaps]

[Choir]
Stay close!
Reach out!
Make room!
Come through!

[Lead, laughing]
That’s how a town gets through.

[Bridge: music drops to piano and strings]
Some days the words arrive too late
Some hurts don’t leave when morning comes

You can’t repair a life at once
Or make the hard things disappear

But you can sit beside the door
And wait until they’re ready to speak
You can bring the soup, remember Tuesday
And ask again next week

[Pause]
So here’s to every patient hand
That doesn’t need to take the stage
Every honest apology
That makes a little space

[Strings swell]
Kindness isn’t weakness
It isn’t keeping score

It’s seeing someone’s burden
And choosing not to add one more

[Drums explode back in]

[Final Chorus: key change]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET THE WHOLE WIDE WORLD COME THROUGH

SHARE THE LOAD
SAY THEIR NAME
LET THEM KNOW THEY MATTER TOO

When the day has been unkind
Be the shelter, be the proof

Every small act leaves a mark

[Choir]
PASS IT ON!

[Lead]
Here’s to the tired, here’s to the new
Here’s to the ones who don’t know what to do

Here’s to the friend who calls again
And the open seat beside a stranger

[Choir]
Stay near!
Reach out!
Make room!

[Lead]
A better world begins with you

[Final Refrain]
Learn their name
Share your bread
Hear the words they haven’t said

Give your time
Tell the truth
Keep a promise, follow through

[Choir rising]
Not for praise
Not for show
Just because we all need room to grow

[Lead]
Let your care be something people know

[Music drops]
And when you’re not sure what to do…

[Pause]
Stay long enough
To ask what would help

[Outro: piano and soft choir]

[Soft Vocal]
Make a little room

[Choir]
A little room

[Lead]
We build a better world
In the way we treat each other

[Final guitar chord]

title: Kinder Land
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You held the door when my hands were full
You stayed to listen when I couldn't talk
No grand display, no silver rule
Just room to breathe, and time to walk

You learned my name, you asked me twice
You made a place at the crowded table
A little care can change a day
A steady hand can make us able

[Pre-Chorus]
What if strength is making space
What if courage starts with grace

[Chorus]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET ANOTHER HEART COME THROUGH
Share the shade, pass the bread
Say the kind thing you can do
When the road is rough and long
We can lift each other on
Step by step, hand to hand
We can build a kinder land

[Verse 2]
The nurse on night shift knows the names
The neighbor clears the walk before the snow
The kid who asks you in the game
The friend who lets the hard truth show

A fair day's pay, a safe place to sleep
A school where every question matters
Promises are things we keep
And kindness mends what anger scatters

[Pre-Chorus]
What if strength is making space
What if courage starts with grace

[Chorus]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET ANOTHER HEART COME THROUGH
Share the shade, pass the bread
Say the kind thing you can do
When the road is rough and long
We can lift each other on
Step by step, hand to hand
We can build a kinder land

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge]
Not every hurt can disappear
Not every answer comes today
But we can meet each other here
And choose a better way

When the rules leave someone out
When a voice is hard to hear
Stand beside them, speak aloud
Make the welcome real and clear

[Breakdown]
One open seat
One honest word
One second chance
One voice heard

[Final Chorus]
MAKE A LITTLE ROOM
LET ANOTHER HEART COME THROUGH
Share the shade, pass the bread
Say the kind thing you can do
When the road is rough and long
We can lift each other on
Step by step, hand to hand
We can build a kinder land

[Outro]
Start right here, with what you can
A kinder world is made by hands

title: Give the Absurd a Second Word
lyrics:
[Intro: clipped spoken delivery]
They said, “Stay inside the lines.”
I brought a ladder and a box of chalk.

[Verse 1]
I drew a door upon the floor
It opened up to seven more
A paper moon, a glass giraffe
A staircase built to make you laugh

I made a hat that hats the hat
A map that folds around the map
You asked me, “Does it make good sense?”
I said, “Not yet. That’s the suspense.”

[Pre-Chorus]
Take the left turn through the blue
Put the upside somewhere new
If the rule says, “This is how,”
Try a different kind of now

[Chorus]
Make a little trouble with the ordinary
Turn the square into a berry
Build a boat from yesterday
Sail it somewhere no one’s named

Make it stranger, make it yours
Kick a window through the doors
If the world says, “That’s absurd”
Give the absurd a second word

[Verse 2]
I taught a spoon to tell the time
It only rang when things were fine
My boots grew wings on Thursday noon
And carried me past Saturn’s moon

A tiny dragon in my coat
Keeps all my brilliant scraps afloat
You bring a thought you nearly hid
We’ll make a castle out of it

[Pre-Chorus]
Take the left turn through the blue
Put the upside somewhere new
If the rule says, “This is how,”
Try a different kind of now

[Chorus]
Make a little trouble with the ordinary
Turn the square into a berry
Build a boat from yesterday
Sail it somewhere no one’s named

Make it stranger, make it yours
Kick a window through the doors
If the world says, “That’s absurd”
Give the absurd a second word

[Instrumental Break: angular guitar counterpoint and fretless bass]

[Breakdown: half-time, playful chant]
One bent spoon!
Two left shoes!
Three good reasons to refuse

Too peculiar!
Too much fun!
Look what happens when we run

[Bridge: piano and strings, intimate]
Some ideas arrive half-dressed
With crooked seams and no address
Don’t send them back, don’t make them neat
Set them down and give them feet

You don’t have to know the end
Before you make the first pretend
A thought can wobble, change its name
And still be worth the little flame

[Build]
Pass me the impossible
I’ll hold it while it grows
You bring the wild beginning
I’ll bring the wrong-way road

[Final Chorus: bright major lift]
Make a little trouble with the ordinary
Turn the square into a berry
Build a boat from yesterday
Sail it somewhere no one’s named

Make it stranger, make it yours
Kick a window through the doors
If the world says, “That’s absurd”
Give the absurd a second word

[Final Refrain]
Change the scale
Swap the sky
Let the fish learn how to fly
Move the moon
Bend the spoon
Give the afternoon a tune

[Outro: drop to close voice]
They said, “Stay inside the lines.”
I made the lines a trampoline.

title: Make a Mess of the Blueprint
lyrics:
[Intro: clipped guitar harmonics, breath, distant room tone]

[Spoken]
I found a door in the middle of the floor.
It had no room behind it.
So I opened it anyway.

[Verse 1]
I put a spoon inside the freezer
Just to see what morning made
Wore two different shoes to breakfast
And called the mismatch brave

The calendar said behave yourself
The kettle said begin
I drew a spiral through the grocery list
And let the wrong day in

[Pre-Chorus]
If the straight line feels suspicious
Take the crooked one instead
There are maps that only open
When you stop obeying them

[Chorus]
MAKE A MESS OF THE BLUEPRINT
TURN THE HANDLE PAST THE SIGN
IF THE ANSWER LOOKS TOO POLISHED
THROW A QUESTION IN ITS EYES

You were not built for tidy endings
You were not designed to blend
Make a little room for wonder
Then make stranger room again

[Verse 2]
I taught a clock to count in sevens
Put a motor on a kite
Sent a postcard to tomorrow
Got a stamp back overnight

Every polished little answer
Keeps a splinter underneath
I would rather hold the splinter
Than mistake the shine for peace

[Pre-Chorus]
Let the hallway change its ceiling
Let the furniture revolt
When the ordinary gets too certain
Give it somewhere else to go

[Chorus]
MAKE A MESS OF THE BLUEPRINT
TURN THE HANDLE PAST THE SIGN
IF THE ANSWER LOOKS TOO POLISHED
THROW A QUESTION IN ITS EYES

You were not built for tidy endings
You were not designed to blend
Make a little room for wonder
Then make stranger room again

[Instrumental Break: broken-meter bass and toms, guitar fragments, chopped vocal syllables]

[Call and Response]
What if?
Try it.
Why not?
Again.

[Bridge: half-time, piano, bowed guitar harmonics]
Some nights the clever thing is simply
To admit you do not know
Some days the bravest act is leaving
One small window open low

Keep the cracked cup on the table
Keep the question in your coat
There is no prize for being finished
There is only more to notice

[Breakdown]
Count the corners
Miss a number
Change the key
Forget the reason

[Final Chorus: bright major, expanding harmonies]
MAKE A MESS OF THE BLUEPRINT
LET THE COLORS CROSS THE LINE
IF THE ANSWER LOOKS TOO POLISHED
BUILD A BETTER KIND OF WHY

You were not built for tidy endings
You were not designed to blend
Make a little room for wonder
Then make stranger room again

[Final Refrain]
Wrong turn
New door
Small spark
Much more

Keep the odd idea breathing
Keep the impossible in sight
If the world asks for a straight face
Give it seven shades of bright

[Outro: guitar harmonics, bass pulse, close vocal]
I opened the door with nothing behind it.
Now something is growing there.

title: Arriving Sideways
lyrics:
[Intro]
They gave me a measuring tape
And a shape to fit inside
I folded up the little map
And drew beyond its lines

[Spoken]
They said, “Pick one.”
I picked the whole strange box of crayons.

[Verse 1]
I wear two mismatched shoes to town
One takes the stairs, one skips the ground
My pockets hold a paper moon
A bent spoon, and a kazoo

You asked me which way people go
I said, “The way the wild seeds blow”
Then built a tiny door in air
And walked through it with purple hair

[Pre-Chorus]
If every rule is made of string
Then watch what happens when I swing
I’ll turn the “wrong” way into art
And give the odd bits all my heart

[Chorus]
Make room, make room, I’m arriving sideways
With a pocketful of thunder and a hat full of Mondays
Call me too much, call me peculiar
I’m not a puzzle, I’m the whole panorama
If your doorway only lets one shape through
Cut a new window; let the weird come through

[Verse 2]
I taught my chair to spin in place
My teacup wears a tiny cape
The clock ran backward through the hall
And nobody corrected it at all

I made a kite from old receipts
It flew above the bakery street
The baker waved a rolling pin
And said, “That’s how adventures begin”

[Pre-Chorus]
A thought can wear its Sunday shoes
Then change its mind and join the blues
A crooked line can find its way
To something no straight road could say

[Chorus]
Make room, make room, I’m arriving sideways
With a pocketful of thunder and a hat full of Mondays
Call me too much, call me peculiar
I’m not a puzzle, I’m the whole panorama
If your doorway only lets one shape through
Cut a new window; let the weird come through

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge]
Some days the room gets very small
And every eye becomes a wall
I tuck my bright ideas away
And practice being beige all day

Then from my sleeve a paper fish
Says, “You forgot your own odd wish”
So I unfold the hidden page
And let my colors leave the cage

[Breakdown]
One crooked thought
One brave hello
One little seed
Can split the stone

[Build]
No perfect label, no fixed design
The strange in yours can sit with mine
We’ll make a place where every shape
Can bend, invent, and change its name

[Final Chorus]
Make room, make room, we’re arriving sideways
With a pocketful of thunder and a hat full of Mondays
Call us too much, call us peculiar
We’re not a puzzle, we’re the whole panorama
If your doorway only lets one shape through
Cut a new window; let the weird come through

[Final Refrain]
Wear the clouds, keep the key
Draw a door where none should be
Change your tune, turn around
Plant a garden upside down

[Outro]
They gave me a measuring tape
I made a ribbon for the sky

title: Build a Wider Doorway
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken, intimate]
They handed me a cardboard moon
And said, “Please wear it facing north.”
I tried it on. It fit the room.
It didn’t fit the shape I was.

[Verse 1]
I kept a drawer of borrowed names,
A paper crown, a rulebook map.
They marked the edges, drew the frame,
Then asked me why I wouldn’t clap.

I learned the proper ways to shrink,
The measured laugh, the lowered eyes.
Then spilled blue ink into the sink
And watched a little ocean rise.

[Pre-Chorus]
Who made the ruler ruler?
Who chose the only door?
I turned the sign around and found
A staircase in the floor.

[Chorus]
MAKE ROOM FOR THE UNLIKELY
LET THE STRANGE THINGS GROW
I’LL TAKE THE SIDEWAYS PASSAGE
WHERE THE WILD IDEAS GO
If your frame can’t hold the person
Standing there in full array,
Don’t trim the edges off your life—
Build a wider doorway.

[Verse 2]
I met a clock that ran in threes,
A teacup full of paper fish,
A quiet kid who planted keys
And grew a garden from a wish.

A woman took the long way home,
A man let every tear arrive.
The odd-shaped pieces found their own
Remarkable ways to fit alive.

[Pre-Chorus]
A label is a little box
With tidy printing on the side.
But people change the weather there;
The shelves are much too small inside.

[Chorus]
MAKE ROOM FOR THE UNLIKELY
LET THE STRANGE THINGS GROW
I’LL TAKE THE SIDEWAYS PASSAGE
WHERE THE WILD IDEAS GO
If your frame can’t hold the person
Standing there in full array,
Don’t trim the edges off your life—
Build a wider doorway.

[Instrumental Break: fractured riff, shifting accents]

[Bridge: half-time, close and vulnerable]
It costs to tell the truth some days.
A room can turn its chairs away.
Still, one small hand can reach the latch;
One honest word can split the patch.

I’m not a puzzle for your shelf.
I’m not a draft you get to mend.
I’m learning how to be myself
Without requesting an amend.

[Build]
One crooked line—
A window.
One wrong turn—
A way through.
All the parts you called too much
Were parts that made me true.

[Final Chorus: expansive, cathartic]
MAKE ROOM FOR THE UNLIKELY
LET THE STRANGE THINGS GROW
I’LL TAKE THE SIDEWAYS PASSAGE
AND I’LL TAKE IT AS I GO
You can keep your little measure,
You can keep your narrow frame;
I will meet the world unedited,
Answering to my chosen name.

[Final Refrain]
Change the plan, change the pattern,
Turn the map and draw it new.
Every strange and splendid angle
Has a place the world can make room for.

[Outro: soft, direct]
If you don’t understand me,
You still met me as I am.

title: Museum of Unfinished Doors
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken, intimate]
They gave me a ruler
I built a small weather system
Inside the margins

[Verse 1]
I kept a jar of impossible things
A blue seed, a bent spoon, a paper moon
At lunch I taught the salt to sing
By Friday it had swallowed the room

You said, “Please make it ordinary”
I tried; the ordinary grew teeth
It bit through every careful box
And planted tiny forests underneath

[Pre-Chorus]
So take this map of folded skin
Turn it around and let the maze begin

[Chorus]
I am a museum of unfinished doors
A dozen strange keys and a thousand more
If I spill past the edges, let the colors run
I was not made to be only one

[Verse 2]
I wore Tuesday sideways on my head
Taught a clock to count in oranges
The neighbors called the doctor in
The doctor asked for my address

I sent him a flock of paper fish
They circled once, then changed their minds
You laughed so hard you dropped your script
And found a whole new voice inside

[Pre-Chorus]
No perfect shape, no final draft
The crooked answer makes me laugh

[Chorus]
I am a museum of unfinished doors
A dozen strange keys and a thousand more
If I spill past the edges, let the colors run
I was not made to be only one

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge: half-time, exposed]
Some days the room gets small again
Some days I fold to fit
Then you leave a window open
And I remember how to split
One thought into a hundred birds
One fear into a drum of rain
I don’t need to solve the world
I need to make it weird again

[Final Chorus]
I am a museum of unfinished doors
A dozen strange keys and a thousand more
Let the floor turn liquid, let the ceiling run
I was not made to be only one

[Outro]
Keep the ruler
Keep the lines
I’ll grow a garden
In the margins this time

title: Pumpkin Spice is Back
lyrics:
[Intro]
First cool morning, paper cup in hand
A little cinnamon weather rolling through the land

[Verse 1]
The chalkboard changes, leaves turn gold
That familiar swirl returns each fall
Espresso meeting pumpkin, spice in the foam
One first warm sip and the season feels like home

[Pre-Chorus]
You see the sign, you know the cue
A yearly little ritual, waiting just for you

[Chorus]
Pumpkin spice is back again
Golden warmth around the bend
Sweet cream clouds and cinnamon
A small bright comfort when the cold moves in
Every year, that first delight
Autumn served up just right

[Verse 2]
Pumpkin loaf beside the cup, soft crumb, sugared top
A latte held between both hands while busy hours stop
The barista calls your name above the morning rush
You take it out beneath the trees, let the season hush

[Pre-Chorus]
The menu turns, the air grows crisp
And there it is, that first familiar sip

[Chorus]
Pumpkin spice is back again
Golden warmth around the bend
Sweet cream clouds and cinnamon
A small bright comfort when the cold moves in
Every year, that first delight
