Autumn served up just right

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge: half-time]
Not just a flavor, not just a cup
It’s the week the wool coats all come up
It’s meeting you where September ends
A simple treat that feels like friends

[Final Chorus]
Pumpkin spice is back again
Raise a cup to old traditions
Pumpkin bread and cinnamon
Little seasonal celebrations
Every year, the colors turn
Every year, the same hearts yearn
When that first autumn menu arrives
A warm small wonder comes alive

[Outro]
The last leaves fall, the cup is gone
We’ll meet again when the year turns on
Pumpkin spice, until then

title: The Blue Shirt
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You said you liked the blue one, so I wore it through the heat
I learned the corners of your moods, the soft spots of your speech
At dinner I swallowed my reply and passed the salt instead
You called me easy to be with; I called it getting by

[Pre-Chorus]
I kept a ledger no one saw
Of every yes that cost me more

[Chorus]
I made a home inside your comfort
Left no room to turn around
I was everybody’s answer
Till I couldn’t hear my own sound
What a lovely little blessing
To be needed, praised, and kind
What a terrible price to pay
For leaving myself behind

[Verse 2]
I knew your coffee, knew your sister, knew the date you hate
I took the late train home so you could leave at eight
When you asked if I was happy, I said, “Sure, it’s all okay”
Then stood at my own sink with nothing left to say

[Pre-Chorus]
I kept the peace by losing ground
And wore a smile to hide the count

[Chorus]
I made a home inside your comfort
Left no room to turn around
I was everybody’s answer
Till I couldn’t hear my own sound
What a lovely little blessing
To be needed, praised, and kind
What a terrible price to pay
For leaving myself behind

[Bridge: half-time]
You don’t have to hate me
For me to say no
I can love you honestly
And still decide to go
I can leave the plate unwashed
Let the hard truth sit
You can be disappointed
I can live with it

[Final Chorus]
I won’t build my life from favors
I won’t bargain to belong
I can care without surrender
I can stay and still be strong
What a bittersweet blessing
To notice where I crossed the line
I can give with both hands open
And keep one life that’s mine

[Outro]
The blue shirt hangs there by the doorway
This time, I choose what feels like mine

title: No Crown to Guard
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I practice my entrance in the dark glass
Chin set high, every doubt rehearsed
I say my name like a closing argument
As if the room must make me first

I count the nods, I keep the score
I call it proof, then ask for more
If no one sees the crown I wear
Was it ever really there?

[Pre-Chorus]
One voice says, take the whole room
One says, why must they make room?
One builds a throne from borrowed praise
One asks what stays when it decays

[Chorus]
Is this confidence, or just a taller mask?
Do I know my worth, or need you to ask?
I can stand my ground without standing above
I can want to be seen and still make room for love

[Verse 2]
I turn a simple no into a trial
Dress every bruise in polished wit
I make a joke before you find the tender place
Then wonder why you never sit

But when I finish talking, there you are
Not a mirror, not a judge, not a star
You have your own weather, your own name
Not an audience to feed my flame

[Pre-Chorus]
One voice says, never show the seam
One says, a seam is not a defeat
One needs the last word every time
One lets the quiet answer mine

[Chorus]
Is this confidence, or just a taller mask?
Do I know my worth, or need you to ask?
I can stand my ground without standing above
I can want to be seen and still make room for love

[Bridge]
If I am strong, I can hear you
If I am sure, I can be wrong
I don't need to win the silence
To know where I belong

Let the praise come, let it pass me
Let the hard truth reach my skin
There is courage in the open hand
There is room to let you in

[Final Chorus]
This is confidence; it doesn't need a throne
I can name my gifts and leave your gifts your own
I can take the lead and listen when you speak
I don't have to be the tallest to be strong, or loud to be seen

[Outro]
No crown to guard, no role to play
I know my worth—and yours can stay

title: I Choose You in the Ordinary
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You leave your keys beside the bowl
And tell me how the meeting went
I watch the steam lift from your tea
While evening gathers at the window

You know the names of all my storms
And when to let the silence stay
Then touch my wrist, and ask me plain
If I want company today

[Pre-Chorus]
No grand design, no perfect phrase
Just you remembering how I take my tea

[Chorus]
I choose you in the ordinary
In the dishes, in the drive
In the way you save the last warm slice
And ask if I got home all right
When all the bright occasions pass
And every borrowed ribbon’s gone
I choose you in the ordinary
And I’ll keep choosing as we go

[Verse 2]
Your coat is hanging by the stairs
A little rain still on the sleeve
You tell me what you’re scared to lose
I tell you what I can’t yet name

We don’t make promises of ease
We make a little room to change
A hand held out across the table
A soft place to return again

[Pre-Chorus]
No flawless map, no fixed reply
Just you beside me while we learn the way

[Chorus]
I choose you in the ordinary
In the dishes, in the drive
In the way you save the last warm slice
And ask if I got home all right
When all the bright occasions pass
And every borrowed ribbon’s gone
I choose you in the ordinary
And I’ll keep choosing as we go

[Bridge]
If work runs late, I’ll leave the porch light
If words come wrong, we’ll start anew
I won’t ask you to be unchanging
I want the life that keeps becoming you

[Half-Time Breakdown]
Stay for the morning
Stay for the mess
Stay when we’re certain
Stay when we guess

[Final Chorus]
I choose you in the ordinary
In the hard days and the bright
In the honest little ways we turn
Toward each other every night
When all the years have changed our plans
And time has rearranged the road
I choose you in the ordinary
And I’ll keep choosing as we go

[Outro]
Keys beside the bowl
Your coat beside mine
I choose you here
One day at a time

title: You Deserve a World Called
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You saw the crack beneath the paint
The rules were paper, not restraints
You asked why every road ran straight
Then built a turn they called a mistake

You named the bargains no one named
And showed the cost behind the frame
They called you odd for noticing
You called it what it was: a hinge

[Pre-Chorus]
When you can see the bolts and seams
You learn a wall can come apart
But seeing clearly has a price
It leaves you standing there alone

[Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing through it
You’re the hand that moves the stone
You can change the shape of living
But you can’t always change alone
When the room goes quiet round you
When your truth has made you roam
Keep a place for your own heart
While you make the world a home

[Verse 2]
You pulled the label from the jar
And found the thing was not the name
You let the overlooked speak first
You made a door where none had been

They praised the bridge, then missed the builder
They crossed, then hurried on ahead
You stood beside the new way through
With all the words you left unsaid

[Pre-Chorus]
The view is wider from the edge
The air is thinner there as well
You turn the map for everyone
Then wonder who can read your face

[Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing through it
You’re the hand that moves the stone
You can change the shape of living
But you can’t always change alone
When the room goes quiet round you
When your truth has made you roam
Keep a place for your own heart
While you make the world a home

[Bridge]
Some nights the brave idea is simple:
Let somebody sit beside you
No grand design, no need to fix it
Just say, “I’m tired. Stay a while.”

The world may take the road you opened
And never know who cleared the ground
But you are more than what you altered
You deserve to be found

[Half-Time Breakdown]
I see the seams
I feel the space
I need a hand
I need a face

[Final Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing through it
You’re the hand that moves the stone
You can change the shape of living
You don’t have to do it alone
Let the ones who know your language
Find you where the fields are sown
Keep a place for your own heart
You deserve a world called home

[Outro]
You saw the crack
You made a way
Now let someone
Walk with you today

title: Leave a Chair Beside the
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You saw the seam in the painted sky
The little crack they walked right by
You heard the gears beneath the floor
And couldn’t call the grinding normal anymore
You named the hunger dressed as fate
You watched them bolt the garden gate
They said your eyes were hard to please
You said, “That lock was made by people—give me the keys.”

[Pre-Chorus]
And when you point to what is real
They call the wound a thing you feel
But seeing clearly has a cost
A compass works by knowing when you’re lost

[Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing through it
You’re the hand that can undo it
Every rule was built by someone
Every wall can come apart
But the ones who turn the handle
May be standing there alone
You can change the shape of everything
And still walk home unknown

[Verse 2]
You moved the chairs, you changed the plan
You made a place where more could stand
You said the quiet part out loud
Then watched the room dissolve into a crowd
The phone stayed dark; the kettle clicked
Your victory felt strangely quick
A hundred doors swung open wide
No one beside you when you stepped outside

[Pre-Chorus]
You don’t regret the truth you gave
You only miss the ones you couldn’t save
The view is wide, the table small
A longer reach can mean no hand at all

[Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing through it
You’re the hand that can undo it
Every rule was built by someone
Every wall can come apart
But the ones who turn the handle
May be standing there alone
You can change the shape of everything
And still walk home unknown

[Bridge: half-time breakdown]
If I make a place for you
Will you come in from the cold?
I can move the doorframe
I can leave the porch light on
I can tell you what I saw
I can’t make you see it too
And the hardest part of changing things
Is not knowing who comes through

[Build]
Still, the bolt can turn
Still, the beam can bend
Still, a different kind of seeing
Can make a different end

[Final Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing through it
You’re the hand that can undo it
Every rule was built by someone
Every wall can come apart
Though the ones who turn the handle
May be standing there alone
You can change the shape of everything
And make a wider home

[Outro]
Leave a chair beside the doorway
Leave the kettle warm
If you’re first to see the opening
You don’t have to be the only one

title: Architects of Tomorrow
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You see the gears behind the wall
While others sleep or never call
The cracks in glass, the hollow floor
You walk right past their bolted door
They call it strange to see so clear
To watch the future disappear

[Chorus]
And it gives you the power to shatter the mold
A quiet inventor with nothing to hold
You carry the lever, you carry the stone
To rebuild the city, but walk it alone
Oh, seeing the design is a heavy decree
To build a new world from the top of the tree

[Verse 2]
The blueprints burn inside your head
While normal days go soft and dead
You hold the key, you hold the fire
To lift the world up ever higher
But bridges rust where giants stand
No footprints left upon your sand

[Chorus]
And it gives you the power to shatter the mold
A quiet inventor with nothing to hold
You carry the lever, you carry the stone
To rebuild the city, but walk it alone
Oh, seeing the design is a heavy decree
To build a new world from the top of the tree

[Bridge]
The quiet rooms where no one stays
The empty hours, the silent days
You bought the truth with all your warmth
A solitary eye inside the storm

[Final Chorus]
And it gives you the power to shatter the mold
A quiet inventor with nothing to hold
You carry the lever, you carry the stone
To rebuild the city, but walk it alone
Oh, seeing the design is a heavy decree
To build a new world from the top of the tree

[Outro]
The architects of tomorrow
Always sleep in the cold
[Instrumental fade out]

title: Leave a Chair Beside the Table
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You saw the crack beneath the paint
The rule dressed up as common sense
You asked why every crooked beam
Was called a wall that must not bend
They laughed when you named what they hid
Like naming it made you the flaw
But once you see the hinge and pin
You know the door was never law

[Pre-Chorus]
You held the truth out in your hands
They stepped away, you understand

[Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing clearly
You’re the one who sees the seam
Every world was once somebody’s
Wild and unapproved idea
But the ones who move the mountains
Often sleep beyond the crowd
You can change the shape of everything
And still feel missing from it now

[Verse 2]
You take apart the easy answer
Find the cost they left outside
Put a name beside the number
Give the quiet ones a side
You draw a road through old assumptions
Cut a window through the wall
Then turn to tell the room what changed
And find no one there at all

[Pre-Chorus]
You made a place where none could stand
Now who will reach and take your hand?

[Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing clearly
You’re the one who sees the seam
Every world was once somebody’s
Wild and unapproved idea
But the ones who move the mountains
Often sleep beyond the crowd
You can change the shape of everything
And still feel missing from it now

[Bridge: half-time, intimate]
At dinner, you rehearse the sentence
Then let the potatoes cool
Your sister says, “You think too deeply”
You smile and pass the serving bowl
You wanted more than being right
You wanted someone there beside you
Someone who could face the open door
And not ask you to go hide, too

[Build]
So if your hands are tired from holding
What the room refuses to see
Leave a light on in the window
There are others finding keys

[Final Chorus]
You’re not strange for seeing clearly
You’re a signal through the years
Every world begins with someone
Who can look straight through the fear
And the ones who move the mountains
Need a place to set them down
You can change the shape of everything
You don’t have to change alone now

[Outro]
Leave a chair beside the table
Leave the door unlatched tonight
There are others seeing clearly
There are others looking for the light

title: You Saw the Crack
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You saw the crack beneath the paint
The careful lie they called restraint
You asked why every door was small
And heard the hinges in the wall
They called you difficult to know
You noticed where the seams would go
A crooked thought, a stubborn flame
A better question without a name

[Pre-Chorus]
You weren't made to fit the frame
You saw the frame was built to tame

[Chorus]
Maybe strange is seeing clearly
When the room prefers a blur
You can turn the truth to motion
You can change what others were
But the hands that move the mountain
May come home to empty chairs
Still, the world is less alone now
Because you saw what wasn't there

[Verse 2]
You marked the ramp beside the stairs
Made room for voices no one hears
You moved the table, changed the rule
Made space for someone called a fool
They praised the bridge, forgot the shore
You kept on building something more
Then walked back through your quiet door
With no one there to ask what for

[Pre-Chorus]
The view that lets you see ahead
Can leave you speaking to yourself instead

[Chorus]
Maybe strange is seeing clearly
When the room prefers a blur
You can turn the truth to motion
You can change what others were
But the hands that move the mountain
May come home to empty chairs
Still, the world is less alone now
Because you saw what wasn't there

[Bridge: half-time, intimate]
I know the cost of being first
Of naming what the silence hides
They take the path you cut through stone
Then leave you standing off to the side
If you are tired, let it show
You don't have to lead tonight
The ones who walk the road you opened
Will learn to leave a porch light

[Final Chorus]
Maybe strange is seeing clearly
And refusing to look away
You can turn the truth to motion
You can bend the shape of days
Though the hands that move the mountain
May come home to empty chairs
What you changed will keep on reaching
Past the loneliness you bear

[Outro]
You saw the crack
You made a door
Someone comes through
And asks for more

title: I Need Some Space
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Your message waits beside the sink
My brother calls; I stop to think
The calendar has swallowed days
With names I love in colored rays
I give you all the careful words
Then lose the one I meant to say
My hands keep reaching out for everyone
While mine are slipping away

[Pre-Chorus]
I don't want less of you
I need a little room to breathe

[Chorus]
I can love you and still need space
A quiet hour, an unhurried place
I won't disappear, I won't let go
I need some ground where my own roots grow
The door stays open, the light stays on
I can come back whole when the day's gone
I can love you and still need space
And meet you with my whole heart again

[Verse 2]
Your son has lost his blue raincoat
My friend needs help to move a chair
Dad asks if I can make it Sunday
And I say yes before I'm there
I know the small things make a life
The rides, the meals, the staying late
But care can turn to keeping score
When I don't leave room to hesitate

[Pre-Chorus]
I don't want less of you
I need a little room to breathe

[Chorus]
I can love you and still need space
A quiet hour, an unhurried place
I won't disappear, I won't let go
I need some ground where my own roots grow
The door stays open, the light stays on
I can come back whole when the day's gone
I can love you and still need space
And meet you with my whole heart again

[Bridge]
Tonight I'll leave the dishes there
I'll let the phone ring once or twice
I'll sit beside the kitchen window
And hear the radiator click
No grand goodbye, no locked-out heart
No tally of who's owed what when
Just enough silence to remember
How to offer love again

[Breakdown]
Not a wall
Not a leaving
Just a breath
Just a minute

[Final Chorus]
I can love you and still need space
A quiet hour, an unhurried place
I won't disappear, I won't let go
I need some ground where my own roots grow
The door stays open, the light stays on
I can come back whole when the day's gone
I can love you and still need space
And meet you with my whole heart again

[Outro]
I'll call you when I can be here
Not only present, but truly near

title: Leave Some Space
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Your name lights up while I’m halfway home
Mum needs a ride, and the crew needs a plan
You’ve got a long day you don’t want to face alone
I say, “I’m here,” before I know if I can

I keep every birthday tucked under my tongue
Every small promise folded in my coat
Then I get to my door with the evening undone
And can’t remember the last thing I chose

[Pre-Chorus]
I thought love meant never letting go
Of every hand that reached for mine
But even a heart that answers everyone
Needs a little room to stay alive

[Chorus]
I can love you and leave some space

[Chorus]

One deep breath, one honest no

[Final Chorus: escalating, anthemic]

I can miss you and still take a day
There’s a chair by the window, a book left open

I won’t disappear to prove I care
I’ll come back with more of me to share

I can love you and leave some space

[Outro]
I’ll call you tomorrow

A little room, too

title: Room for Me
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Your sister calls while I’m halfway through a page
Dad needs a ride, your old friend’s having a day
I know the little things you trust me to remember
The name of your dog, the date in late November

You say, “Are you there?” I say, “Of course I am”
Then stare at all the hours I’ve already handed out
I love the people gathered at my door
I just can’t keep arriving with nothing left in store

[Pre-Chorus]
I keep every promise balanced in my hands
Till one more gentle ask becomes too much to stand

[Chorus]
I want to love you and still have room to breathe
To give you something true, not what is left of me
I’m not turning from you, I’m learning where I end
Make a little space, and I can come back again

[Verse 2]
Your birthday card is waiting by the kettle
Three unread messages, a coat against the metal
I miss the easy quiet I could find before
And feel the guilt arrive before I close the door

I’ll call you Sunday; I mean every word
But tonight I need the small, unclaimed part of the world
No grand goodbye, no list of who was wrong

[Pre-Chorus]
I kept saying yes so nobody would hurt

[Chorus]
I want to love you and still have room to breathe
To give you something true, not what is left of me
I’m not turning from you, I’m learning where I end

[Half-Time Breakdown]
Let me be quiet

title: Borrowed Keys
lyrics:
[Intro]
I kept a drawer of borrowed keys
For every door you asked me to keep

[Verse 1]
I learned the shape of everybody’s hurt
The late-night call, the ride home from work
I made a bed where their storms could land
Kept saying yes with an open hand

I knew your coffee, your mother’s name
Which old regret still burned the same
I gave out pieces like spare change
Then wondered why I felt so strange

[Pre-Chorus]
Now the room goes quiet, and I can’t tell
If I’m empty—or just used to giving myself

[Chorus]
I gave my heart away in handfuls
Till I couldn’t feel its weight
Now you reach for me with kindness
And I brace like it’s too late
I have loved so many people
I forgot I could be loved
Tell me, if I’ve spent it all on everyone
Is there any left for us?

[Verse 2]
Your blue mug’s still beside the sink
The one you left the night you couldn’t think
I stayed awake till the birds began
And called it care, because I can

I never asked what I might need

[Pre-Chorus]
You say my name like it can stay

[Chorus]
I gave my heart away in handfuls

And I brace like it’s too late
I have loved so many people
I forgot I could be loved

Is there any left for us?

[Bridge: half-time breakdown]

[Build]
I’m still here
I’m still here

Not a debt you have to clear

[Final Chorus]
I gave my heart away in handfuls

Now your hand rests over mine
And I don’t pull away this time

[Outro]
Stay a little
I’ll try to let you
Stay a little
I’ll try to let you

title: I Can Stay
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I kept a chair pulled out for everyone
Made room before they asked me to
I learned the shape of every aching heart
And wore it like a coat I never knew

I remembered birthdays, borrowed coats
Stayed up till the shaking passed
Now my own hands hover at the door
Like I have to earn a place at last

[Pre-Chorus]
I gave away the softest parts
Till I forgot they had my name

[Chorus]
I loved too many people like a promise
Spent my whole heart trying to make them stay
Now when someone reaches out to hold me
I turn my face and say, “I’m okay”
If I poured myself out till there’s nothing
Does that mean I’m not the kind you choose?
I’m learning love was never meant to leave me
With no love left to give myself to

[Verse 2]
Your message waits; I read it three times
Searching for the catch beneath the care
You say you want to know me as I am
I don’t know what to do with someone there

I know how to listen through the silence
How to tell a joke before they cry
But when you ask me what I’m needing
Every answer folds and hides

[Pre-Chorus]
I made a home in everybody’s storms
Then wondered why my own room felt so bare

[Chorus]
I loved too many people like a promise
Spent my whole heart trying to make them stay
Now when someone reaches out to hold me
I turn my face and say, “I’m okay”
If I poured myself out till there’s nothing
Does that mean I’m not the kind you choose?
I’m learning love was never meant to leave me
With no love left to give myself to

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge]
Maybe I mistook being needed
For being worthy of a place
Maybe I called it kindness
When I disappeared to keep their faith

You don’t have to pay me back
You don’t have to make me whole
Just sit beside me while I practice
Not abandoning my own soul

[Half-Time Breakdown]
I am not the sum of every goodbye
I am not the debt of every hand I held
There is still a room inside me
I can enter for myself

[Final Chorus]
I loved too many people like a promise
Spent my whole heart trying to make them stay
But I can let your kindness reach me
I don’t have to turn it all away
If I poured myself out till there’s nothing
I can start with one small truth:
Love was never meant to leave me
With no love left to give myself to

[Final Refrain]
I can keep a little for the morning
I can let my own name sound like home
You can love me without being owed it
I can stay, and not be alone

[Outro]
I can stay
I can stay

title: I Gave Out The Keys
lyrics:
[Intro]
I kept a spare key under every mat
Learned every birthday, every coat, every cat

[Verse 1]
You called from the airport; I stayed on the line
I missed my own dinner to make sure you were fine
I carried your boxes up three flights of stairs
Then went home too tired to notice who cares

I knew how to listen, how to soften a room
How to say, “Take your time,” while I swallowed my own
I gave out my yes like a glass of cold water

[Pre-Chorus]
I made a home in the hands of the leaving

Now when you reach for me, I flinch at the door
Afraid I’ve got nothing worth asking for

[Chorus]
I gave my heart away by the handful
Till my own hands came up bare
I made myself useful to everyone
Then wondered who would stay there
If love is a room, I gave out the keys

I’m not hard to love—I’ve been pouring so long
I forgot I could keep some at all

[Verse 2]
Your blue mug still sits by the sink at my place
The chipped one you used when you slept here for days
I learned all the names of the storms in your life
But forgot mine was rising the same night

I said, “I’m all right,” with a practiced small smile
While the laundry stayed folded for more than a while
I kept every promise you needed me to
Then heard my own voice asking, “Who’s left for you?”

[Pre-Chorus]
I made a home in the hands of the leaving
Kept every porch light on through the season
Now when you reach for me, I flinch at the door
Afraid I’ve got nothing worth asking for

[Chorus]
I gave my heart away by the handful
Till my own hands came up bare
I made myself useful to everyone
Then wondered who would stay there
If love is a room, I gave out the keys
And slept in the hall by the wall
I’m not hard to love—I’ve been pouring so long
I forgot I could keep some at all

[Bridge: half-time, intimate]
The last train leaves at ten past nine
I let it go so you could make yours on time
Your coat on my shoulders, your name in my phone
I can’t keep calling that proof I’m alone

[Build]
Maybe the cup isn’t empty forever
Maybe a hand can unclench
Maybe the love I kept sending outward
Can find its way home again

[Final Chorus]
I gave my heart away by the handful
But these hands are still mine to spare
I can be tender and still have a doorway
I can let someone meet me there
If love is a room, I can keep one key
And open the door when I’m sure
I’m not hard to love—I was giving it all

[Outro]
The blue mug stays; I don’t have to throw it away

title: The Prison and the Power in
lyrics:
[Intro: sparse, haunting prepared piano ostinato, distant tape hiss]

[Verse 1]
I see the angles where the edges don't meet
I trace the patterns on the crowded street
The world is beautiful, a shifting design
But there's a barrier, a boundary line
They look at me like I am out of frame
A sudden glitch inside their perfect game
It is a heavy cost, this quiet sight
To be the only one who sees the light

[Pre-Chorus: cello distortion swells, tension rising]

[Chorus: explosive riddim bass waves, gated snare, choir pads]

title: Stand Strange

[Intro]
[Prepared piano ostinato, sparse, eerie tape saturation]
[Cello distortion enters slowly]

I hear the frequencies between the spoken words
A different pattern in the movement of the birds
They build their houses with the windows facing in

[Pre-Chorus]
[Glitch chopped percussion building]
[Bittersweet synth pads rising]

title: I See It Sideways
lyrics:
[Intro]
They gave me a window
And called it the world
I leaned to the side
And saw it turn

[Verse 1]
I noticed the bruise beneath the joke
The bent nail holding up the sign
While everyone agreed the room was fine
I heard the small unsaid things
Gather under every table
And carried them home in my coat

They said, “You make it harder”
They said, “Just let it be”
But the cracks were drawing maps
Only I could see

[Pre-Chorus]
It hurts to stand where no one stands
To speak in shapes they cannot name
But every odd angle in my sight
Shows where the walls can change

[Chorus]
I see it sideways
I see what could be
The cost is a distance
That follows me
But strange is a doorway
Cut through the stone
I ache at the edges
Then bring the walls down

[Verse 2]
I felt the cold seat left for me
The careful pause after my words
The way a room can close without a sound
Still I kept the crooked sketch
Of a kinder kind of living
And drew the missing doors around

You called me difficult
I called it noticing
The rules were made by someone
They can be remade by us

[Pre-Chorus]
It hurts to stand where no one stands
To speak in shapes they cannot name
But every odd angle in my sight
Shows where the walls can change

[Chorus]
I see it sideways
I see what could be
The cost is a distance
That follows me
But strange is a doorway
Cut through the stone
I ache at the edges
Then bring the walls down

[Bridge]
Some days I want the easy room
The chair pulled close, the welcome plain
To leave the questions at the door
And not explain my face again

But you were there, with tired eyes
Still holding out your hand
So I will keep the view I have
And help you understand

[Final Chorus]
We see it sideways
We see what could be
The cost is the distance
We carry unseen
But strange is a doorway
Wide enough now
We ache at the edges
And change the way through

[Outro]
I see it sideways
You’re not alone
The world can be wider
Than the rooms we were shown

title: The Painful Gift
lyrics:
[Sparse Intro: eerie prepared piano ostinato, distant distorted cello drones]

[Verse 1]
I see the streetlights bending through a shattered glass
A million colors that the crowd just walks right past
They see a pavement, I see a burning map
I live inside the silence of a thunderclap
The privilege of looking through a different lens
Is knowing how the circle starts and where it ends

[Chorus]
But it's a beautiful curse, a heavy crown to wear
To see the future standing in the freezing air
They call it madness when you refuse to bend
Isolated at the table, talking to the wind
But in the dark, the quiet power starts to grow
The hands that feel the pain are those that change the show

[Verse 2: detuned synth leads, glitch chopped percussion]
My eyes are cameras catching what they try to hide
A quiet war of colors fighting deep inside
The punishment is standing right outside the door
While they are dancing on a safe and level floor
I am the glitch inside their perfect, tidy code

[Chorus]
But it's a beautiful curse, a heavy crown to wear
To see the future standing in the freezing air

Isolated at the table, talking to the wind

The hands that feel the pain are those that change the show

[Outro: plate reverb, fading piano chords]
Seeing it all.
Feeling apart.
The painful gift.
The silent power.
My actual eyes.

title: Find the Frame
lyrics:
[Intro]
At the edge of the classroom map
I saw a country no one had drawn

[Verse 1]
I read the room by its crooked seams
Found little doors in the in-between
While every face wore the proper mask
I kept asking what no one asked

They called my angle a defect
A bent compass, a wrong effect
But from the place they left me standing
I saw the whole design was failing

[Pre-Chorus]
It hurts to watch from the outside in
To know the shape of the walls you’re in
Still, every crack lets daylight through
And I can change what I can see from here

[Chorus]
I’m strange enough to see the hinge
And brave enough to make it turn
I pay for every different view
But there’s a world in what I learn
You shut the door; I find the frame
You call me lost; I name the road
This lonely sight can split the stone
And give the next one room to grow

[Verse 2]
At lunch I learned the language of forks
And how to laugh when the whole room talks
I kept a notebook under my sleeve
Of things the rules forgot to believe

A crooked answer, a tender doubt
A better way to let someone out
The ones who never fit the picture
Can redraw the frame around the picture

[Pre-Chorus]
It hurts to watch from the outside in
To know the shape of the walls you’re in
Still, every crack lets daylight through
And I can change what I can see from here

[Chorus]
I’m strange enough to see the hinge
And brave enough to make it turn
I pay for every different view
But there’s a world in what I learn
You shut the door; I find the frame
You call me lost; I name the road
This lonely sight can split the stone
And give the next one room to grow

[Bridge]
Some nights the difference has teeth
It takes my seat, it steals my sleep
I watch the others cross the room
As if they know what I should do

But you, with your careful, unheard thought
You’re not a mistake that needs to be taught
Take the view that cost you so much
And let it become the hand that lifts us

[Final Chorus]
I’m strange enough to see the hinge
And strong enough to make it turn
I paid for every different view
Now watch the closed walls twist and learn
You shut the door; we change the frame
You call us lost; we name the road
This lonely sight can split the stone
And give the next ones room to grow

[Outro]
The world looked fixed from where they stood
I saw it move—and knew it could

title: Strange Is a Key
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You notice the crack in the painted wall
The tiny wrong note beneath the call
You read a room by the chairs left turned
And feel each rule before it’s learned

They say your questions make things hard
You keep a map made from the discarded parts
A private country behind your eyes
Where every locked door has another side

[Pre-Chorus]
It costs to stand where no one stands
To carry weather in your hands
But what you see that they pass by
Can redraw the borders of the sky

[Chorus]
Strange is a key that cuts both ways
It opens a world, it leaves a bruise
You stand outside their easy circle
With a wider view, with more to lose
And when the frame won’t hold your shape
You learn what frames are made to do
The ache that tells you you don’t belong
Can be the force that changes what belongs to you

[Verse 2]
At lunch, your joke lands a second late
You count the seconds while they change the subject
But on the walk home, the street rearranges
A paper cup becomes a planet turning

You catch the small exclusions in the light
The quiet “not for you,” the softened lie
And though it hurts to name what others miss
You make a place where no one has to shrink

[Pre-Chorus]
It costs to stand where no one stands
To carry weather in your hands
But what you see that they pass by
Can redraw the borders of the sky

[Chorus]
Strange is a key that cuts both ways
It opens a world, it leaves a bruise
You stand outside their easy circle
With a wider view, with more to lose
And when the frame won’t hold your shape
You learn what frames are made to do
The ache that tells you you don’t belong
Can be the force that changes what belongs to you

[Bridge]
Some nights the distance has a name
A chair pulled back, a call unanswered
You wonder if the price is worth the seeing
If being right means being nowhere

Then one small hand reaches for yours
A kid who thought their colors were a flaw
You don’t explain the whole wide world
You make a little room, and leave the door unlatched

[Final Chorus]
Strange is a key that cuts both ways
It opens a world, it leaves a bruise
You stand outside their easy circle
And bring a wider view back through
When the frame won’t hold our shapes
We learn what frames are made to do
The ache that told us we don’t belong
Can be the force that changes what belongs to who

[Outro]
You saw another way
You made another way
And someone walks it now

title: The Shape in Your Heart
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You drew a map on the back of a receipt
A second sunrise where the old roads meet
You said, “There’s room where the wall runs out”
They smiled like they knew what you were talking about

You kept a sketch in your jacket seam
A crooked little blueprint of a bigger dream
They called it strange, said, “That won’t hold”
You kept the page when the room went cold

[Pre-Chorus]
You don’t need their eyes to see it
You don’t need their hands to free it

[Chorus]
Keep seeing what they can’t see yet
Keep making space where there wasn’t any
If they call your bright idea too strange
Let it be strange, let it be ready
You’re not wrong for imagining more
You’re not lost for opening the door
The world you picture can begin
With one small thing you won’t give in

[Verse 2]
You named a garden on a vacant lot
Found a use for every thing they forgot
A table built from a discarded frame
A place for the ones who were told they’re too much to claim

They asked why you’d spend your days this way
You said, “I can see it, so I’ll start today”
A pencil mark, then a borrowed tool
A little less impossible, a little less cruel

[Pre-Chorus]
You don’t need their eyes to see it
You don’t need their hands to free it

[Chorus]
Keep seeing what they can’t see yet
Keep making space where there wasn’t any
If they call your bright idea too strange
Let it be strange, let it be ready
You’re not wrong for imagining more
You’re not lost for opening the door
The world you picture can begin
With one small thing you won’t give in

[Bridge]
Maybe they’ll understand it later
Maybe they never will
You can hold the shape of what could be
And take the first step still
Not every seed looks like a forest
Not every start looks wise
But a future once belonged to someone
Who trusted what they saw inside

[Final Chorus]
Keep seeing what they can’t see yet
Keep making space where there wasn’t any
If they call your bright idea too strange
Let it be strange, let it be ready
You’re not wrong for imagining more
You’re not lost for opening the door
The world you picture can begin
With one small thing you won’t give in

[Outro]
One mark, one hand, one place to start
You’re allowed to trust the shape in your heart

title: Lay the Better Ground
lyrics:
[Intro]
They drew a fence around the field
And called the empty ground complete
But I can see the orchard there
With room enough for every seed

[Verse 1]
You count the bolts, I count the doors
That no one thought to try

lyrics:

Own the mess I made and make a kinder way
I was fine with being almost, fine with getting by

title: Your Open Hands
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You leave your coat across my chair
And ask me how the day went wrong

[Chorus]

title: One Honest Act of Grace
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left your coat beside the stairs

[Pre-Chorus]

[Chorus]

[Verse 2]

[Pre-Chorus]

[Chorus]
Make room at the table

[Final Chorus]

title: The Things I Haven’t Been
lyrics:

[Chorus]

I’m trying to understand you

I can make a little room here

[Verse 2]

[Pre-Chorus]

[Chorus]
I’m trying to understand you

Let the first response sink
I’m trying to understand you

For the things I haven’t been

[Bridge]

[Breakdown]

Stay here

[Final Chorus]
I’m trying to understand you
Before I tell you what I think
Let the silence have a minute
Let the first response sink
I’m trying to understand you

For the things I haven’t been

lyrics:

[Chorus]

I’m trying, trying to understand

[Verse 2]

[Pre-Chorus]
I won't pretend I know your road

[Chorus]
I’m trying to understand

I’m trying to understand
Keep my first reply inside

I’m trying, trying to understand

[Final Chorus]
I’m trying to understand
Not win, not make you see my side
I’m trying to understand
Keep my first reply inside

title: I Can't Read You
lyrics:

title: Be Gentle
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You left your coat beside the chair

title: Leave a Door Unclosed
lyrics:

title: Change The Way We Walk Away
lyrics:
